info.title: Ianua Identity Provider API
info.description:
Ianua is a **multi-tenant identity provider** with an integrated **zero-trust proxy**.
This API covers everything you operate it with: authentication, authorization, OAuth2,
SAML/OIDC federation, organization and tenant management, routing and policy for the
proxy, webhooks, messaging, and real-time event streams.

## Identity planes

Endpoints are scoped to one of three planes, from widest to narrowest:

- **Platform**: operators who run the deployment itself. Manage organizations,
  operators, and impersonation. Paths under `/api/v1/operators` and `/api/v1/organizations`.
- **Organization**: owners and members who administer a customer organization and its
  tenants through the dashboard. Paths under `/api/v1/organizations/{org_slug}/…`.
- **Tenant**: the end users that an organization's tenants serve. Paths under
  `/api/v1/organizations/{org_slug}/tenants/{tenant_slug}/…`.

A request can only reach what its plane allows; anything more returns `403`.

## Authentication

All authenticated requests use a **bearer token**:

```
Authorization: Bearer <session-token>
```

Obtain one by logging in:

- **Organization users** → `POST /api/v1/login` with `{ "email", "password" }`.
- **Tenant users** → `POST /api/v1/organizations/{org_slug}/tenants/{tenant_slug}/login`.

Both return a `refresh_token`: use it as the bearer token above. Some operations require
multi-factor authentication or a stepped-up session and will respond `401` until satisfied.

## Conventions

- **Pagination**: list endpoints page by cursor. Send `limit` (1 to 100, default 20) and,
  for the next page, `after` set to the `next_cursor` of the page before. Each page is
  `{ items, next_cursor, limit }`, and `next_cursor` is `null` on the last page. A cursor
  is opaque and belongs to the `sort` it was made with; sent with another sort, it is
  refused with `422`. SCIM lists keep `startIndex` and `totalResults`, as SCIM requires.
- **Sorting**: `?sort=-created_at,name` (prefix `-` for descending). Allowed fields are
  listed in each `sort` parameter's description.
- **Timestamps**: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 (e.g. `2026-07-01T14:22:09Z`).
- **Errors**: a consistent envelope: `{ "error", "message", "details" }`. Common statuses:
  `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not found, `409` conflict, `422` validation,
  `429` rate limited.

## Real-time

Endpoints under the **Real-time** tag are **WebSocket** upgrades (documented with a `101`
response). Connect with a WebSocket client and the same bearer token to receive live
notification and dashboard streams.

get.description:
The CloudFormation template a customer runs in their AWS account to
make the one role the platform assumes, trusting only the platform's
account and only with the external id they were given. Public on
purpose: it holds no secret, since the account id and external id are
parameters the customer fills in, and someone about to make a role in
their own account may read exactly what it will do first. Served by the
deployment that will assume the role, so a self-hosted install never
points customers at a template made for another platform.

200.description: The CloudFormation template, shown inline as `ianua-connect.yaml` and kept for an hour

get.description:
Returns audit-log entries across the whole platform: platform,
organization and tenant records alike, with the same filters, sorting
and paging as the organization's log; `tenant_id` narrows to one
tenant. Read-only.

Requires an operator's own key.

parameters.name: event_type
parameters.description:
Only events whose type starts with this, such as
`organization.org_user`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
Only events after this RFC 3339 timestamp. Named `since` because
`after` is the page cursor.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only events before this RFC 3339 timestamp.

parameters.name: actor
parameters.description:
Only events this actor performed: `system`, `anonymous`, or
`<kind>:<uuid>` with kind `user`, `org_user`, `operator`, `api_key`,
`oauth_client` or `service`.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description:
Only events in this tenant. A tenant's own log is always its own,
whatever this says.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Only events about the entity with this id.

parameters.name: ip_address
parameters.description: Only events from this client address.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: occurred_at, event_type.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Starts an export of audit-log entries across the whole platform, with
the same filters and formats as the organization's export, written by
the worker in full. Poll `GET /api/v1/audit-log/exports/{id}` for the
file. Records `operator.audit_log_export_requested`.

Requires an operator's own key.

429.description: As many platform exports are waiting as may

get.summary: Get an export of the platform's audit log (operator)
get.description:
Where the export stands, and once ready a signed `download_url` that
works once, for a few minutes. Records
`operator.audit_log_export_downloaded` for each link handed out.

Requires an operator's own key.

200.description: The export, with a download link once written

post.description:
Where the payment provider posts what happened: a payment method added,
a charge failed, or what was owed is paid. Nobody signs in: the
provider's signature over the exact body is what lets a notice in, and
it is checked before anything in it is read. A notice the platform does
not act on is taken and changes nothing. Settling what was owed lifts a
suspension the platform made for not paying, never one an operator
made. Records `organization.payment_method_changed`,
`organization.payment_failed` or `organization.payment_settled`.

requestBody.description: The provider's notice, byte for byte, signed in the `Stripe-Signature` header

403.description: The signature does not verify, or the notice is too old

404.description: The organization it names has no subscription

409.description: A charge failed while a trial runs

422.description: A verified notice could not be read

get.description:
Follows a download link the platform made for an audit log export or a
personal data export, and streams the file as an attachment under a name
the platform chose. A link works for a few minutes and opens its file
once; every reason it opens nothing answers the same `404`. Public: the
link is the whole proof, and it names no person.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The sealed ticket the download link carries

404.description: The link opens nothing: forged, changed, run out, used before, or its file is gone

get.description:
The picture an installed integration carries, drawn on a 24 by 24 grid.
It holds only shapes, checked when the integration was built, and is
served so a browser never runs anything in it. Public: it is the same on
every deployment and names no tenant.

parameters.name: integration
parameters.description: The integration, such as `github`

200.description: The integration's picture, SVG of shapes only

404.description: No integration is installed under this name

get.description:
The logo a tenant uploaded, at the address its branding gave out. The
address changes with every new logo, so the answer is cached for good.
Public: mail clients and sign-in pages fetch it with no credentials.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The tenant the logo address names

200.description: The logo, as a PNG or a JPEG

get.summary: Take a service's answer to a sign-in
get.description:
Where every integration's service sends the browser back after a
person signed in there to connect an account. The `state` finds the
connection, and the service's `code` is swapped for a credential at
once, kept sealed. The browser is sent on to the dashboard's
`/integrations/connected` page with `connection` and a one-time `code`
after the `#`, never the credential; the dashboard finishes the
connection with the person's session. When it cannot be taken the page
is told `error`: `declined` at the service, `unknown` for a `state` no
connection has, `expired` for one that ran out or was answered already,
`unreachable` when the service did not answer, or `refused` when it
refused the code. Public.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The `state` the browser carried to the service.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The service's code.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: The service's error, such as `access_denied`.

302.description: On to the dashboard, with the connection and its one-time code, or why it cannot be finished

post.summary: Receive a service's event for one account
post.description:
Where a service with one address per account sends its events. Nobody
signs in. The delivery is proven once, with what the channel holds,
then read for every workflow waiting on that account, each started as
at a registration's own address. Until the channel is live nothing is
read, apart from the service's own check of the address. Public.

requestBody.description: The service's delivery, byte for byte, signed the way the service signs

200.description: The proof the service asked for, to show the platform holds the address

204.description: Taken, or the service's token kept

401.description: No such channel, it is not live, or the delivery is not proven

502.description: What the delivery announced could not be read from the service, so it should be sent again

post.description:
Where a service sends the events a workflow is registered for, at the
address its registration was given when the workflow was published.
Nobody signs in: the service's signature with the registration's
secret is checked before anything else is read. A delivery that is the
trigger's event, and passes its filters, starts the version in service
for its publisher; a delivery the service sends again starts nothing
twice; anything else is taken and starts nothing. `401` alike for an
unknown registration and a forged or unsigned delivery, and `409` once
the registration is no longer in service, so the service stops. Records
`workflows.execution_started`, or `workflows.start_refused` when the
publisher may not have it start now. Public.

requestBody.description: The service's delivery, byte for byte, signed the way the service signs

200.description: The proof the service asked for, to show the platform holds the address

204.description: Taken, or the service's secret kept

401.description: No such registration, or the signature does not check out

409.description: The registration is no longer in service

head.description:
Answers that the address takes events, as Trello asks with a `HEAD`
request before it takes a webhook, which arrives while the
registration is still being made. It answers the same for every
address, so it says nothing of which registrations exist, and reads
and starts nothing. Public.

post.summary: Receive a service's event for the deployment's app
post.description:
Where a service that sends every event of the deployment's app to one
address sends them, such as Slack's Events API. The signature with the
app's secret is checked first, then the event goes to each registration
for the workspace or site it names, each checked and started as at a
registration's own address. A service's request to prove the platform
holds the address is answered. Public.

requestBody.description: The service's delivery, byte for byte, signed with the deployment's app secret

200.description: The proof the service asked for, to show the platform holds the address

401.description: Not signed with the deployment's app secret, or not an integration

get.description:
Returns every BCP 47 locale tag the platform accepts, such as `en-US`
or `de-DE`: the exact set a user's `locale` preference is checked
against. Useful for a locale picker. Static, public data, needing no
sign-in.

post.summary: Log in as an organization user
post.description:
Public dashboard sign-in by email/password, without organization or tenant path slugs.
Returns `session_id`, bearer `refresh_token`, organization and the requested `tenant_slug`
or first reachable active tenant. With no tenant access, tenant fields are `null`;
`…/switch-tenant` can enter one granted later.
Unknown addresses, wrong passwords and locked/deactivated/invited accounts all give `404`.
Correct passwords can reveal `403 email_not_verified`, or a password/network policy refusal.
`mfa_required` limits the session to completing sign-in: `…/mfa/verify`, enrollment when
`mfa_enrollment_required`, or a mailed link when `email_confirmation_required`.
If the password matches several organizations, no session opens: `status: "choose_organization"`
lists them. Repeat credentials with `organization`. Records `organization.org_login_succeeded`
or, for known-account refusals, `organization.org_login_failed`.
Under sign-in pressure, an unremembered `fingerprint_hash` gets `401 challenge_required`
before password checking. Solve `challenge` (absent if unavailable) and send `challenge_proof`.
Counts are per named organization or shared if unnamed, with identical answers for all addresses; capacity gives `429`/`Retry-After`.

401.description: Sign-in is under pressure and this device must pass a challenge first (`challenge_required`, naming it in `challenge`)

403.description: Forbidden (e.g. organization not active, address not confirmed)

404.description: Invalid credentials (unknown email or wrong password)

429.description: Too many requests, or the server is busy checking passwords (with `Retry-After`)

post.summary: Confirm a sign-in from the mailbox
post.description:
Finishes a member's sign-in that waits for them to confirm it from
their mailbox (`email_confirmation_required` at login). Send the
`token` from the mailed link and the `refresh_token` of the waiting
sign-in, which the browser that began it holds. Neither alone finishes
anything: the link proves the mailbox, the refresh token names the
sign-in it confirms.

When the organization requires a second factor the member has not set
up, `mfa_enrollment_required` is `true` and they set one up next.
Records `organization.org_mfa_verified`. Public.

403.description: The link is unknown, used or another member's

404.description: No live sign-in holds the refresh token

post.description:
Mails a link that signs a member in to the dashboard without a
password. An address may hold an account in several organizations: each
account that may sign in by mail gets its own link, naming its
organization, so following one is the choice. Each link replaces the
ones sent before it and works once, for a few minutes.

Always answers `204`, whether or not the address has an account and
whether or not a link went, no sooner than a fixed floor, so the answer
tells nobody which addresses have accounts. An organization that signs
its members in through single sign-on, or does not allow mailed links,
gets no link. Records `organization.org_magic_link_requested` for each
link sent. Public, limited per address.

204.description: A link went to the address, if a member could use one

post.summary: Sign in with a mailed link
post.description:
Spends the `token` from a link `…/login/magic-link` mailed and opens a
session for its member, as a password sign-in does: in the tenant named
by `tenant_slug`, or the first they reach. Following the link proves the
mailbox; a member with a second factor still owes it (`mfa_required`).
A link refused for the organization's settings stays unspent. Records
`organization.org_login_succeeded`, or `organization.org_login_failed`
for a refused link of a known member. Public.

403.description: The organization does not take a mailed link from here, or signs in through single sign-on

404.description: The link is unknown, used or replaced

post.description:
Begins a member's dashboard sign-in through their organization's
identity provider. Send the `organization` slug, and `tenant_slug` to
land in a tenant other than the first the member reaches. The answer
names the provider's page to send the browser to, and a `binding`
secret: keep it for the length of the sign-in and send it with the
provider's answer to `…/login/sso/callback`. Only the browser holding it
finishes the sign-in.

The provider answers to the dashboard: an OIDC provider redirects to
`/login/sso/oidc`, a SAML provider posts to `/login/sso/saml`. An
unknown organization, one with no provider, a provider switched off and
a protocol the organization does not take from here all answer the same
`403`. Records `organization.org_sso_sign_in_started`. Public.

403.description: Single sign-on is not available for this organization from here

post.description:
The dashboard hands on what the identity provider sent the browser back
with: `{"protocol": "oidc", "state", "code"}` from a redirect, or
`{"protocol": "saml", "relay_state", "saml_response"}` from a posted
form, with the `binding` the start handed this browser. The answer is
checked, the member it proves is found, and their session opens as a
password sign-in's does; the session's token comes back here, never in
an address.

Every step refuses by default with `403`: an answer to no sign-in
started here, one brought back by another browser, one from a provider
switched off or replaced since, a forged or replayed assertion, and an
address that is no member's or that the provider did not prove. Nobody
becomes a member by signing in. Records
`organization.org_login_succeeded`. Public.

403.description: The answer is not one this browser's sign-in awaits, or does not prove a member

get.description:
Returns the calling operator's notifications, the platform inbox.
Sortable (for example by `severity`) and paginated; `unread_only=true`
returns only unread ones. Each entry carries the `event_type` that
produced it, its `category` and `severity`, a `title` with an optional
`body`, an optional `resource_id` naming what it is about, the `read`
flag and `created_at`. Requires an operator's own key.

parameters.name: unread_only
parameters.description: If true, only return unread notifications.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, severity, category.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

get.description:
The calling operator's delivery channel for each category, as
`{ category, channel }` pairs: `InApp`, `InAppAndEmail` or `Disabled`.
A category the operator never set is `InApp`. Requires an operator's
own key.

patch.description:
Sets the calling operator's delivery channel for the categories listed,
as `{ category, channel }` entries; the other categories keep theirs.
Answers the whole set after the change, and records
`notifications.operator_preferences_updated` in the platform's trail.
Requires an operator's own key.

post.description:
Marks every one of the calling operator's notifications read and says
how many changed (`marked`). Records
`notifications.all_notifications_read` in the platform's trail.
Requires an operator's own key.

get.description:
How many of the calling operator's notifications are unread: a cheap
badge poll instead of fetching the list. Requires an operator's own key.

post.description:
Marks one of the calling operator's notifications read. There is no
mark-unread. `404` when the notification is not in their inbox. Records
`notifications.notification_read` in the platform's trail, so the
operator's other devices follow. Requires an operator's own key.

get.description:
Returns every operator account, optionally filtered by `status`
(`Active` / `Disabled`), sortable and paginated. Each entry carries the
`email`, lifecycle `status`, and `created_at`. Read-only. Requires an
operator's own key.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Filter by account status (`Active` or `Disabled`). Omit to return
operators of every status.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, email, status.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Creates a new operator account in `Active` status with the given
`email` and `password` (hashed). Operators are platform-level staff who
administer the deployment itself, not scoped to any organization or
tenant. Returns the new operator's `id`. Returns `409` if the email is
already registered, or `422` for an invalid email. Records
`operator.operator_created`, naming the operator who made it. Requires
an operator's own key.

get.description:
Returns the jobs that used up their tries, across every tenant, newest
first and paginated. Each entry carries the job's `id`, its
`job_type`, the `tenant_id` it worked for (`null` for the platform's
own work), how many `attempts` it made, the `reason` its last run
failed, `created_at` and `last_attempted_at`. A job's payload is never
shown: only its handler reads it, and it may name what only its tenant
should see. Read-only. Requires an operator's own key.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Gives a job that used up its tries one more attempt, due at once, once
whatever made it fail is put right. It keeps the attempts it made and
why the last one failed; should the new attempt fail too, it is dead
again. Returns `404` for a job the queue does not hold, and `409` for a
job that is not dead (waiting, running, done, or retried by someone
else meanwhile) or whose same work, queued again under its key, waits
or runs already. Of two operators retrying one job at once, one puts it
back. Records `operator.dead_job_retried`, naming the operator, the
job, its kind, its tenant and how often it ran, never its payload.
Requires an operator's own key.

409.description: Not dead, retried meanwhile, or the same work waits

delete.description:
Ends one of the calling operator's own grants early by its `id`, so they
can no longer act as that user. Returns `404` if the grant doesn't exist,
`403` if it is another operator's (disabling its holder ends every grant
they hold), and `422` if it is already revoked. Records
`operator.impersonation_revoked`. Requires an operator's own key.

post.description:
Exchanges an operator's address and password for a short-lived operator
key, the way onto the operator plane; every later call carries the key.
The **raw key is returned once**. The key ends after the deployment's
operator key lifetime. Every refusal answers `404` alike: an address no
operator holds, a wrong password, a disabled account, or a network
locked out of the address after three wrong passwords in five minutes,
for an hour. Records `operator.operator_api_key_created`, or
`operator.operator_sign_in_failed` with why. Limited per client
address; a `429` with `Retry-After` means slow down.

201.description: Signed in; the key is shown once

get.description:
Returns a single operator by `id`: `email`, `status`, and `created_at`.
Returns `404` if the operator doesn't exist. Read-only. Requires an
operator's own key.

post.description:
Disables an `Active` operator, so they can no longer sign in, and
**revokes all their outstanding impersonation grants**. Their keys stop
working at once. Nobody disables themselves, so the platform always
keeps someone who can run it.

**State.** `Active → Disabled`. Returns `404` if the operator doesn't
exist, `403` for the caller naming themselves, or `422` if they're
already `Disabled`. Records `operator.operator_disabled`. Requires an
operator's own key.

Asks to move the operator `id` to `new_email`. A link to confirm goes to
the new address, and the address the account has now is warned with a
link that stops the change; the account keeps its old address until the
link is followed. Operators sign in with keys, so another operator asks
on their behalf: naming yourself is `403`. Returns `404` for an unknown
operator, `409` when another operator has the address, and `422` when
it is the one they have. Records
`identity.management_email_change_requested`. Requires an operator's
own key.

Re-enables a `Disabled` operator so they can sign in and act again.

**State.** `Disabled → Active`. Returns `404` if the operator doesn't
exist, `403` for the caller naming themselves, or `422` if they're
already `Active`. Records `operator.operator_enabled`. Requires an
operator's own key.

Lets the calling operator (`id` being their own) act as a specific
tenant user (`tenant_id` + `user_id`) until `expires_at`, recording the
mandatory `reason`. Used for support and break-glass access. Returns
`404` if the tenant or the user in it doesn't exist or `id` is another
operator, `403` if the tenant forbids impersonation, `409` while the
operator already holds an active grant for that user, and `422` if
`expires_at` isn't in the future or is more than 24 hours ahead. Answers
the grant's id: a request to the user's tenant carrying the operator's
own key and the id in the `ianua-operator-impersonation` header acts as
the user, checked again on every request. Records
`operator.impersonation_granted`. Requires the operator's own key.

Mints a new API key for the calling operator, `id` being their own. The
**raw key is returned once** (only its hash is stored) alongside the
`key_prefix` used to identify the key later. Send `expires_at` for a key
that ends; one acting through a key that ends sooner is `403`, and an
instant already passed is `422`. Another operator's `id` is `404`.
Records `operator.operator_api_key_created`. Requires the operator's own
key.

requestBody.description: When the key ends; send none for a key that never ends

post.description:
Revokes every key the calling operator holds at once, the one this
request came with included, and returns how many (`revoked`) went.
Another operator's `id` is `404`. Records one
`operator.operator_api_key_revoked` when any key went. Requires the
operator's own key.

Revokes one of the calling operator's keys by its `key_prefix`; it stops
working at once. Returns `404` if no key has that prefix or `id` is
another operator, `403` if the key is another operator's, and `422` if
it is already revoked. Records `operator.operator_api_key_revoked`.
Requires the operator's own key.

get.description:
Every organization on the platform, optionally filtered by `status`
(`Active` / `Suspended` / `Closed`), sortable and paginated. Each entry
carries the slug, display name, plan, and lifecycle status. Read-only.
Requires an operator's own key.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Only organizations of this status (`Active`, `Suspended`, `Closed`).
Omit for every status.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, updated_at, name, slug, status.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
A signed-in member founds another organization and first tenant, becoming owner under the same
address, already verified. The new account has its own `password`: an
address holds one account per organization. Their current account and
organization stay as they are; sign in to the new one with the new
password. The organization starts on the plan a sign-up gets.

Returns the new `org_slug`, `tenant_slug`, `admin_user_id` and
`status: "provisioning"`, as a sign-up does. Requires the member's own
session. Records `organization.created`, `tenant.provisioned`,
`organization.tenant_created`, `organization.subscription_started`,
`organization.org_user_created` and
`organization.org_user_email_verified`.

401.description: Unauthenticated, or a key rather than a session

403.description: This installation takes no new organizations, or the caller's address was never verified

get.description:
The caller's own organization (named by `{org_slug}`) with its slug,
display name, contact email, plan, and lifecycle `status`. Read-only.
Requires a member's own session or organization API key.

patch.description:
Partial update: send `name`, `contact_email`, and/or `display_name` to
change just those; omit any to leave it. A field sent with its current
value records nothing and notifies nobody. This edits profile fields
only: the status has its suspend, reactivate and close endpoints, and
the plan its own. Returns `422` for an invalid value. The app decides
whether the caller may update the organization.

get.description:
Counts audit events of the organization and the tenants the caller
reaches by UTC day: every tenant for an owner or admin, the tenants
granted to a member, none for a viewer.
Inclusive `from` and `to` dates use `YYYY-MM-DD`; defaults span the year
ending today. Reversed or oversized windows return `422`.
Returns `total`, `max_count`, occurring `categories` and oldest-first
`days`, including quiet days, with `count`, `level` (0 to 4) and `by_category`.
Categories group authentication, access, administration, identity,
provisioning and other events. Requires organization audit-read rights;
this read changes nothing. Use the tenant calendar for one tenant.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day of the window (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC, inclusive). Defaults to one year before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day of the window (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC, inclusive). Defaults to today.

get.description:
The organization's API keys, sortable and paginated. Each entry carries
the display `name` and a `key_prefix` for identification; the raw key is
never included. Read-only. The key inventory is credential material, so
the app lets only those who may view keys read it.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, name, last_used_at, expires_at.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Mints a new organization API key under a display `name`, carrying the
`scopes` it may act with and an optional `expires_at`. The **raw key is
returned once**: only its hash is stored, alongside the `key_prefix`
used to identify it later. A key reaches only what its scopes name and
never more than the member minting it holds. Returns `422` for an
invalid name or scope, or an expiry in the past.

Permanently revokes an org API key by its `key_id`, so it stops
authenticating at once. A member of the organization or the platform
may revoke one. Returns `404` if the key does not exist. Records
`organization.org_api_key_revoked`.

get.description:
Returns this organization's audit-log entries, filtered by `event_type`
(a prefix), a time window (`since` / `before`, RFC 3339), the `actor`,
a `tenant_id`, the `target` entity and the client's `ip_address`,
sortable and paged by cursor (`after` / `limit`, 20 by default, at most 100). Each entry
records the event type, actor, tenant, target, address, details and
time. The log holds the organization's own records and those of the
tenants the caller reaches: every tenant for an owner or admin, the
tenants granted to a member, none for a viewer. A `tenant_id` they do
not reach reads as a tenant with no records. Read-only.

Requires a member who may read the organization's audit log.

parameters.name: event_type
parameters.description:
Only events whose type starts with this, such as
`organization.org_user`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
Only events after this RFC 3339 timestamp. Named `since` because
`after` is the page cursor.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only events before this RFC 3339 timestamp.

parameters.name: actor
parameters.description:
Only events this actor performed: `system`, `anonymous`, or
`<kind>:<uuid>` with kind `user`, `org_user`, `operator`, `api_key`,
`oauth_client` or `service`.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description:
Only events in this tenant. A tenant's own log is always its own,
whatever this says.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Only events about the entity with this id.

parameters.name: ip_address
parameters.description: Only events from this client address.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: occurred_at, event_type.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Starts an export of the organization's audit-log entries, with the same
filters as the list, as `csv` (the default, columns
`id,event_type,actor,tenant,target_id,ip_address,occurred_at,acted_through,through_id`) or
`json`. The worker writes every matching entry, newest first, as the log
stood when the export was asked for; nothing is cut off. Poll
`GET .../audit-log/exports/{id}` for the file. Only a few exports may
wait at once. The file holds what the caller reaches when they ask, as
the list does. Records `organization.audit_log_export_requested`.

Requires a member who may export the organization's audit log
(`org:audit_log:export`); viewing it is not enough.

429.description: As many exports are waiting as the organization may have

get.description:
Where the export stands: `pending`, `ready`, `failed` or `expired`. Once
ready it says how many entries the file holds and until when it may be
downloaded, with a signed `download_url` that works once, for a few
minutes. Each answer while it is ready hands out a fresh link and
records `organization.audit_log_export_downloaded`. An export holding
records of a tenant the caller does not reach now answers `404`.

Requires a member who may export the organization's audit log
(`org:audit_log:export`); viewing it is not enough.

200.description: The export, with a download link once written

get.description:
Everything about how this organization's administrators reach the
management plane: the methods allowed, the password rules, the MFA
policy, session and idle lifetimes, the lockout threshold and duration,
the IP allowlist, and the step-up policy.

Distinct from a tenant's `auth-config`, which governs that tenant's own
users. An organization that never changed it gets the defaults. Read
from the organization record, so whoever may view the organization may
read it.

put.description:
Full replace, not a partial update: send every field, plus `proof`, the
caller's password typed again (with a code from their second factor
when they have one), so a stolen session alone never weakens how the
organization is protected. A rejected config changes nothing.

**These settings govern the accounts with the most reach in the
system.** `ip_allowlist` refuses every address outside it, including
your own; removing `Password` from `enabled_methods` stops password
sign-in for every administrator; `max_login_attempts` applies from the
next failure. Turning on `require_mfa_new_device` is what gives "trust
this device" its meaning.

Returns `422` when the config contradicts itself: no method enabled, a
method org sign-in does not implement, a password floor below 8, an
idle timeout outlasting its session, a lockout threshold under 2, or a
sensitive assurance level below the ordinary one. Records
`organization.auth_config_updated`.

403.description: Forbidden, or the proof is wrong

get.description:
The logo, color and mail sender name of the organization's own
dashboard and mail. A part never set is `null`, and the platform's
applies. Read-only.

delete.description:
Returns every part to the platform's look at once. Records
`organization.branding_reset`.

patch.description:
Changes only the parts the body names: absent leaves a part as it is,
`null` returns it to the platform's, a value replaces it. A change of
nothing records nothing. Records `organization.branding_updated` for
each part changed. The app decides whether the caller may change it.

post.description:
Permanently closes the organization: its sessions end and the
organization and its data are scheduled for deletion. This is the
terminal state and cannot be undone.

**State.** `Active | Suspended -> Closed` (terminal). Returns `404` if
the organization does not exist, or `422` if it is already `Closed`.
Records `organization.status_changed`.

get.description:
Every cloud this organization has begun connecting, whether or not the
connection is finished. Never returns a credential. Seeing that a
connection exists is a read of the organization.

200.description: Every cloud this organization has connected

post.description:
Returns the steps to follow, and for AWS the external id to place in the
role's trust policy. Safe to call again: the same external id comes
back, because replacing it would break a trust policy already built.
Connecting a cloud is a change to the organization.

200.description: What to do next, and the external id where that cloud uses one

422.description: This deployment cannot drive that cloud

delete.description:
Forgets the credential. Refused while any tenant still has a database in
that account: dropping the grant would leave infrastructure we can no
longer reach, running and billing. Records
`organization.cloud_account_disconnected`.

409.description: Tenants still run in this account

put.summary: Submit and verify a cloud credential
put.description:
Stores the grant, then uses it once against a harmless endpoint and
records what happened.

A credential the cloud **rejects** is not an error: it comes back as a
connection in the `failed` state with a reason, because that is the
answer to "does this work". Only being unable to ask (our own outage) is
a `500`, and that leaves the connection retryable.

Submitting again is how rotation works, and returns the connection to
unverified until the new secret has proved itself.

200.description: The connection, with the result of proving it

422.description: The credential is malformed, for another cloud, or names a cluster nobody can reach

get.summary: List networks in a connected cloud account
get.description:
What the customer already has in that region, named the way they named
it, so a tenant is placed against something they recognise. An empty
list is a real answer: the account has nothing suitable there, which is
exactly when building a network is offered instead.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Region to list networks in, e.g. eu-central-1

200.description: Networks a database could be placed in

403.description: Forbidden, or the connection is not verified

422.description: Unknown region, or one this cloud cannot serve

post.description:
Uses the stored credential again. Worth calling before relying on a
connection made weeks ago: a role can be deleted and an Azure client
secret expires.

200.description: The connection, with the result of proving it

409.description: No credential has been submitted yet

422.description: The credential needs correcting, such as a cluster address nobody can reach

get.description:
Returns the signed-in org user's own devices, in the order they were
trusted. Revoked ones are kept for history and still listed: read
`status` to tell them apart, since only a `trusted` device skips MFA.
Requires the member's own session.

post.description:
Remembers the device the caller is signing in from, so later sign-ins
from it can skip MFA step-up. Only a sign-in that proved a second factor
may remember a device. Send the secret the browser made for itself
(`fingerprint_hash`, 64 hex digits); only its digest is kept.

The IP and User-Agent recorded come from this request, not from the
body: the list is a security surface, and a client that could name its
own IP could make a strange device look familiar.

**State.** Registers the device as `Trusted`. Returns `409` once the
caller holds the maximum number of trusted devices: revoke one to free a
slot. Records `organization.org_device_trusted`.

403.description: The sign-in proved no second factor

post.description:
Drops the MFA skip for one of the caller's own devices. Use it the
moment a laptop is lost, sold, or looks unfamiliar in the list.

**State.** Moves the device `Trusted → Revoked`, which is terminal: it
must be trusted again from scratch. Returns `404` for a device belonging
to anyone else, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe for device ids,
and `409` for one already revoked. Records
`organization.org_device_revoked`.

post.summary: Stop a pending email change (organization member)
post.description:
Follows the cancel link mailed to the address the account has now: the
change is dropped and its confirmation link stops working. Records
`identity.management_email_change_cancelled`. Public: the token is what
proves the request came from the current mailbox.

404.description: Unknown token, or a change no longer waiting

post.summary: Replace a dead email change link (organization member)
post.description:
Submit the same `token` and another confirmation goes to the address the
change waits on, never to one supplied here. A change already confirmed
answers `404`, and so does the old token once this succeeds.
`retry_after_seconds` is how long to hold the button down. Records
`identity.management_email_change_link_resent`. Public, matching the
confirm endpoint.

404.description: Unknown token, or no such organization

post.summary: Check an email change link without confirming it (organization member)
post.description:
Submit the `token` and get back `Valid`, `Expired`, `AlreadyUsed` or
`Invalid`. A link for a change whose account is gone reads `Invalid`.
Public, matching the confirm endpoint.

Follows the `token` mailed to the new address and moves the account its
change was asked for onto it, marked verified; the old address is told
where it went. The token alone authorizes it, so it applies to the
account the change names, never to whoever happens to be signed in.
Records `identity.management_email_change_confirmed`. Public.

409.description: The new address was taken meanwhile

post.description:
Starts moving the calling member's own account to `new_email`. The
member proves who they are again with their `password` and, when they
have a second factor, a `code` from it. A link to confirm goes to the new
address, the current one is warned with a link that stops the change,
and nothing moves until the confirmation is followed at
`.../email/confirm-change`. Records
`identity.management_email_change_requested`. Requires a member's own
session.

401.description: Unauthenticated, or acting through a key

403.description: What was typed again does not prove who you are, or a code is owed

409.description: Another organization account has the address

422.description: Validation error, or the address you already have

delete.description:
A member who may update members takes the account in `tenant_id` out of
the group of linked accounts the `email` names. A group left with no
account goes. Returns `404` if no such link exists, or `422` for an
invalid email. Records `organization.identity_unlinked`.

get.description:
The organization's own identity provider: its name, protocol, whether it
is switched on, and how far its word is taken. Its configuration and
secrets are never shown. Read-only. The app decides whether the caller
may read the organization's sign-in settings.

post.description:
Adds the provider the organization's members sign in to the dashboard
through, over SAML or OIDC, configured as a tenant's connection is. An
organization has one. It starts switched off and untrusted: switch it on
with `PUT …/identity-provider/status` once it is tested. An OIDC client
secret is kept sealed and never shown or recorded. Records
`organization.org_identity_provider_added`. The app decides whether the
caller may change the organization's sign-in settings.

409.description: The organization has a provider already

422.description: Validation error, an OIDC issuer with no usable configuration, or SAML settings asking for signed requests

delete.description:
Deletes the organization's provider. A sign-in already sent to it is
refused when it comes back. Records
`organization.org_identity_provider_removed`.

patch.description:
Changes the provider's `name`, its `config`, whether its addresses are
taken as proven (`email_trust`) and whether its report of factors is
believed (`assurance_trust`), all together; a field left out keeps its
value. The provider decides who reaches the dashboard, so the caller
sends `proof`, their password typed again with a code from their second
factor (`403 step_up_required` without it). Records one
`organization.org_identity_provider_changed`; a change of nothing
records nothing.

403.description: Forbidden, or the proof is wrong

put.summary: Switch the identity provider on or off
put.description:
Sets the provider's `status` to `Active` or `Disabled`. Members sign in
through it only while it is `Active`. Send `proof`, the caller's
password typed again with a code from their second factor. Records
`organization.org_identity_provider_changed`.

403.description: Forbidden, or the proof is wrong

post.description:
Revokes one of the caller's own org sessions by its `session_id`,
invalidating its refresh token immediately. Send the session id you want
to end (typically the current one). Returns `404` for a session that is
not the caller's and `422` for a malformed session id. Ending another
member's session is `…/sessions/{session_id}/revoke`. Records
`organization.org_session_revoked`. Requires the member's own session.

404.description: Not one of the caller's sessions

get.description:
The calling member's own account (`id`, `email`, `display_name`,
`status`, `role` and preferences) and `access`: the tenants they reach
and their permissions in each. Every member reads their own account,
whatever their role. Read-only.

patch.description:
Self-service update of the calling member's own `display_name`,
`locale` and `timezone` (email and password have their own endpoints).
Each field is applied when present and left unchanged when omitted or
`null`. `locale` and `timezone` override the organization defaults.
Returns `422` for an invalid display name, locale or timezone. Records
`organization.org_user_display_name_changed` and
`organization.org_user_preferences_updated` for what changed.

get.description:
The calling member's own role, reachable tenants, and permissions per
tenant. This is what a dashboard is built from: call it after a grant
change to refresh without signing in again. Every member may read it,
whatever their role, a `Billing` contact or a `Viewer` too.

Aggregate figures for this organization over an adjustable window
(`since` / `until`, RFC 3339, at most 90 days): sign-in timing and
success, users, tenants, active sessions and proxied API usage, each
trended against the window before. Read-only. The app decides whether
the caller may view metrics.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Window start (RFC 3339). Defaults to 30 days before `until`.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Window end (RFC 3339). Defaults to now.

delete.description:
Un-enrolls TOTP MFA for the calling org user: they'll no longer be
prompted for a code at login. Send a current `code` from the
authenticator, so a stolen session is not enough to strip it. Returns
`403` when the code is wrong or the organization requires a second
factor, and `404` if MFA isn't currently enrolled. Records
`organization.org_mfa_unenrolled`. Requires the member's own session.

post.description:
Drops the calling member's authenticator setup that was begun and never
confirmed, so they can start again with a new secret. Giving up is the
first step of starting again, so it asks for the same proof as begin:
`proof` from a member signed in, nothing from a sign-in waiting for its
factor. Otherwise whoever held a stolen session could give up each setup
the member starts. Nothing is recorded: the setup never protected
anything.

requestBody.description: Optional: the member's password typed again when signed in; nothing from a sign-in waiting for its factor

204.description: The pending setup was given up

post.description:
Starts TOTP enrollment for the calling org user and returns the
`otpauth_uri` to render as a QR code in an authenticator app. MFA isn't
active until the user confirms a code from the app.

Setting up a factor changes how the member signs in, so a member signed
in proves who they are again first: send `proof` with their password,
and a code from any factor they already hold (`403 step_up_required`
without it). A sign-in that must set up a factor before it is let in
(`mfa_enrollment_required`) sends no body: the sign-in itself is its
leave, for a few minutes after it began. Records
`organization.org_mfa_enrollment_started`.

requestBody.description: Optional: the member's password typed again when signed in; nothing from a sign-in waiting for its factor

post.description:
Completes enrollment: the user enters a `code` from their authenticator
app; if it verifies, MFA is enabled and a set of single-use
`recovery_codes` is returned (shown once: store them). Records
`organization.org_mfa_enrolled`.

A sign-in that had to set up its first factor passes its `session_id`,
with that sign-in's refresh token as the bearer (`403` when the two are
different sessions): the code proves the new factor, so that session is
complete and can be used straight away.

post.summary: Answer a sign-in with a recovery code
post.description:
For a member who lost their authenticator: the caller, authenticated by
the refresh token of the sign-in that owes a second factor, sends one of
their unused recovery `code`s in its place. The code is spent; of two
sign-ins offering it at once, only one gets through. It shares the
factor's lock, so switching between the two buys no extra guesses.

When the organization asks for more than a password,
`mfa_enrollment_required` is `true`: the member sets up a new factor
(`…/mfa/begin`, `…/mfa/confirm`) before the session is let in. Records
`organization.org_mfa_verified`.

403.description: The code is wrong, used, or the sign-in does not take it

404.description: Unknown sign-in, or no second factor or codes

409.description: The sign-in already proved a factor

post.description:
Makes a new set of recovery codes for the caller, after using most of
them or fearing they were seen. A recovery code lets its holder past the
second factor, so the caller proves who they are again first: send
`proof` with their password and a code from their factor (`403
step_up_required` without it). The new codes come back once; every
earlier code stops working. Records
`organization.org_recovery_codes_generated`. Requires the member's own
session.

403.description: Forbidden, or the proof is wrong

404.description: No second factor or recovery codes

get.description:
Returns whether the calling org user has MFA enrolled (`enabled`) and
the `method` (e.g. `Totp`) if so. Read-only. Requires the member's own
session or key.

post.description:
Second step of an MFA-gated login: the caller, authenticated by the
refresh token of the sign-in that owes the factor, submits a TOTP `code`
from their authenticator. On success the sign-in records the factor and
can proceed. Returns `403` if the code is wrong or already used, and
`422` if it is empty. Records `organization.org_mfa_verified`.

409.description: The sign-in already proved a factor

get.description:
Returns the calling member's notifications in their organization's
inbox. Sortable and paginated; `unread_only=true` returns only unread
ones. Same entry shape as the other inboxes. Requires a member's own
session or organization API key.

parameters.name: unread_only
parameters.description: If true, only return unread notifications.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, severity, category.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

get.description:
Every place outside the app this organization's notifications are
posted to: its name, `kind` (`slack`, `teams` or `webhook`), the
categories and least severity it receives, and whether it is `active`
or `paused`. Addresses and signing secrets are never shown. Read-only.

Requires a member who may view the organization's notifications.

post.description:
Posts this organization's notifications of the listed `categories`, at
`minimum_severity` or above, to a Slack channel or a Teams channel
(through its webhook address on their own hosts) or to a public HTTPS
endpoint of the organization's own, active at once. The address is
sealed at once and never shown again. A webhook's posts are signed: its
`signing_secret` is in this answer and never again. No category, a
category twice, or a Slack or Teams address on another host is `422`;
the plan's destination limit is `403`. Records
`notifications.destination_added`, naming the kind only.

Requires a member who may manage the organization's notifications.

put.description:
Replaces the destination's name, address and filter whole, with the
address typed again. A webhook gets a new signing secret, in this
answer and never again. Records `notifications.destination_changed`.

Requires a member who may manage the organization's notifications.

delete.description:
Stops posting to the destination for good and forgets its address and
secret. Records `notifications.destination_removed`.

Requires a member who may manage the organization's notifications.

post.description:
Stops posting to the destination until it is resumed; one already
paused is `422`. Records `notifications.destination_paused`.

Requires a member who may manage the organization's notifications.

Starts posting to a paused destination again; one not paused is
`422`. Records `notifications.destination_resumed`.

Requires a member who may manage the organization's notifications.

get.description:
The calling member's delivery channel for each category, as
`{ category, channel }` pairs: `InApp`, `InAppAndEmail` or `Disabled`.
A category the member never set is `InApp`. Requires a member's own
session or organization API key.

patch.description:
Sets the calling member's delivery channel for the categories listed,
as `{ category, channel }` entries; the other categories keep theirs.
Answers the whole set after the change, and records
`notifications.member_preferences_updated` in the organization's trail.
Requires a member's own session or organization API key.

post.description:
Marks every one of the calling member's notifications read and says how
many changed (`marked`). Records `notifications.all_notifications_read`
in the organization's trail. Requires a member's own session or
organization API key.

get.description:
How many of the calling member's notifications are unread. Requires a
member's own session or organization API key.

post.description:
Marks one of the calling member's notifications read. `404` when the
notification is not in their inbox. Records
`notifications.notification_read` in the organization's trail. Requires
a member's own session or organization API key.

get.description:
Returns the signed-in org user's registered passkeys: name,
authenticator type, when each was enrolled and last used. Only the
caller's own keys are visible; key material is never returned.

post.description:
Begins registering a WebAuthn passkey for the org user. Returns a
one-time challenge for `navigator.credentials.create()`; hand the
attestation to the register-confirm endpoint to finish. The name the
authenticator shows comes from the member's record, never from the
request.

A member signed in sends no body. A sign-in that waits for the second
factor the organization requires sends `{"from": "WaitingSignIn"}`,
with that sign-in's refresh token as the bearer: the passkey then
finishes it. Records `organization.org_passkey_registration_started`.

requestBody.description: Optional: which sign-in the passkey is added from

post.description:
Finishes enrolling a passkey for the org user. From here on they can
sign in at the flat login page with the passkey: no password, and no
MFA step, since the authenticator itself proves a second factor.

A passkey signs in on its own, so adding one takes proof: a member
signed in sends `proof` with their password typed again (and a code
from any factor they hold); a sign-in waiting for its second factor
sends none, and the new passkey finishes it. A duplicate credential or
the per-member cap returns `409`. Records
`organization.org_passkey_registered`.

delete.description:
Deletes one of the caller's passkeys. The device can no longer be used
to sign in; password login is unaffected. Removing it changes how the
member signs in, so devices and sessions from before stop counting,
except the session it was removed from. A passkey belonging to another
user is `404`, indistinguishable from one that doesn't exist. Records
`organization.org_passkey_removed`.

patch.description:
Changes the display name of one of the caller's passkeys. A passkey
belonging to another user is `404`, indistinguishable from one that
doesn't exist. Records `organization.org_passkey_renamed`.

post.description:
Self-service password change for the calling member: proves them with
the `old_password` and sets `new_password`, checked against the
organization's rules. Every session the member has ends, the one they
asked from included, so whoever else held one is out. Returns `422` if
the new password is too weak. Records
`organization.org_user_password_changed`.

get.description:
The fixed catalog of permissions the org plane recognizes, grouped by
domain: the set an org API key's `scopes` may name. Send an entry's
`label` verbatim as a scope. A static enumeration with no stored data,
readable by any member of the organization.

post.description:
Moves the organization to the `plan` sales agreed (`Free`, `Starter`,
`Business` or `Custom`), billed `monthly` (the default) or `annual`. A
Custom plan may carry `limits` negotiated for it, every field of a
plan's limits, none below the free plan's; without them it works under
the Business limits. An arranged plan is invoiced by hand, so no payment
method or trial is asked for, but what the organization uses must fit
(`409`). Requires an operator's own key: members choose a sold plan with
`PUT …/subscription`. Arranging what the organization already has
changes nothing. Records `organization.subscription_changed` and
`organization.plan_changed`.

409.description: The organization uses more than the arranged limits allow

post.description:
Lifts a suspension: a `Suspended` organization returns to `Active` and
its tenants can serve traffic again. Only the platform lifts a
suspension the platform made.

**State.** `Suspended -> Active`. Returns `404` if the organization does
not exist, or `422` if it is not `Suspended`. Records
`organization.status_changed`.

get.description:
Returns the organization's currently live sessions (across all org
users), sortable and paginated, each with geo coordinates and client
info for the "where am I logged in" security view. Read-only. Requires
a member who may view the organization's sessions.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, last_active_at, expires_at.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Signs another member out of one session, invalidating its refresh token
immediately: for a lost laptop or a session that looks unfamiliar in
the active-session list. A platform action: taken by a member who may
update members, or by an operator for the platform. Records
`organization.org_session_revoked`.

404.description: No such session in this organization

get.description:
The organization's plan and billing cycle, where it stands (`trialing`
until `trial_ends_at`, `active`, or `past_due` since `past_due_since`),
whether a payment method is on file and whether its one trial was used.
Read-only. The app decides whether the caller may read the bill.

put.description:
Moves the organization to `Free`, `Starter` or `Business`, billed
`monthly` or `annual`. What it uses must fit the plan (`409` otherwise).
A paid plan needs a payment method on file (`…/subscription/checkout`),
or starts the organization's one trial: the answer is then `trialing`
with `trial_ends_at`. Custom is arranged with sales, never chosen here.
Choosing the plan and cycle it is already on changes nothing. Records
`organization.subscription_changed` and, when the plan changed,
`organization.plan_changed`. The app decides whether the caller may
change what the organization pays.

403.description: Forbidden, or a plan that is not sold here

409.description: The organization uses more than the plan allows, has no payment method and no trial left, or owes a payment

post.description:
Opens a page at the payment provider where the member adds the card or
mandate the organization is charged through, with receipts going to
the member's address. Send the member to `checkout_url`. Nothing
changes here: the method is recorded when the provider reports it.
Records `organization.checkout_started`. The app decides whether the
caller may change what the organization pays.

409.description: The deployment has no payment provider

500.description: The payment provider did not answer

post.description:
Freezes an `Active` organization: its sessions all end at once and its
tenants stop accepting traffic (deny-by-default) until it is
reactivated. An owner may pause their own organization; an operator may
suspend any, for billing or policy issues.

**State.** `Active -> Suspended`. Returns `404` if the organization does
not exist, or `422` if it is not `Active`. Records
`organization.status_changed`.

Swaps the caller's organization session for a new one working in
`tenant_id`, without signing in again. An organization session works in
one tenant, or on the organization alone; moving is checked against the
member's grants as signing in is: an owner reaches every tenant of the
organization, a plain member only those they were let into. A member
who signed in before they were granted a tenant moves into it here.

The new session carries the sign-in on and ends when the old one would
have, so moving never extends a sign-in. The old session and its refresh
token stop working in the same step: use the `refresh_token` returned.
Records `organization.org_session_moved`. Requires the member's own
finished session.

200.description: The session that replaced the old one

403.description: The member may not reach that tenant

404.description: No such tenant in this organization

post.summary: Copy a tenant's setup into another
post.description:
Starts copying the named `parts` of one tenant's setup into another
tenant of the same organization, such as production's settings, roles
and routes into a fresh staging tenant. Users, sessions, signing keys
and secrets are never copied, and OAuth applications arrive without
their secrets. The copy runs in the background, part by part; follow it
with the id this answers.

Source and target the same tenant, no parts or a part named twice are
`422`. A closed source, a target that cannot be filled, or a target
another clone still fills is `409`. Records `tenant.clone_started` under
the target.

Requires a member who may make tenants in the organization, or an
operator.

409.description: Source closed, target unfillable or already being filled

get.summary: Follow a copy of a tenant's setup
get.description:
How far a clone has come: the parts it copies, those copied so far,
and whether it is `copying`, `completed` or `failed` (with why). A
member reads only clones into their own organization's tenants; any
other is `404`. Read-only.

Requires a member of the organization, or an operator.

Returns the tenants in this organization, optionally filtered by
`status` (`Provisioning`, `Active`, `Suspended`, `Archived` or
`Deleted`), sortable and paginated. Read-only.

A member who may view the organization's tenants sees every one of
them; any other member sees only the tenants they hold a grant in, the
same set the tenant routes admit them to. An operator sees every tenant
of the organization.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Only tenants in this status: `Provisioning`, `Active`, `Suspended`,
`Archived` or `Deleted`. Omit for every status.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, updated_at, display_name.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Creates a new tenant within this organization in `Provisioning` status:
its default roles, sign-in settings and signing keys are set up before
it goes `Active`. Provide a `slug`, `display_name`, `contact_email`,
`timezone`, `locale` and optionally a `residency`. A tenant starts with
no primary domain: it registers and proves one afterwards. The plan on
record decides whether there is room for another tenant and whether it
covers the residency (`403` otherwise). Returns the new tenant's `id`.

Returns `409` if another tenant of the organization has the slug (another
organization's tenant may), `404` if the organization does not exist, or
`422` for an invalid slug, name, address, timezone, locale or residency.
Records `tenant.provisioned` and `organization.tenant_created`.

Requires a member who may create the organization's tenants, or an
operator.

get.description:
Returns this tenant: name, primary domain, contact address,
timezone and locale, lifecycle `status`, where its data lives and where
its users sign in. Read-only.

Requires `TenantSettings(View)` for someone acting in the tenant, the
right to view the organization's tenants for a member, or an operator.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a tenant and takes it off its organization, so it
no longer counts against the plan. Irreversible. It must be `Archived`
first (`422` otherwise), and its grace must have run since (`409`
otherwise); the platform can cut the grace short with an early
deletion.

**State.** `Archived → Deleted` (terminal). Returns `404` if the tenant
does not exist. Records `tenant.status_changed` and `tenant.deleted`.

Requires a member who may delete the organization's tenants, or an
operator.

patch.description:
Partial update: send any of `display_name`, `contact_email`,
`timezone`, `locale`, `primary_domain` and `readable_address` to change just those; omit a
field to leave it. The primary domain must be one the tenant has
registered and proved (`422` otherwise). The token issuer changes with
the authentication configuration, not here. Records `tenant.renamed`,
`tenant.contact_email_changed`, `tenant.timezone_changed`,
`tenant.locale_changed` and `tenant.primary_domain_changed` for what
changed.

`readable_address` defaults to false. True explicitly publishes the tenant
and organization names in DNS and public certificate transparency logs;
false withdraws serving without erasing that public history. Null is
refused. Enabling requires nested platform addressing. Each actual change
records `tenant.readable_address_changed`.

Requires `TenantSettings(Update)`.

get.description:
Public JWK Set for checking `X-Ianua-Assertion`, separate from tenant
token-signing JWKS: neither kind of credential verifies against the other.
Includes the active key and keys rotated out within a day, never retired
keys; undecodable entries are skipped. Entries carry `kty`, `kid`, `alg`
(`ES256`) and key parameters. Refresh on an unknown `kid`; keys rotate
every thirty days. Returns `404` before keys exist. Records nothing.

404.description: No such tenant, or no assertion keys

get.description:
Serves the tenant's public signing keys as a JWKS document, so relying
parties can verify tokens this tenant issued. Includes every key still
published: active ones, and rotated ones through the grace period; never
revoked ones. Each entry gives `kty`, `kid`, `alg`, and the key
parameters (RSA `n`/`e`, EC `crv`/`x`/`y`, or EdDSA `crv`/`x`). A key
that fails to decode is skipped rather than failing the whole set.

Returns `404` if the tenant has no key set yet. Public: no
authentication. Records nothing.

404.description: No such tenant, or no keys

get.description:
The standard OpenID discovery document, so relying parties configure
themselves. Every URL is under this tenant's issuer: the authorization,
token, `userinfo`, pushed request, device, introspection, revocation,
end session and registration endpoints, and the JWKS document. It names
the grants, response modes, prompts, `acr` values, claims, signing
algorithms and client authentication methods offered, PKCE with
`S256`, the `iss` in authorization answers, and back- and front-channel
logout. Public. Records nothing.

Serves the transmitter metadata the Shared Signals framework asks for,
so a receiver can discover the tenant's transmitter: the `issuer` its
tokens carry, the `jwks_uri` their keys are published at, push and poll
delivery, the endpoint streams are registered at, and the status,
subject and verification endpoints. Those are per stream: each names
`{stream_id}` where the receiver puts its stream's id, and the receiver
calls them with the key it was handed at registration as its bearer.
Public: no authentication. Records nothing.

post.description:
Promotes a `Provisioning` tenant to `Active`, enabling sign-in and API
access.

**State.** `Provisioning → Active`. Returns `404` if the tenant does not
exist, or `422` if it is not `Provisioning`. Records
`tenant.status_changed`.

Requires an operator: provisioning activates a tenant itself once its
infrastructure exists, and this is the override for when it cannot.

get.description:
The same heatmap as the organization calendar, counting only this
tenant's events. Same window (`?from=&to=`), same response shape and
the same categories; use it for a tenant's own dashboard and the
organization calendar for the roll-up across all tenants. Read-only.

Requires `AuditLog(View)` in the tenant.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day of the window (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC, inclusive). Defaults to one year before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day of the window (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC, inclusive). Defaults to today.

get.description:
Returns this tenant's agent identities, sortable and paginated. Each
entry carries the agent's name, description, owner and lifecycle
`status`. Requires `Agents(View)`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, updated_at, name, status.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Registers an AI-agent principal for this tenant in `Active` status,
owned by the caller. Supply a display `name` and an optional
`description`. Optionally configures the attestation trust policy at
creation through `trusted_methods` (`spiffe`, `aws`, `gcp`, `tpm`),
`re_attest_every` (seconds) and `allowed_origins`, the first two given
together. An agent that will sign in with a durable key brings the
public half of a pair it made in `key`; its first credential is enrolled
from it. Creation is held to the tenant plan's agent limit. Returns the
new agent's `id` and that credential; `409` when another agent of the
tenant already has the name, `422` for an invalid name, policy or key
and `429` once the plan's limit is reached. Records
`agents.agent_created`. Requires `Agents(Create)`.

409.description: Another agent of the tenant has the name

get.description:
Returns the approval requests of every agent in the tenant, in the shape
an agent's own list answers. `?status=pending` is the tenant's approval
inbox; leaving it out returns the full history. Decide each through its
agent's `.../approvals/{approval_id}/approve` or `/deny`. Requires
`Agents(View)`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Narrows to one lifecycle state (`pending`, `approved`, `denied`,
`expired`, `consumed`, `withdrawn`). Left out for the full history,
resolved requests included.

get.summary: Read agent messages through the relay
get.description:
The agent presents its task token as the bearer credential. The relay
returns up to `max_messages` (at most 100) of the next messages on the
topic, each with the sender, its delegation and whom it acted for, as
verified from the signed provenance. A message whose provenance does
not verify is dropped and recorded, never returned. Reading another
agent's area needs an open channel, and raises the reader's data mark
to the topic's class. Rate limited per address.

parameters.name: max_messages
parameters.description: Maximum number of messages to return (default 10, at most 100).

200.description: The next messages on the topic

401.description: No valid task token for this tenant

post.summary: Publish an agent message through the relay
post.description:
The agent presents its task token as the bearer credential and sends
the message as the request body. The relay forwards it only when the
token is live and issued for this tenant, the agent is in good
standing, its delegation covers the topic for publishing, the topic
carries agent messages and declares a schema, the message is JSON of at
most 64 KiB that matches the schema, and the topic is cleared at least
as high as the data the agent has touched. The relay forwards the
message in canonical form and signs its provenance. Every decision is
recorded (`agents.message_authorized` or `agents.message_denied`). Rate
limited per address.

requestBody.description: The message: JSON matching the topic's schema

401.description: No valid task token for this tenant

422.description: The message does not match the topic's schema

get.summary: Read evidence as a reviewer agent
get.description:
The reviewer names itself in the `Ianua-Agent-Id` header and signs in
with an assertion its own key signed, in the `Ianua-Agent-Assertion`
header; each assertion is spent on use. Every request checks again that
a person's assignment stands, the reviewer holds no capability, and the
two agents still answer to different people. Rate limited per address.

parameters.name: after_seq
parameters.description: Return records after this chain position (default: from the start).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many records at most (default 50, at most 200).

parameters.name: ianua-agent-id
parameters.description: The reviewer agent's id

parameters.name: ianua-agent-assertion
parameters.description: The assertion the reviewer's key signed

403.description: Assertion refused, not assigned, or no longer independent

post.summary: Give a verdict as a reviewer agent
post.description:
Advisory only: a `concern` or a `containment_requested`, with a note and
the `seq` of at least one evidence record of the reviewed agent it rests
on. The verdict is recorded for a person; the reviewer acts on nothing.
Signed in as at the review desk's evidence. Records
`agents.review_verdict`.

parameters.name: ianua-agent-id
parameters.description: The reviewer agent's id

parameters.name: ianua-agent-assertion
parameters.description: The assertion the reviewer's key signed

204.description: Recorded for a person to act on

403.description: Assertion refused, not assigned, or no longer independent

422.description: Invalid verdict, or it cites records not the agent's

get.description:
Returns one page of run summaries across the tenant, newest first, in
the shape an agent's own list answers. `?status=` narrows to one lifecycle
state: `?status=awaiting_approval` is the tenant's run-approval inbox.
Requires `Agents(View)`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Narrows to one lifecycle state (`running`, `awaiting_approval`,
`paused`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `halted`,
`over_budget`). Left out to include every state in the page.

`awaiting_approval` is the run-approval inbox: each entry carries the
run's id, its purpose, and the `pending_tool`, `pending_arguments`
and `pending_at_step` held for sign-off.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

422.description: Invalid status, cursor or page limit

get.summary: List unregistered agents seen at work
get.description:
Returns the callers the gateway, the OAuth server or a cloud scan saw
acting like agents with no agent behind them: a person's key used by a
script, a client nobody tied to an agent, a workload holding
credentials. Each says where it was seen, what tells it apart, what it
called itself, and how often and when it was seen. `?shown=all` adds
those already registered or dismissed. A sighting grants nothing.
Requires `Agents(View)`.

parameters.name: shown
