parameters.description:
`unreviewed` for those nobody has dealt with yet, the default, or
`all`.

post.description:
Records that a sighted caller is no agent at all, dropping it from the
unreviewed list. What it does is still allowed or refused by the usual
rules. Records `agents.agent_sighting_dismissed`. Requires
`Agents(Manage)`.

post.summary: Register a sighting as an agent
post.description:
Records that a sighted caller is one of the tenant's agents, created for
it or already there, which puts it under delegations like any agent.
Records `agents.agent_sighting_registered`. Requires `Agents(Manage)`.

Emergency stop for the whole tenant: suspends every active agent at
once. The proxy refuses their tokens from the next request and their
runs halt before their next step. Unlike containment it can be undone,
by resuming each agent once it is known to be safe. Returns how many
were suspended. Every agent stops or none does. Records
`agents.all_agents_suspended` once, with the count. Requires
`Agents(Update)`.

get.description:
Every template in the tenant, newest first, retired ones included.
Requires `Agents(View)`.

post.description:
Writes down what one kind of agent task needs: the most it may be
granted, the kinds of action it may take, the paths, the most sensitive
data, the budget and the longest lifetime. Nothing can be granted under
it until a different person approves it. Records
`agents.task_template_proposed`. Requires `Agents(Delegate)`.

get.description:
One template, with its ceiling, its limits, and who proposed and
approved it. Requires `Agents(View)`.

post.description:
Must be a different person than proposed it. Delegations can be granted
under it from now on. Records `agents.task_template_approved`. Requires
`Agents(Delegate)`.

422.description: The proposer cannot approve, or it is not awaiting approval

post.description:
No new delegation can be granted under it. Delegations already granted
keep their own expiry; revoke them to end them sooner. Records
`agents.task_template_retired`. Requires `Agents(Delegate)`.

get.description:
Returns one agent by `id`: its display name, description, owner,
lifecycle `status` (`Active`, `Suspended`, `Revoked`) and attestation
policy. Requires the agent's owner or `Agents(View)`; anyone else gets
`404`, the same as for an agent this tenant does not have.

delete.description:
Removes an agent and its credential and approval history for good. The
agent must be revoked first. Records `agents.agent_deleted`. Requires
the agent's owner or `Agents(Delete)`.

patch.description:
Changes an agent's display `name` and `description` (leaving the
description out clears it); its owner and status are unchanged.
`trusted_methods` (`spiffe`, `aws`, `gcp`, `tpm`) and `re_attest_every`
(seconds) name the attestation trust policy together: leave both out to
keep it, send both as `null` to clear it, or send both with values to
replace it. Accepts `PUT` and `PATCH`. `404` if the agent does not
exist, `409` when another agent of the tenant already has the new name
or the agent changed meanwhile, `422` for an invalid name or policy, or
when the two fields disagree on which of those three this is. Records
`agents.agent_updated`. Requires the agent's owner or `Agents(Update)`.

409.description: The agent changed since it was read, or another agent of the tenant has the name

post.summary: Accept an agent offered to me
post.description:
The person an agent was offered to becomes its owner. What they hold is
read from their own sign-in, so a right lost since the offer no longer
counts. The agent keeps its status, keys and delegations; a delegation
the old owner granted still names them. Records
`agents.agent_ownership_transferred`, naming both owners.

403.description: Offered to someone else, or the caller may not own an agent

409.description: Not on offer: none was made, or it lapsed

get.description:
Returns the audit records the agent produced: what it did, for whom, and
whether each action was allowed or refused. Filterable by `event_type`
and a time window (`since`, `before`, RFC 3339), sortable and paged by
cursor (`after`, `limit` 20 when left out). Requires the agent's owner or
`Agents(View)`.

parameters.name: event_type
parameters.description: Only events whose type starts with this, such as `agents.delegation`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
Only events after this RFC 3339 timestamp. Named `since` because
`after` is the page cursor.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only events before this RFC 3339 timestamp.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: occurred_at, event_type.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

get.description:
Returns the agent's approval requests, newest first. `?status=` narrows
to one lifecycle state; leaving it out returns the full history,
resolved requests included: an approval's value as a record outlives
its decision window. Each entry names who asked and, once decided, who
decided and when. Requires the agent's owner or `Agents(View)`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Narrows to one lifecycle state (`pending`, `approved`, `denied`,
`expired`, `consumed`, `withdrawn`). Left out for the full history,
resolved requests included.

post.summary: Open a person's approval for a held action
post.description:
Records a pending approval for an agent's call under one of its
delegations, naming the exact call (`method` and `target`), and lets the
people who decide know. The call proceeds only once approved. The people
behind the delegation may not approve it. Records
`agents.approval_requested`. Requires the agent's owner or
`Agents(Update)`.

A person authorizes the held agent action. A delete, configuration,
financial or admin action, or one whose class is unknown, needs two
different people, each sending a fresh second-factor code as
`{"mfa_code": "..."}`: the first approval is recorded and the action
keeps waiting; the second grants it. The agent's owner and the people
behind its delegation may not approve, and the approver must be cleared
for the data the action has touched. `403` with a step-up error when the
code is missing, `403` for a wrong code or an approver with no second
factor, `404` if the approval does not exist, `422` if it is no longer
pending or the caller may not approve it, and `429` past the hourly
approvals one person may give. Records `agents.approval_signed` or
`agents.approval_granted`. Requires `Agents(Approve)`.

403.description: Forbidden, or a fresh second-factor code is needed

422.description: Not pending, or the caller may not approve it

post.description:
A person refuses the held agent action; a run that raised it drops the
call and goes on without it. `404` if the approval does not exist,
`422` if it is no longer pending. Records `agents.approval_denied`.
Requires `Agents(Approve)`.

get.description:
What ianua itself computed about the action, before what the agent
says: the exact call and the registered tool's method, path, action
class and data class; the most sensitive data the agent has touched;
whom it acts for; how often it was refused, drifted or met another
agent lately; and the open channels into it. The agent's own summary
comes last as `agent_claim`, with invisible characters stripped.
Requires the agent's owner or `Agents(Approve)`.

put.description:
Configures which platform attestations (`spiffe`, `aws`, `gcp`, `tpm`)
the agent accepts for secret-zero bootstrap, from which accounts,
projects or workloads, and how often it must re-attest. Deny by
default: bootstrap succeeds only for a verified attestation this policy
trusts. `404` if the agent does not exist, `422` for an unknown method,
no methods, no origins, or a zero interval. Records
`agents.agent_updated`. Requires the agent's owner or `Agents(Update)`.

post.description:
Reports whether the agent's live delegations grant an `action`, or,
given a `method` and `path` instead, whether the agent would be let
through for that request: the request is resolved against the tenant's
routes to find the governing policy, then checked the way the proxy
would. Nothing happens: no token is issued and no request is forwarded.
Answers `allow` or `deny` with a reason. `404` if the agent does not
exist, `422` when neither or both forms are given or the permission is
unknown. Requires the agent's owner or `Agents(View)`.

Reports whether the agent may exercise a `relation` on a `resource`,
with nothing happening. Deny by default: the agent needs a delegated
resource capability over the object, and either an exact match or a
relationship the graph confirms. `404` if the agent does not exist.
Requires the agent's owner or `Agents(View)`.

get.description:
Previews what containing the agent would cut: every delegation it holds
and every delegation descended from those, the exact set the kill-switch
revokes, with how many delegations and distinct agents that is. Requires
the agent's owner or `Agents(View)`.

post.summary: Bootstrap an agent from a platform attestation (secret-zero)
post.description:
The agent proves what it is with a platform `attestation` (a SPIFFE SVID,
a signed AWS `sts:GetCallerIdentity` request, a GCP instance identity
token, a TPM quote) bound to a challenge from
`POST .../bootstrap/challenge` and to the key it enrols; the platform
verifies it against the agent's attestation policy and enrols the public
key the workload made (`algorithm`, `public_key`) as a short-lived
identity credential. No
standing secret, and the private key never leaves the workload. No
session: the agent signs in by the attestation, and every failure is
`403`. Rate limited per address. Records `agents.agent_bootstrapped`.

post.summary: Request an attestation challenge (step 1 of bootstrap)
post.description:
Returns a single-use nonce bound to this agent. Bind it to the public key
the workload will enrol (SHA-256 of `ianua-attestation-binding-v1`, a
zero byte, the nonce, a zero byte and the key's DER), carry that binding
in the attestation, and send both to `/bootstrap`. Attestation material,
a SPIFFE SVID say, is a public document, so presenting it alone proves
nothing; the binding is what proves the caller is the workload, now,
enrolling its own key, rather than someone holding a copy of its
certificate or a token seen in passing. The challenge expires within
minutes and is spent on first use, so a captured request cannot be
replayed. No session; rate limited per address. Records
`agents.attestation_challenge_issued`.

post.summary: Compile an intent into a narrowed scope (dry-run)
post.description:
Turns a natural-language `intent` and a `requested` scope into the
narrowed capability set the intent implies for this agent, with a digest
for drift monitoring. It only narrows: the result never exceeds
`requested`. Nothing is granted. Requires `Agents(View)`.

Emergency stop: revokes the agent, its keys, and its whole delegation
blast radius in one action, every delegation it holds and every
delegation descended from those. The proxy refuses the revoked tokens at
once, and every agent it delegated to is cut off with it. Containing an
agent with no live delegations revokes none. Returns how many
delegations were revoked. Records `agents.agent_contained`. Requires the
agent's owner or `Agents(Delete)`.

get.description:
Returns the identity credentials the agent holds, active and rotated
ones, as public metadata (never a private key). Requires the agent's
owner or `Agents(View)`.

post.description:
Enrols the public half of a key pair the agent made for itself
(`algorithm`, `public_key`) and returns the credential's metadata (`id`,
`kid`, `algorithm`, `public_key`). The private half never leaves the
agent: the platform neither generates nor returns one. The agent signs
assertions with its key for the token exchange.

An enrolled credential is unattested (`attestation` is `null`) and its
`kid` is generated by the server; neither is settable here. Attestation
binding happens only through `POST .../bootstrap`, where the platform
has a proof to verify.

`404` if the agent does not exist, `409` if it is not active, `422` for
an unknown algorithm or a key that is not a public key of it. Records
`agents.credential_minted`. Requires the agent's owner or
`Agents(Update)`.

delete.description:
Revokes an identity credential for good: assertions signed by it no
longer verify. `404` if the credential is not the agent's, `422` if it
was revoked already. Records `agents.credential_revoked`. Requires the
agent's owner or `Agents(Delete)`.

post.description:
Retires the credential (it stays verifiable during a grace period but no
longer signs) and enrols the replacement public key the agent made, with
the same expiry. A refused key leaves the old credential as it was.
Returns the new credential; the retired one reports its `rotated_at`,
`grace_ends_at` and `grace_period_seconds` when listed, so the window it
counts down is visible. `404` if the credential is not the agent's,
`422` if it was revoked. Records `agents.credential_rotated`. Requires
the agent's owner or `Agents(Update)`.

get.description:
Returns everything the agent asked of anyone, newest first, answered
or not. Requires the agent's owner or `Agents(View)`.

post.summary: Ask a person for a delegation (agent)
post.description:
An agent that needs more than it holds asks a person for it, signed in
as itself with an assertion its own key signed in the
`Ianua-Agent-Assertion` header: what it needs (`granted` and the limits
asked for), of whom (`asked_of`, a tenant user or an organization
member), and why (`reason`). Asking grants nothing: the person sees the
request and grants or refuses it, within a day. An agent keeps only a
few requests open and makes only so many an hour (`429`). No session.
Rate limited per address. Records `agents.delegation_requested`.

parameters.name: ianua-agent-assertion
parameters.description: An assertion the agent's own key signed, made for the deployment's token audience

401.description: No assertion, or no such tenant

403.description: The assertion does not sign the agent in, or it may not act

404.description: The person asked is not one of the tenant's

429.description: Too many requests open, or made this hour

post.description:
The person an agent asked grants what it asked for, as a delegation
from them, checked like any grant: they must own the agent or be
allowed to delegate to agents, and it is held to what they hold now,
never to what the agent asked for. The agent takes its task token from
the delegation through the token exchange. Records
`agents.delegation_request_approved` and the grant.

403.description: Not the person asked, or more than they hold

post.description:
Refuses what an agent asked for. The person asked refuses it, and so
may someone allowed to manage agents, to stop an agent pestering
people. A refused request grants nothing and is never answered again.
Records `agents.delegation_request_denied`.

403.description: Neither the person asked nor allowed to manage agents

get.description:
Returns the delegations the agent holds, each with its delegator (and
their name), what it grants, its expiry, its parent for a
sub-delegation, how much of its budget is used, and whether it was
revoked. Requires the agent's owner or `Agents(View)`.

delete.description:
Revokes a delegation and every delegation descended from it: a
delegation is only valid while each one above it is, so the whole
subtree goes at once. `404` if the delegation is not the agent's.
Records `agents.delegation_revoked`. Requires the agent's owner or
`Agents(Delegate)`.

post.description:
Narrows one of the agent's delegations into a child for another agent:
the child can never exceed the parent, its depth is one greater, and it
cannot outlive it. It may set its own budget, paths, apps, approval rule
and key binding, each inside the parent's; its budget shares the
parent's with the children already passed on. A sender-constrained
parent stays sender-constrained on the child, and an approval rule stays
too. Mints a task token for the receiving agent.

Passed on by a person with a say over the holding agent, signed in as
any tenant caller, or by the holding agent itself, signing in with an
assertion its own key signed, sent in the `Ianua-Agent-Assertion`
header. Rate limited per address.

`403` on escalation, exceeded depth or a refused assertion, `404` if the
delegation or the receiving agent is missing, `409` if the receiving
agent is not active or (under a sender-constrained parent) has no active
credential to bind. Records `agents.delegation_granted`.

parameters.name: ianua-agent-assertion
parameters.description: The assertion the holding agent signed, when the agent itself passes it on

403.description: Forbidden: more than the parent grants, deeper or longer than it allows, a wider limit or a budget past what it has left, or the assertion refused

409.description: The receiving agent is not active, or the parent is sender-constrained and the receiving agent has no single active credential to bind

422.description: Validation error, or a field the body does not know

post.description:
Gives a delegation its lifetime again, counted from now, so an agent
working on keeps its authority without a new grant. Only the person who
granted it renews it, and only while they still hold everything it
grants, to an agent that may still receive authority. Only a delegation
a person granted at the top of its chain is renewed; one expired or
revoked is granted anew instead (`422`). Records
`agents.delegation_renewed` with when it now expires.

403.description: Forbidden: not its delegator, or no longer holding what it grants

422.description: Not granted by a person at the top of its chain, or revoked or expired

post.summary: Grant a resource to a delegation
post.description:
Adds one `{relation, resource}` to a granted delegation's resources,
without granting the whole delegation again. The caller must hold the
resource themselves (the same rule as granting or passing on), and for
a sub-delegation the resource must also be within what its parent
grants. Granting one already held changes nothing. Records
`agents.delegation_resource_granted`. Requires `Agents(Delegate)`.

403.description: Forbidden: more than the caller holds, or for a sub-delegation more than its parent grants

422.description: Validation error, or the delegation is revoked

delete.summary: Revoke a resource from a delegation
delete.description:
Removes one `{relation, resource}` from a delegation, leaving the rest
of what it grants, and the delegation itself, untouched. Revoking one
not held changes nothing. Records `agents.delegation_resource_revoked`.
Requires the agent's owner or `Agents(Delegate)`.

422.description: Validation error, or the delegation is revoked

get.description:
Returns the union of what the agent's live delegations grant: the
authority the proxy would enforce right now. Revoked or expired
delegations add nothing. `404` if the agent does not exist. Requires the
agent's owner or `Agents(View)`.

What ianua recorded about the agent, oldest first, each record with its
place (`seq`) and hash in the tenant's chain, and the scheduled sweep's
last verdict on the whole chain (`not_verified_yet` before the first
sweep). Requires the agent's owner or `Agents(View)`.

parameters.name: after_seq
parameters.description: Return records after this chain position (default: from the start).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many records at most (default 50, at most 200).

post.summary: Lower a stopped agent's data mark
post.description:
An agent's mark only rises while it runs, because its context holds
what it read. Once it is suspended, a person who has looked may lower it
so the agent can return to less sensitive work. Refused (`409`) while
the agent is active. Records `agents.exposure_reset` with the reason
given. Requires the agent's owner or `Agents(Delegate)`.

422.description: Not lower than the current mark

post.description:
Delegates a slice of the caller's own authority to the agent: the
granted capabilities can never exceed what the caller holds. The grant
is bound by a lifetime, a maximum sub-delegation depth, and optionally a
task, an intent, a budget, a resource scope, the apps it reaches, an
approval gate and a sender constraint; under a `template_id` it must fit
that approved template. Returns the new delegation and its task token;
`403` if it asks for more than the caller holds, `404` if the agent does
not exist, `409` if the agent is not active or `sender_constrained` was
asked for but the agent has no single active credential to bind. Records
`agents.delegation_granted`. Requires `Agents(Delegate)`.

403.description: Forbidden: more than the caller holds

409.description: Agent not active, or sender_constrained was asked for but the agent has no single active credential to bind

422.description: Validation error, or a field the body does not know

post.summary: Offer an agent to another person
post.description:
The owner names the tenant user who is to look after the agent from now
on, such as before moving teams. Nothing moves until they accept, signed
in themselves; the offer lapses after a week. Whether they may own an
agent is worked out from what the tenant's records say they hold. A new
offer replaces one standing. Answers the agent with the standing offer.
Records `agents.agent_ownership_offered`. Requires the agent's owner or
`Agents(Manage)`.

403.description: Forbidden, or the recipient may not own an agent

409.description: The recipient owns the agent already

delete.summary: Withdraw or decline an agent offer
delete.description:
Ends a standing offer unaccepted: the owner withdraws it, or the person
it was made to declines it. The agent stays with its owner. Records
`agents.agent_ownership_offer_withdrawn`. Requires the owner, the
recipient or `Agents(Manage)`.

post.description:
Makes the agent prove itself again: from the next request the proxy
refuses every token it presents until it bootstraps again with a fresh
platform attestation. Unlike containment this leaves its delegations in
place; it earns them back by attesting. Asking twice changes nothing
more. Records `agents.reattestation_required`. Requires the agent's
owner or `Agents(Update)`.

Reactivates a suspended agent so its delegations work again. `404` if
the agent does not exist, `422` if it was revoked (revocation is
final). Records `agents.agent_resumed`. Requires the agent's owner or
`Agents(Update)`.

post.summary: Assign a reviewer to an agent
post.description:
Sets `reviewer_agent_id` to watch the agent in the path. Refused
(`422`) unless the two answer to different people (the owners and every
person in the lineage of their live delegations differ) and share no
delegation; refused (`403`) while the reviewer holds any capability. A
reviewer reads evidence and does nothing else, and from now on cannot be
granted capabilities. Records `agents.reviewer_assigned`. Requires a say
over both agents: `Agents(Update)`, since their owners differ.

403.description: Forbidden, or the reviewer holds capabilities

422.description: The two agents are not independent

get.description:
Every assignment where the agent reviews or is reviewed, newest first,
ended ones included. Requires the agent's owner or `Agents(View)`.

post.description:
The reviewer loses access to the agent's evidence on its next request.
Records `agents.review_ended`. Requires the reviewed agent's owner or
`Agents(Delegate)`.

Revokes an agent for good: it can never be reactivated and all its
authority is withdrawn. `404` if the agent does not exist, `422` if it
was revoked already. Records `agents.agent_revoked`. Requires the
agent's owner or `Agents(Delete)`.

get.description:
Returns one page of run summaries, newest first, including token use and
spend. `?status=` narrows to one lifecycle state. Pass `next_cursor` as
`?after=` for another page. Read an individual run for its steps and answer.

`?status=awaiting_approval` is the run-approval inbox: the runs paused
on a tool call waiting for a person, each carrying the run's id, its
purpose, and the `pending_tool`, `pending_arguments` and
`pending_at_step` held for the decision. Decide with
`POST .../runs/{run_id}/approve` or `/deny`.

Requires the agent's owner or `Agents(View)`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Narrows to one lifecycle state (`running`, `awaiting_approval`,
`paused`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `halted`,
`over_budget`). Left out to include every state in the page.

`awaiting_approval` is the run-approval inbox: each entry carries the
run's id, its purpose, and the `pending_tool`, `pending_arguments`
and `pending_at_step` held for sign-off.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

422.description: Invalid status, cursor or page limit

post.summary: Run an agent toward a goal
post.description:
Starts a governed run and answers at once with the `running` run; a
worker drives the loop from there, calling only the tools the run was
granted whose action is inside the run's `purpose`: a tool outside it is
refused whatever the model asks for. `spend_limit_micros` caps what its
model calls may cost; the run stops as `over_budget` once it is spent.
`ask_past_micros` pauses it once it spent that much, recording
`agents.run_held_at_spend`, until whoever may resume it lets it go on.
Poll the run to watch it, pause it to look closer, and cancel it to
stop early. Records `agents.run_started`. Requires the agent's owner or
`Agents(Delegate)`.

404.description: Agent or model provider not found

get.description:
Returns one run with its full step trace: the record of what the agent
did. Requires the agent's owner or `Agents(View)`, and clearance for
the data the run has read.

post.description:
Approves the tool call a run paused on (`awaiting_approval`) through the
approval request the run raised for it: the same decision as approving
that request in the inbox. A low-risk call resumes at once. A delete,
configuration, financial or admin call needs two different people, each
sending a fresh second-factor code as `mfa_code`; the run resumes on the
second.

The body names the call approved (`tool`, `arguments`, `at_step`, as the
run shows them). A decision naming a call the run raised no open
approval for is refused with `404`, and one landing after the run moved
on with `409`, rather than applied to whatever is there now. `422` if
the run is not awaiting approval or the caller may not approve it, such
as the person who started it. Answers where the run stands now; read
the run for its steps. Requires `Agents(Approve)`.

403.description: Forbidden, or a fresh second-factor code is needed

404.description: Run not found, or no open approval for that call

409.description: The held call changed since it was looked at

422.description: Not awaiting approval, or the caller may not approve it

put.summary: Change the call a run holds
put.description:
Replaces the `arguments` of the tool call a run is paused on
(`awaiting_approval`), such as pointing a payment at the staging ledger
instead. The approval request raised for the old call is withdrawn and
a new one is raised for the changed call, which waits for its approvers
like any other. The change keeps the tool and its class of action:
another tool or class is `409`. Answers the run and the new approval
request. Records `agents.held_call_revised`. Requires `Agents(Approve)`
and clearance for the data the run has read.

200.description: Changed; waiting on a new approval

404.description: Run not found, or no open approval for its call

409.description: The run moved on, or the change is not one the tool takes

422.description: Not awaiting approval, or invalid arguments

post.description:
Asks a run in flight to stop; the loop notices between steps, records
the stop, and lands in `cancelled`. Approvals a paused run waited on are
withdrawn. Cancelling a finished run changes nothing. Returns the run
as it stood when asked. Records `agents.run_cancel_requested`. Requires
the agent's owner or `Agents(Delegate)`.

post.summary: Deny a paused run's tool call
post.description:
Refuses the tool call a run paused on and resumes it; the refusal is
recorded and handed back to the model, which goes on without the call.
`422` if the run is not awaiting approval. Answers where the run stands
now. Records `agents.approval_denied`. Requires `Agents(Approve)`.

Holds a running run before its next step, so a person can look at what
it did so far. A paused run takes no step and makes no call until it is
resumed; cancelling it still works. `422` if the run is not running,
such as one waiting on an approval or one that ended. Records
`agents.run_paused`. Requires whoever started the run, the agent's
owner or `Agents(Update)`.

409.description: The run took a step since it was read; try again

post.summary: Answer a run's held call in words
post.description:
Instead of letting the call a run is paused on run, tells the agent
something, such as "use the staging ledger instead". The call is never
made: its approval request is denied, the `reply` is recorded as the
run's next step (`replied`) for the model to read, and the run goes on.
Takes the same right as denying the call. Records
`agents.approval_denied`. Requires `Agents(Approve)`.

404.description: Run not found, or no open approval for its call

409.description: The run holds another call now

422.description: Not awaiting approval, or an invalid reply

post.description:
Hands a paused run back to a worker, which takes its next step. `422`
if the run is not paused. Records `agents.run_resumed`. Requires
whoever started the run, the agent's owner or `Agents(Update)`.

409.description: The run changed since it was read; try again

post.description:
Disables an agent for now: while it is suspended none of its delegations
work and any task token it holds is refused at the proxy. Undone by
resuming it. `404` if the agent does not exist, `422` if it was revoked.
Records `agents.agent_suspended`. Requires the agent's owner or
`Agents(Update)`.

Makes the caller the agent's owner, for an agent whose owner left or
moved to other work, so it never stays with nobody looking after it.
The agent keeps its status, keys and delegations; a delegation the old
owner granted still names them. Records
`agents.agent_ownership_transferred`, naming both owners. Requires
`Agents(Manage)`, and the right to create agents.

200.description: Taken over: the caller owns it

403.description: Forbidden, or the caller may not own an agent

post.summary: Exchange an assertion for a task token (client credentials)
post.description:
The agent proves it holds its identity key by presenting an `assertion`
it signed for this tenant's token endpoint; the platform verifies it
against the agent's stored public key, spends it so it cannot be used
twice, and mints a task token for at most the authority the agent holds
through its live delegations. No session: the agent signs in by the
assertion, and every failure to sign in is `403`, the same whether the
agent exists or not. Rate limited per address. Records
`agents.token_issued`. A refusal that looks like an attack (a replayed
or forged assertion, or one naming another agent) records
`agents.token_attack_refused` about the agent it named, at most once an
hour per agent and kind of attack, and alerts the tenant's
administrators.

403.description: Assertion refused or agent not active

post.description:
Soft-deletes an `Active` or `Suspended` tenant: every session is signed
out and its data is kept through a grace period. Until the grace has
run it can be restored; after it, deleted.

**State.** `Active | Suspended → Archived`. Returns `404` if the tenant
does not exist, or `422` from any other status. Records
`tenant.status_changed`.

Requires a member who may delete the organization's tenants, or an
operator.

get.description:
Returns this tenant's own audit-log entries, with the same filters,
sorting and paging as the organization's log. The log read is always
this tenant's: a `tenant_id` naming another is ignored. Read-only.

Requires `ViewAuditLog`.

parameters.name: event_type
parameters.description:
Only events whose type starts with this, such as
`organization.org_user`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
Only events after this RFC 3339 timestamp. Named `since` because
`after` is the page cursor.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only events before this RFC 3339 timestamp.

parameters.name: actor
parameters.description:
Only events this actor performed: `system`, `anonymous`, or
`<kind>:<uuid>` with kind `user`, `org_user`, `operator`, `api_key`,
`oauth_client` or `service`.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description:
Only events in this tenant. A tenant's own log is always its own,
whatever this says.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Only events about the entity with this id.

parameters.name: ip_address
parameters.description: Only events from this client address.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: occurred_at, event_type.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Starts an export of this tenant's own audit-log entries, with the same
filters and formats as the organization's export, written by the worker
in full. Poll `GET .../audit-log/exports/{id}` for the file. Records
`tenant.audit_log_export_requested`.

Requires `ExportAuditLog` (`idp:audit_log:export`); viewing the log is
not enough.

429.description: As many exports are waiting as the tenant may have

get.summary: Get an export of the tenant's audit log
get.description:
Where the export stands, and once ready a signed `download_url` that
works once, for a few minutes, as for the organization's exports.
Records `tenant.audit_log_export_downloaded` for each link handed out.

Requires `ExportAuditLog` (`idp:audit_log:export`); viewing the log is
not enough.

200.description: The export, with a download link once written

get.description:
Every stream of this tenant's audit records to a SIEM: its name, where
it sends (kind, address, index, site or host, and the name of any
header, never a credential), which event types it sends (`null` for
all), and whether it is `active`, `failing` (since when, how many sends
in a row) or `paused` (why, since when). Read-only.

Requires the right to view the tenant's compliance settings.

post.description:
Sends new tenant audit records to Splunk HEC, Datadog, syslog over TLS, or
any public HTTPS endpoint, each by `destination.kind`. `events` narrows
it to some event types. Addresses must be public; the credential
(collector token, API key, header value) is sealed at once and never
shown again.

A stream copies every record out of the platform, so the body carries
`proof`, the caller's own sign-in typed again: a change made with an
API key, or with a proof that does not hold, is `403`, and a proof
missing the code of the caller's second factor asks for it. The plan's
audit stream limit is `403`. Records `tenant.audit_stream_created`,
naming the kind of destination only.

Requires the right to change the tenant's compliance settings.

409.description: As many streams as the tenant may keep

put.description:
Replaces the stream's name, destination and events whole, with the
destination's credential typed again. Like adding one, the body carries
`proof`, the caller's own sign-in typed again. Records
`tenant.audit_stream_changed`.

Requires the right to change the tenant's compliance settings.

delete.description:
Stops the stream for good and forgets its destination and credential.
Records `tenant.audit_stream_removed`.

Requires the right to change the tenant's compliance settings.

post.description:
Stops sending records through the stream until it is resumed; records
made meanwhile are not sent later. A stream already paused is `409`.
Records `tenant.audit_stream_paused`.

Requires the right to change the tenant's compliance settings.

Starts sending through a paused stream again, whether an administrator
paused it or its destination refused too many sends in a row. A stream
not paused is `409`. Records `tenant.audit_stream_resumed`.

Requires the right to change the tenant's compliance settings.

get.description:
The last verdict of the scheduled sweep that walks the tenant's
hash-linked audit records, proving no record was removed, reordered or
edited after the fact. Answers `status` (`intact`, `intact_so_far` while
a long chain is still being walked, `broken`, or `not_verified_yet`
before the first sweep), `verified_at`, the last record verified
(`checked_through_seq`), and the first tampered record when it is
broken. The chain is not walked in the request. This is the evidence
that an agent stayed in purpose. Read-only.

Requires `AuditLog(View)`.

200.description: The last verdict on the chain

get.description:
Everything about how this tenant's users sign in: the methods allowed,
the password rules, the MFA policy, session and idle lifetimes, the
lockout threshold, self-registration, the IP allowlist, the token
issuer and the step-up policy.

A tenant that has never changed it gets the defaults: password only,
12 characters with upper, lower and a digit, MFA off, 8-hour sessions,
10 attempts then a 15-minute lockout, and a relaxed step-up policy.

Read-only. Requires `AuthConfig(View)`.

put.description:
Replaces all fields together. Requires a session and fresh `proof`: password
with second-factor `code`, mailed sign-in link or passkey answer. API keys
and invalid proof give `403`. Remembered devices matter only with `require_mfa_new_device`.

`mfa_policy: Required` demands a factor immediately; removing `enabled_methods`
stops those sign-ins. Refuses changes that shut out the current sign-in.
Password rules apply at the next change/reset, not to existing passwords.

Returns `422` when the configuration contradicts itself: no method
enabled, a password floor below 8, an idle timeout outlasting its
session, a lockout threshold under 2, or a sensitive assurance level
below the ordinary one. Records `tenant.auth_config_updated`.

Requires `AuthConfig(Update)`.

post.description:
Emergency access for when normal authorization is in the way of an
active incident. Mints a **time-boxed** grant of the permissions it
names (`system_permissions`, `custom_permissions`) so a user can act
during an outage or security event.

Break-glass is deliberately loud, not a backdoor: every grant is fully
audited with who, why, and for how long, and it expires on its own. The
approver is the caller; whether they may approve it, and how much they
may give, is the tenant's break-glass policy's to decide. Revoke it early
at the break-glass revoke endpoint once the incident is contained.

422.description: Validation error, or a grant naming nothing

post.description:
Ends an active emergency grant immediately, before its natural expiry.
Call this the moment elevated access is no longer needed: the shorter
the window, the smaller the blast radius.

The revocation is audited alongside the original grant, closing the loop
on the incident. Revoking a grant that is already revoked or has already
expired returns `409` (not a no-op); guard the UI accordingly.

get.description:
Returns the device entries the signed-in user has registered: all of
them, in creation order.

The list is **not** filtered to active devices: a `Revoked` device is
kept for history and still appears here, though it no longer gets the
MFA skip. Read `status` to tell the two apart: only `trusted` entries
take the fast path, and only they can be revoked.

**Device status.** Entries are `Trusted` until they move
`Trusted → Revoked` (terminal) via the device-revoke endpoint; there is
no automatic expiry.

post.description:
Marks the current device as trusted so future logins from it can skip
MFA step-up until the tenant's trust window expires. This is the
"remember this device" checkbox on the login screen.

Trust is a convenience traded against risk: only offer it on devices the
user controls, never shared or public machines. The grant is scoped to
this user and can be pulled at any time from the device list. Each user
has a capped number of trusted devices; exceeding it returns `409`
(revoke one first to free a slot). The address and user agent recorded
are the request's own.

**Device status.** Registers the device in **`Trusted`** status, letting
it skip MFA within the trust window. The only transition out is
`Trusted → Revoked`.

Removes trust from a device. The next login from it has to pass full MFA
step-up again: the fast path is gone.

Use this the instant a device is lost, sold, or looks unfamiliar in the
trusted list. Revocation takes effect immediately and is scoped to the
signed-in user's own devices.

**Device status.** Moves the device `Trusted → Revoked`. `Revoked` is
terminal: a revoked device is treated as unknown on the next login and
must be trusted again from scratch. Revoking a device that's already
revoked returns `409`.

get.description:
The caller's own certificates, as recorded when issued: label, validity
and whether revoked. Never the PEM. Requires a tenant user's own
session.

post.description:
Signs a certificate from a signing request made on the device: the
private key never leaves it. A person binds to the LDAP directory only
over a connection presenting this certificate, with their password; a
password alone binds nobody. Issuing one is as sensitive as changing a
password, so the
body carries a fresh `proof` (password, mailbox link or passkey). The
PEM is answered once and not kept for showing again. Requires a tenant
user's own session.

403.description: The proof did not prove who they are

delete.description:
Ends the certificate's power to authenticate LDAP writes at once. A
certificate of someone else's answers `404`, as one that does not exist
does. Records `authentication.ldap_certificate_revoked`.

get.description:
Every service account of the tenant, by name, with its scope and status.
Never a secret. Records nothing.

post.description:
Makes an active account an application binds to the directory as, with
what it may reach: `ReadOnly`, the only access, under one to sixteen
base DNs. The answer carries its `secret` this once; only its hash is kept.
Checked against the plan's limit. Records
`authentication.directory_service_account_created`.

201.description: Created, with its secret shown once

403.description: Forbidden, or the plan's limit is reached

get.description:
One service account with its scope and status. Never its secret.
Records nothing.

delete.description:
Removes the account; a connection bound as it reads nothing more from
its next search. Records
`authentication.directory_service_account_deleted`.

post.summary: Switch an LDAP service account on
post.description:
`Disabled -> Active`: it binds again. Records
`authentication.directory_service_account_status_changed`.

post.summary: Switch an LDAP service account off
post.description:
`Active -> Disabled`: it binds no more, and connections bound before
stop counting at their next request. Records
`authentication.directory_service_account_status_changed`.

post.summary: Rotate an LDAP service account's secret
post.description:
Gives the account a new secret, shown this once; every connection bound
with the old one stops counting at its next request. Records
`authentication.directory_service_account_secret_rotated`.

put.summary: Change what an LDAP service account may reach
put.description:
Replaces the account's access and base DNs. Connections bound before
read the new scope at their next request. Records
`authentication.directory_service_account_scope_changed`.

post.description:
Ends the session the bearer names, so its refresh token can no longer be
used, whether or not it finished signing in. Not idempotent: ending a
session that already ended returns `409`; guard the UI against
double-logouts, or ignore `409`.

Only this session is ended; the user's other active sessions (other
devices, browsers) keep working. Revoke those separately.

**Session status.** Moves the session `Active → Revoked`. `Revoked` is
terminal: the session can never be reactivated, so the user signs in
again for a new one. Records `authentication.session_revoked`.

Passwordless login: emails a single-use sign-in link to the address.
Always returns `204` regardless of whether the email exists, to prevent
enumeration. Public, no session required.

204.description: If the email belongs to an active user, a sign-in link was sent

post.summary: Consume a magic link and start a session
post.description:
Verifies the single-use token from the emailed link and returns a
session (`session_id` + `refresh_token`). The token is consumed, so the
link can't be used again. Public, no prior session required.

Like a password sign-in, the session may still owe a second factor
(`mfa_required`), or one being set up first (`mfa_enrollment_required`).

delete.description:
Turns off the signed-in tenant user's second factor. Requires a `code`
from the authenticator being removed, the same proof changing a password
requires of the old password: without it, a stolen session was enough to
strip the factor and enrol another. If the tenant's policy requires MFA,
the user is asked to set one up again on their next sign-in.

post.description:
Returns a fresh TOTP secret as an `otpauth://` URI for a QR code.
Signed-in people supply `proof` (password and any existing factor);
a waiting `mfa_enrollment_required` sign-in uses its temporary permission.
Enrollment stays `Pending` until a code confirms `Pending → Verified`.
Calling again replaces the pending secret and requires scanning again.
Active MFA returns `409` and must first be disabled, except that a
waiting sign-in which spent a recovery code may replace the lost factor
while its enrollment permission remains fresh.

403.description: The proof does not prove the person, a code is needed (`step_up_required`), or the tenant has second factors off

post.description:
Gives up an authenticator setup that was begun and never confirmed, so
the next enrollment starts from a new secret. Takes the same `proof` as
starting one: a signed-in person proves who they are again, a sign-in
waiting for the factor sends none. An active factor is not touched; turn
it off with `DELETE …/auth/mfa`.

403.description: The proof does not prove the person

post.summary: Start setting up mailed or texted codes
post.description:
Begins a second factor whose codes are mailed to the account's address
(`email_code`) or texted to `phone_number` (`sms_code`), and sends the
first code at once. Confirm it with that code at the enroll-confirm
endpoint. A signed-in person sends a `proof` of who they are; a sign-in
that answered `mfa_enrollment_required` sends none. A setup still waiting
to be confirmed is replaced. Codes reach a lower assurance than an
authenticator app, so a tenant whose baseline needs more does not offer
them. Records `authentication.mfa_enrollment_started` and
`authentication.mfa_code_sent`.

200.description: The first code is on its way

403.description: The proof does not prove the person, or the tenant does not offer this factor

409.description: A second factor is already in force

post.description:
A valid code activates the pending authenticator (`Pending → Verified`)
and returns single-use recovery codes, shown only once; keep them safe.
Wrong or stale codes return `403` and leave enrollment pending; repeated
failures lock it (`429`). Records `authentication.mfa_enrolled` and
`authentication.recovery_codes_generated`.
To finish a `mfa_enrollment_required` sign-in, send its `session_id`
with its refresh token as bearer. Different sessions return `403`;
matching ones finish enrollment and make that session usable at once.

403.description: Wrong or used code, or the sign-in named is not the bearer's own session

get.description:
The kinds of second factor the tenant offers the person (`totp`,
`email_code`, `sms_code`), the one they hold and how far it went, and,
for a sign-in waiting for its factor (named by `session_id`), what it
still owes. Read-only.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description:
The session a sign-in answered with, while it waits for its second
factor.

200.description: What may be set up, what is held, what is owed

403.description: The sign-in named is not the bearer's own session

post.description:
Mails or texts a fresh code for the person's code factor, in force or
still to be confirmed: for a sign-in waiting for it (name its
`session_id`), or for a person signed in who must prove the factor again
before a change. The code replaces any sent before. Records
`authentication.mfa_code_sent`.

200.description: A code is on its way

403.description: The sign-in named is not the bearer's own session

404.description: No factor in use, or the waiting sign-in is gone

409.description: The factor is an authenticator app, or the sign-in owes nothing

429.description: A code went out moments ago

get.description:
Returns whether the signed-in tenant user has MFA enrolled (`enabled`)
and the `method` (e.g. `Totp`) if so. An enrollment that was begun but
never confirmed with a code counts as not enabled. Read-only: the tenant
twin of the organization plane's MFA status.

post.description:
Completes a step-up challenge. When a login returns `mfa_required: true`,
the session is limited until the user submits a valid code from their
authenticator app here, with the session's own bearer.

A correct code promotes the session to fully authenticated. Codes are
time-based and short-lived; a wrong or expired code returns `403`.
Repeated failures count toward lockout: once exceeded, the response is
`429` (account locked). No authenticator handy? Use a recovery code
instead.

**Enrollment status.** Only a **`Verified`** enrollment can answer a
step-up challenge. This endpoint doesn't change the enrollment status; it
clears the session's step-up requirement.

Begins a passwordless sign-in with a registered passkey. Returns a
one-time challenge for the browser's `navigator.credentials.get()` call,
which the user satisfies with a biometric or security-key tap.

The challenge is short-lived and single-use. Pass the browser's
assertion response to the login-confirm endpoint to complete
authentication and receive a session.

**Anti-enumeration.** An unknown email, or a known user with no
registered passkeys, returns a **dummy challenge** of the same shape so
the response is indistinguishable from a real one: the endpoint can't be
used to probe which accounts or passkeys exist.

Completes a passwordless sign-in. Submit the assertion from the browser's
`navigator.credentials.get()` call; the server verifies the signature
against the stored credential and the challenge issued at start, then
updates the authenticator's sign counter.

On success you get a session and a `refresh_token`, exactly like a
password login, but nothing phishable ever crossed the wire. The
authenticator proved possession and user verification, so the session
usually owes nothing more.

An unrecognized credential returns `404`; a failed assertion
verification returns `403`, as does a sign counter that went
**backwards** (a cloned authenticator).

403.description: The assertion does not verify, or a cloned authenticator

post.description:
Begins a usernameless sign-in: no email, no credential list. This powers
conditional UI: the browser offers a saved passkey from the empty email
field, and the credential the user picks names its own account.

Returns a one-time challenge for `navigator.credentials.get()` with
`mediation: "conditional"`. Complete it at the regular login-confirm
endpoint with the assertion and the credential id.

Begins registering a WebAuthn passkey: a phishing-resistant credential
backed by the device's secure hardware (Touch ID, Face ID, Windows Hello,
a security key). Returns a one-time challenge for the browser's
`navigator.credentials.create()` call.

Nothing is stored yet: the challenge is bound to the signed-in user and
expires quickly. The name the authenticator shows comes from their
account, never from the request. Hand the browser's attestation response
to the register-confirm endpoint to finish. Records
`authentication.passkey_registration_started`.

Finishes enrolling a passkey. Submit the attestation response from the
browser's `navigator.credentials.create()` call, with a `proof` that the
signed-in person is who they say (their password typed again, with a
code when they have one): a passkey signs in on its own, so a stolen
session must not add one. The server verifies the attestation against the
challenge issued at start and stores the resulting public-key credential.

From here on, the user can sign in with the passkey. A
challenge/attestation that fails verification returns `403`; a duplicate
credential id returns `409`; hitting the per-user passkey cap returns
`409` (remove one first). Every other session opened before the passkey
ends; this one stays. Records `authentication.passkey_registered`.

403.description: No proof, a wrong one, a code needed (`step_up_required`), or an attestation that does not verify

409.description: Duplicate credential, or the passkey cap is reached

get.description:
Returns the caller's registered passkeys: name, authenticator type, when
each was enrolled and last used. This backs the passkey table in the
account security settings. Only the caller's own keys are visible; the
public-key material itself is never returned.

delete.description:
Deletes one of the caller's passkeys. The device can no longer be used to
sign in; password login is unaffected. Removal is written to the audit
log. A passkey belonging to another user is `404`, indistinguishable from
one that doesn't exist.

patch.description:
Changes the display name of one of the caller's passkeys. The name is
purely cosmetic: it exists so "MacBook Touch ID" and "YubiKey in the
drawer" stay tellable apart. A passkey belonging to another user is
`404`, indistinguishable from one that doesn't exist.

post.description:
Updates the signed-in user's password. Requires the **current** password
as proof, and a code from their authenticator (`mfa_code`) when they
have one: knowing a live session isn't enough, so a stolen token alone
can't lock the real owner out.

The new password must satisfy the tenant's password policy (length,
complexity, reuse history, common passwords). A tenant that blocks
breached passwords refuses one with `422`; one that only warns takes it
and says so in `password_breach`. Every other session the user holds
ends; the one the change was made from stays. Records
`authentication.password_changed`.

200.description: Changed, with what the breach lookup said

403.description: The current password is wrong, or a code is needed (`step_up_required`)

409.description: Changed too recently, or the new password was used recently

422.description: The new password breaks the tenant's rules

429.description: Too many requests or wrong codes

post.summary: Send the code a password reset asks for
post.description:
Public: the reset link's `token` proves access without a session.
For mailed or texted factors, replaces the current code and sends it to
the factor's destination; submit it as `mfa_code` at reset-confirm.
Unknown, expired or spent links, authenticator factors and absent factors
send nothing and return the same `204`. Asking again during the cooldown
returns `429`. Sending records `authentication.mfa_code_sent`.

429.description: A code went out moments ago, or too many requests

post.description:
Finishes the forgot-password flow. Present the token from the reset
email together with a new password. The token is single-use and expires
quickly: a used, expired, or forged token returns `404`.

The new password must meet the tenant's password policy. On success the
password is replaced and **all existing sessions are revoked**, so every
device has to sign in again with the new credentials.

If the account has an active second factor, `mfa_code` is required: the
response is `403` with a step-up-required code when it is absent, and a
plain `403` when it is wrong. A factor that mails or texts its codes is
sent one through the reset-code endpoint first. `password_breach` says
what the breach lookup found.

200.description: Reset, with what the breach lookup said

403.description: A code is needed (`step_up_required`), or the code is wrong

422.description: The new password breaks the tenant's rules

post.description:
Kicks off the forgot-password flow. If the email maps to a real account,
a time-limited, single-use reset link is sent to it.

The response is **always** `204`, whether or not the address exists: the
endpoint never reveals which emails are registered. Complete the flow at
the reset-confirm endpoint with the token from the email.

The tenant twin of the org plane's re-send, and the way out of the
`Expired` screen the reset-status endpoint produces. Submit the same
`token` from the dead link and another email goes out, superseding it.

Keyed on the token, not an address, so it reveals nothing about who has
an account. An expired or already-spent token is exactly what this
expects; it only has to name its user.

The response carries `retry_after_seconds`, the cooldown before another
is accepted. Asking again inside it returns `429` with the seconds still
to wait in the message.

Public, because the reader of a reset email is by definition signed out.

post.summary: Check a reset link without following it
post.description:
The tenant twin of the org plane's check. Submit the `token` and get back
`Valid`, `Expired`, `AlreadyUsed`, or `Invalid`, so the page a link lands
on can show the right thing before the reader types a password. Nothing
here spends the token.

`AlreadyUsed` means the password was changed on this link; `Expired`
means it was not, and another can be requested.

A `Valid` link also returns the tenant's `password_policy`, the rules the
reset will enforce, so the form can check a password before submitting
it. Other statuses carry no policy.

Public, because the reader of a reset email is by definition signed out.

The fallback for MFA when the authenticator device is lost or
unavailable. Satisfies a step-up challenge using one of the recovery
codes issued at enrollment instead of a TOTP code.

Recovery codes are **single-use**: redeeming one burns it, and the
remaining count drops by one. When they run low, the user should
re-enroll to generate a fresh set. An unknown or already-used code
returns `403`; too many attempts lock the account (`429`). Redeeming
against a session that's already MFA-verified returns `409`.

200.description: The new codes, shown this once

403.description: The proof does not prove the person, or a code is needed (`step_up_required`)

post.description:
A session the platform suspended, because its binding broke or its risk
rose, stops counting until its holder proves themselves again. Submit a
code from the authenticator, with the session's own bearer, to lift the
suspension. Records `authentication.session_resumed`, or
`authentication.mfa_failed` for a wrong code, which counts toward the
factor's lockout.

404.description: Not the caller's session, or no active second factor

422.description: Malformed code, or the session is not suspended

get.description:
Public (no session). What the tenant's sign-in page offers besides a
password: whether magic links and passkeys are switched on, and the
identity providers to show as "Sign in with ..." buttons (active
connections whose protocol is switched on, by name). Says nothing the
page does not need.

post.description:
When a sign-in answered `email_confirmation_required`, the person was
mailed a link. The page it opens posts the link's token here with the
refresh token the browser holds for that sign-in, so only the browser
that began the sign-in finishes it. Answers what the session still owes,
such as a factor to set up next.

Records `authentication.mfa_verified`. Public: the session is not
finished yet.

404.description: Unknown, used or someone else's link, or no live sign-in holds the token

post.summary: Start passkey registration for a waiting sign-in
post.description:
The passkey twin of `…/auth/mfa/enroll` for a sign-in that answered
`mfa_enrollment_required`: the person sets up a passkey as the second
factor the workspace requires, with the sign-in's own bearer. Returns the
challenge for `navigator.credentials.create()`.

401.description: The sign-in does not wait for a factor to be set up

post.summary: Confirm passkey registration for a waiting sign-in
post.description:
Finishes adding the passkey a waiting sign-in set up as its second
factor. Send the attestation without a `proof`: the sign-in itself is
the leave to add it, for a few minutes after it began. The new passkey
answers the factor the sign-in owed, so the session can be used straight
away. Records `authentication.passkey_registered`.

204.description: The passkey is added and the sign-in finished

401.description: The sign-in does not wait for a factor to be set up

409.description: Duplicate credential, or the passkey cap is reached

get.summary: Check whether a tenant takes sign-ups
get.description:
Tells a sign-in page whether to offer sign-up, and which rules a
password must meet. It answers as a sign-up would be answered, so the
form never offers what the submit refuses. Public: no session required.

200.description: Whether the tenant takes sign-ups, and its password rules

post.summary: Sign yourself up to a tenant
post.description:
Creates an account in a tenant whose administrators turned sign-up on,
and mails its address a verification link. The account cannot sign in
until its owner follows it. Answers `204` whether or not the address
already has an account, so the form cannot tell anyone who is
registered. Records `identity.user_registered` for a new account.
Public: no session required.

204.description: If the address is free, the account was created and a verification link sent

403.description: The tenant does not take sign-ups, or is at its user limit

422.description: Validation error, including a password that breaks the tenant's rules

post.description:
After the identity provider vouches for someone, their browser is sent
back to the dashboard with a one-time code, never a token. The dashboard
posts the code here with the `state` it sent when it started the
sign-in, and gets the session. A code swapped with any other `state` is
refused, so a code sent to someone else's browser signs nobody in.

A code works once, for a short while, and only while the session it
stands for is still live. `403` otherwise.

The session still owes a second factor when the identity provider
reported none and the person has one here, or the tenant requires one:
`mfa_required` and `mfa_enrollment_required` say which, as after a
password sign-in.

403.description: Code unknown, used or lapsed, or swapped by another dashboard

post.description:
Moves a tenant user to a linked account in the same organization without
password re-entry, for the tenant switcher.

Who switches comes from the caller's own session, never from the body:
their account names its linked identity by address, and the link must
lead back to that very account, both accounts must still hold the
group's verified address, and the target tenant must admit the sign-in
carried over. A sign-in that proved no second factor owes what a
sign-in to the target account would, shown by `mfa_required` and its
companions.

**Session status.** Opens an **`Active`** session for the linked account
in the target tenant. Records `organization.tenant_switched`.

Trades a valid `refresh_token` for a fresh one and extends the session.
Refresh tokens are **single-use**: each call rotates the token, so the
one you send is immediately invalidated and replaced by the one you get
back. Store the new token and discard the old.

**Token-theft detection.** If a token that was *already rotated away* is
ever replayed, the server treats it as a stolen token: it returns `403`
and **revokes every session that user has**, not just this one. An
unknown or expired token returns `404`; in either case, log in again.

**Session status.** Refreshing ends the old session and starts a new one
with a new token, which ends when the original sign-in does: refreshing
never makes a sign-in last longer. Records
`authentication.token_refreshed`.

403.description: A token already refreshed was replayed

get.description:
The longest the tenant lets its people ask for access, or 30 days when
it never set a limit. Anyone who may ask may read it, so a form can
offer only lengths that will be accepted.

put.description:
Holds the tenant's requests to at most `longest_seconds` from now on.
Requests already made keep the length they asked for. More than 30
days is `422`. Setting the limit already set records nothing; a change
records `authorization.access_request_policy_changed`.

Requires `Roles(Update)`.

get.description:
One page of the tenant's access requests, newest first: every one,
only those still `pending`, or only those one account asked
(`asked_by_kind` and `asked_by_id`). Anyone may list their own; listing
others' requires `Roles(View)`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `pending` keeps only those still waiting for an answer.

parameters.name: asked_by_kind
parameters.description: The kind of account that asked, with `asked_by_id`.

parameters.name: asked_by_id
parameters.description: The account that asked, with `asked_by_kind`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Asks, for the caller, for a role or a place in a group for
`length_seconds`, with a reason. The request is always for the person
asking, never someone named in the body. Asking gives nothing: the
access comes only once someone who could give it by hand approves, and
lasts `length_seconds` from then. A length past the tenant's limit is
`422`. A request nobody answers within a week runs out. Records
`authorization.access_requested`.

Any signed-in person of the tenant may ask.

Gives the asker the role or the place in the group until the length
asked for has passed, counted from now. Nobody approves their own
request, and only someone who could give the access by hand approves
it (`403` otherwise). A request that ran out, or an approval that would
break a separation-of-duties rule, is `409`. Records
`authorization.access_request_approved` and the role or membership
given.

Takes back a request still waiting for an answer. Only the person who
asked withdraws it (`403` otherwise). Records
`authorization.access_request_cancelled`.

422.description: Already answered, withdrawn or run out

post.description:
Refuses the request. The same people who could approve it may deny it;
nobody answers their own. Records `authorization.access_request_denied`.

get.description:
One page of the tenant's reviews, newest first: every one, or only the
`open` ones.

Requires `Roles(View)`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `open` keeps only those reviewers are still deciding.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Lists everyone who holds the role, or is in the group, now, and asks
the named reviewers whether each keeps it by `due`. A review with no
reviewer, more than 20, one named twice, or a due date already passed
is `422`; an unknown role, group or reviewer is `404`; a scope nobody
holds is `409`. Records `authorization.access_review_started`.

Requires `Roles(Assign)`.

get.description:
The review header with holder, pending and explicit removal counts.
Read its holders separately through the paginated `items` endpoint.
Its reviewers may read it; anyone else needs `Roles(View)`.

post.description:
Closes an open review without changing anyone's access. Records
`authorization.access_review_cancelled`.

Requires `Roles(Assign)`.

Closes the review and takes away the access of every holder it says
goes. Before the due date every holder must be decided (`409`
otherwise); after it, undecided holders are settled as the review's
`unanswered` says. Removals that would leave the tenant without an
administrator are `409`. A reviewer, or someone holding
`Roles(Assign)`, completes it. Records `authorization.access_review_completed` and each
removal.

Records the caller's choice, `keep` or `remove`, for one holder the
review lists. A later choice replaces an earlier one until the review
completes. Only the review's reviewers decide, and nobody decides on
their own account (`403`). A holder the review does not list is `404`;
a closed or overdue review is `409`. Records
`authorization.access_review_decided`.

get.description:
One page in immutable snapshot position order. The review's reviewers
may read it; anyone else needs `Roles(View)`. Unreadable reviews are `404`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Answers the tenant's app whether `subject` may do `action` on
`resource_type`, or on the one object keyed `object_key`. The answer
comes from the tenant's records: the app permissions the subject holds
through roles and groups, widened by the type's action ladder, and for
one object the relations held on it or on an object above it. Anything
the records do not show is `denied`, with the reason. Every answer is
recorded; one that cannot be recorded is not given.

Requires `Roles(View)`: an answer tells who holds what. An app calls it
with a tenant API key holding that right.

Answers up to 100 questions about one subject in one call, in the order
asked, each as `POST …/authorization/check` would. An empty batch, or
one over the limit, is `422`. Every answer is recorded.

Requires `Roles(View)`.

200.description: The answers, in the order asked

get.description:
The tenant's rules clearing holders of an app permission for
confidential or restricted data; none when nobody wrote one.

Requires the right to view classification rules.

post.description:
From now on, holding `permission` clears for data up to `up_to`. Only
`Confidential` and `Restricted` are cleared by a rule (`422` for a
lower level), and nobody clears others above their own clearance
(`403`). Records `authorization.clearance_rule_added`.

Requires the right to change how data is classified.

201.description: The rules with the new one

409.description: A rule already names the permission

put.description:
Changes the level holders of the `resource:action` permission are
cleared for. The caller must be cleared for both the level before and
the level after (`403`). Records `authorization.clearance_rule_changed`.

Requires the right to change how data is classified.

delete.description:
Holding the `resource:action` permission no longer clears for anything.
The caller must be cleared for what the rule cleared for (`403`).
Records `authorization.clearance_rule_removed`.

Requires the right to change how data is classified.

get.description:
One page of the tenant's recorded decisions, newest first: the access
checks its apps asked, and the requests its policy decided at the
gateway, each with what decided it (the answer's reason, or the policy
version and the rule that matched). Narrow by subject, verdict, policy
version, rule and time; every part given must hold.

Requires `AuditLog(View)`.

parameters.name: subject_kind
parameters.description: The kind of subject decided about, with `subject_id`.

parameters.name: subject_id
parameters.description: The subject decided about, with `subject_kind`.

parameters.name: verdict
parameters.description: `allowed`, `denied` or `challenged`.

parameters.name: policy_version
parameters.description: The number of the policy version that decided.

parameters.name: rule
parameters.description: The name of the policy rule that decided.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only decisions made at or after this time (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

get.description:
Paginated, sortable list of every group in the tenant. Use `?sort=`
(such as `name` or `-created_at`) and `after`/`limit`.

Requires `Roles(View)`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, updated_at, name.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Mints a group for organizing users and assigning roles in bulk.
`parent_id` optionally nests it under an existing group, whose roles it
then inherits; an unknown parent is `404`, and nesting under a group
conferring more than the caller holds is `403`. The name must be unique
within the tenant (`409`), and the tenant plan's group limit applies
(`403` when reached). Records `authorization.group_created`.

Requires `Roles(Create)`.

get.description:
Returns one group by id. `404` if the id does not exist in this tenant.

Requires `Roles(View)`.

delete.description:
Removes a group. **Refused while it has child groups** (`409`): delete
or move them first. Members and role bindings on the group itself do
not block deletion, but a deletion that would leave nobody to
administer the tenant is `403`. An unknown group is `404`. Records
`authorization.group_deleted`.

Requires `Roles(Delete)`.

patch.description:
Gives a group a new name, unique within the tenant (`409` on a
collision). A group a directory keeps in sync is renamed only by the
directory (`403`). Records `authorization.group_renamed`.

Requires `Roles(Update)`.

get.description:
Every principal that holds the group's roles through belonging to it,
each with its kind and, where it could be resolved, its name, a page at
a time with `after`/`limit`, oldest membership first. Machine
identities are listed beside the people: membership is a grant, and a
grant nobody can enumerate is one nobody can review or revoke.

Requires `Roles(View)`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.summary: Add a principal to a group
post.description:
Adds a principal as a member of a group, so the roles bound to the
group apply to it. The body names the kind as well as the id: a
consumer or an agent in a group holds the group's roles at the proxy
exactly as a person does. `until` ends the membership at that time;
left out, it lasts until the member is taken out.

An unknown id for the named kind is `404`; adding a principal that is
already a member, or one who would then hold both roles of a
separation-of-duties rule, is `409`. The caller must hold
everything the group and its ancestors confer, or the request is `403`.
Records `authorization.group_member_added`.

Requires `Roles(Assign)`.

delete.summary: Remove a principal from a group
delete.description:
Ends a principal's group membership, whatever kind of principal it is.
The permissions the membership conferred end at once, including at the
proxy. Removing a principal that is not a member is `404` (not
idempotent); a removal that would leave nobody to administer the tenant
is `403`. Records `authorization.group_member_removed`.

Requires `Roles(Assign)`.

put.summary: Move a group in the tree
put.description:
Puts a group under another one, whose roles it then inherits, or at the
top of the tree with `parent_id: null`. A move under the group itself or
one of its descendants is `422`; a move that hands its members more than
the caller holds, or that would leave nobody to administer the tenant,
is `403`. An unknown group or parent is `404`. Records
`authorization.group_moved`.

Requires `Roles(Update)`.

post.summary: Assign a role to a group
post.description:
Binds a role to a group so every member inherits it. Binding a role the
group already has is `409` (not idempotent); an unknown group or role
is `404`; a role carrying more than the caller holds is `403`. Records
`authorization.group_role_assigned`.

Requires `Roles(Assign)`.

delete.summary: Remove a role from a group
delete.description:
Unbinds a role from a group. Removing a role the group does not have is
`404` (not idempotent); a removal that would leave nobody to administer
the tenant is `403`. Records `authorization.group_role_unassigned`.

Requires `Roles(Assign)`.

get.description:
Returns the fixed catalogue of system permissions the identity provider
recognizes, grouped by area: the same set a role can carry. This is a
static list read from no store, for building a permission picker in the
role editor. Each entry's `value` is what create and update requests
take.

Requires a caller acting in the tenant.

The version an editor works on: the open draft when there is one,
otherwise the live version. The rules in the order they are checked,
what happens to a request none of them matched, where the version sits
in its lifecycle, and its number.

A tenant with neither answers `404`: start a draft with
`POST …/authorization/policy/draft` to open the editor. Read the two
apart with `GET …/policy/live` and `GET …/policy/draft`.

Requires `PolicySet(View)`.

404.description: The tenant has no policy yet

put.summary: Change what the draft does with an unmatched request
put.description:
**`default_action` is the posture.** `Deny` refuses anything no rule
allowed, which is the safe default for a zero-trust deployment. `Allow`
means only the rules refuse anything. A draft in review answers `409`.
Answers the whole draft. Records
`authorization.policy_default_action_changed`.

Requires `PolicySet(Update)`.
