200.description: The draft with its new fallback

get.description:
The draft open beside the live version, being written or in review.
`404` while none is open. Nothing a draft says decides a real request
until it is activated.

Requires `PolicySet(View)`.

post.description:
Opens a draft beside the live version, numbered one past the highest.
`{"from": "blank", "default_action": …}` starts empty with the given
fallback; `{"from": "next_version"}` copies the live version's rules and
fallback (`404` when nothing is live); `{"from": "restore", "version":
n}` brings a past version back as a new draft (`404` for a version the
tenant does not have). A draft already open, or a restore of the live
or open version, answers `409`. The live version keeps deciding
requests while the draft is written. Records
`authorization.policy_draft_started`.

Requires `PolicySet(Update)`.

get.description:
The version deciding real requests now. `404` while nothing is live:
the gateway then decides by each route's own policy alone.

Requires `PolicySet(View)`.

put.description:
Puts the open draft's rules in the order `names` gives, first checked
first. Every rule is named exactly once, or the request is `422`. A
draft in review answers `409`. Answers the whole draft. Records
`authorization.policy_rules_reordered`.

Requires `PolicySet(Update)`.

200.description: The draft in its new order

post.summary: Add a rule to the draft policy
post.description:
Adds one rule, switched on, to the open draft. Rules are checked lowest
`priority` first; a matching deny refuses the request wherever it sits,
otherwise the first matching allow lets it through. A condition that
cannot mean what it says is `422`; a name the draft already has is
`409`.

Only a draft being written is edited: one in review answers `409`.
Editing does not change what is enforced until the draft is activated.
Answers the whole draft. Records `authorization.policy_rule_added`.

Requires `PolicySet(Update)`.

put.summary: Change a rule of the draft policy
put.description:
Rewrites the rule named in the path: its name, conditions, action and
priority, as the body gives them. Whether it is switched on is kept.
`404` when no draft is open or it has no such rule; `409` when the draft
is in review or the new name is another rule's. Answers the whole
draft. Records `authorization.policy_rule_changed`.

Requires `PolicySet(Update)`.

200.description: The draft with the rule changed

delete.summary: Remove a rule from the draft policy
delete.description:
Takes the rule named out of the open draft. A draft in review answers
`409`. Answers the whole draft. Records
`authorization.policy_rule_removed`.

Requires `PolicySet(Update)`.

put.summary: Switch a draft rule on or off
put.description:
Takes a rule out of service, or puts it back, without losing how it was
written: a switched-off rule is kept but skipped. A draft in review
answers `409`. Answers the whole draft. Records
`authorization.policy_rule_switched`.

Requires `PolicySet(Update)`.

200.description: The draft with the rule switched

post.summary: Move a version of the policy through its lifecycle
post.description:
`submit_for_review` freezes the open draft while it is looked over.
`activate` puts the draft in review live, in place of the live version,
which becomes a past one. `reject` sends it back to draft.
`abandon_draft` drops the open draft without it ever going live.
`take_out_of_use` (also read from `archive`) takes the live version out
of service.

Activation requires a different approver when the tenant has one available.
Taking the live version out leaves only each route's policy deciding traffic
until another version is activated.

Invalid transitions give `409`; valid ones record `authorization.policy_*`.

Submitting needs `PolicySet(Update)`; activating, rejecting and taking
out of use need `PolicySet(Activate)`: writing a rule and putting it in
front of live traffic are different amounts of trust.

get.description:
Every version of the tenant's policy, newest first: the open draft, the
live version and the past ones, each with its rules and where it
started. Empty when the tenant never started one. Restore a past one
with `POST …/policy/draft` and `{"from": "restore", "version": n}`.

Requires `PolicySet(View)`.

get.summary: Get one version of the policy
get.description:
The version with this number, whatever its state, so two versions can
be read side by side. `404` when the tenant has no such version.

Requires `PolicySet(View)`.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version's number

get.description:
The roles a user, org user, agent or consumer holds now and where each
comes from: given straight (with its end, if it has one), or through a
group, with every group it is in. A principal the tenant does not know
holds nothing, and answers empty lists rather than `404`.

Requires `Roles(View)`.

One page of the tenant's relationships, newest first: every one, those
about one object (`object_type` and `object_key`), or those one subject
holds (`subject_kind` and `subject_id`).

Requires `Roles(View)`.

parameters.name: object_type
parameters.description: The object's resource type, with `object_key`.

parameters.name: object_key
parameters.description: The object's key in the tenant's app, with `object_type`.

parameters.name: subject_kind
parameters.description: The kind of subject holding a relation, with `subject_id`.

parameters.name: subject_id
parameters.description: The subject holding a relation, with `subject_kind`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Records a fact about one object of the tenant's app: that a person,
agent, app or group holds a relation on it (`{"holds": {"relation",
"subject"}}`), or that it sits under a parent object whose relations
reach it (`{"under": {"resource_type", "key"}}`). The relation must be
one of the actions the object's declared resource type accepts, and an
object cannot sit under itself (`422`). Writing a fact already written
answers it as it was, with no new record. Records
`authorization.relationship_added`.

Requires `Roles(Assign)`, and holding what the relation brings.

delete.description:
Takes the fact away; checks stop reading it at once. Records
`authorization.relationship_removed`.

Requires `Roles(Assign)`, and having been able to give what the relation
brings.

get.description:
Paginated, sortable list of every role in the tenant, default and
custom alike. Each role carries its system and custom permissions and
how many users hold it. Use `?sort=` (such as `name` or `-created_at`)
and `after`/`limit`.

Requires `Roles(View)`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, updated_at, name.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Creates a tenant role bundling **system** permissions (admin gates the identity provider
enforces, such as user and role management and audit; these follow an
`implies` ladder, so `ManageUsers` also covers `Users(View)`), and
**custom** permissions (the tenant's own `resource:action` pairs from its
permission catalogue, carried in tokens for its application to enforce).
Set `is_default` to give the role to every newly registered user.

**Delegation.** Only system permissions the caller already holds can be
granted: minting one they lack is `403`. A custom permission must name a
declared resource type and action (`422` otherwise). The name must be
unique within the tenant (`409`), and the tenant plan's role limit
applies (`403` when reached). Records `authorization.role_created`.

Requires `Roles(Create)`.

get.description:
Returns one role by id, with its system permissions, custom
permissions, whether it is a default role and how many users hold it.
`404` if the id does not exist in this tenant.

Requires `Roles(View)`.

delete.description:
Permanently removes a role from the tenant. Supply `replacement_role_id`
to move every current holder onto that role first; the delete then
succeeds. Without a replacement the delete is **refused while anyone
still holds it** (`409`), and so is deleting a role a group still
carries. A replacement equal to the role being deleted is `422`; an
unknown role or replacement is `404`; a deletion that would leave nobody
to administer the tenant is `403`. Records `authorization.role_deleted`,
and `authorization.role_reassigned` when holders were moved.

Requires `Roles(Delete)`.

patch.description:
Renames a role, replaces its system or custom permissions, or changes
whether new users are given it. Every field is optional; an omitted one
is left alone, and a permission list sent replaces the role's whole set.
A request that changes nothing records nothing.

**Delegation.** Granting system permissions the caller does not hold is
`403`, and so is narrowing a role so far that nobody would be left to
administer the tenant. A rename onto an existing name is `409`; an
unknown role is `404`. Records `authorization.role_renamed`,
`authorization.permission_granted`, `authorization.permission_revoked`
and `authorization.role_default_assignment_changed` for what changed.

Requires `Roles(Update)`.

post.summary: Assign a role to a user
post.description:
Gives a role to a user. `until` ends it at that time; left out, it is
held until it is taken away. Idempotent: giving a role the user already
holds is `204`, not an error, because the state asked for is already
true. An unknown user or role is `404`; a role the user may not hold
beside one they hold, under a separation-of-duties rule, is `409`.
Records `authorization.role_assigned`.

Requires `Users(Update)`: which roles a person holds is part of that
person's record. Holding it does not let a caller hand out authority
they lack: a role carrying permissions the caller does not hold is
refused with `403`.

delete.summary: Revoke a role from a user
delete.description:
Takes a role away from a user. Revoking a role the user does not hold
is `404` (not idempotent), and a revocation that would leave nobody to
administer the tenant is `403`. Records `authorization.role_revoked`.

Requires `Users(Update)`, the same right that gives one.

get.description:
A page of the role's holders, with `after`/`limit`: first everyone
given the role straight (people, agents and apps, each once, `via`
`direct`), then the groups carrying it (`via` `group`): their members,
and the members of the groups under them, hold it too. A holding whose
end has passed is not shown. `404` for a role the tenant does not have.

Requires `Roles(View)`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

get.description:
Every rule of the tenant, oldest first.

Requires `Roles(View)`.

post.description:
From now on nobody is given one of the two roles while holding the
other: straight, through a group, by an approved access request, or by
moving a group. `404` when either role does not exist; `422` when both
are one role. Records `authorization.separation_rule_added`.

Requires `Roles(Update)`.

delete.description:
The two roles may be held together again. Holdings given while the
rule stood are not touched. Records
`authorization.separation_rule_removed`.

Requires `Roles(Update)`.

post.description:
Evaluates supplied request, subject, time, location, device, risk, assurance
and `DPoP` facts without affecting live requests. Omitted facts stay unknown:
refusal rules can match them, allowance rules cannot, as at the gateway.

`version` picks what to run: `live` (the default) answers "what happens
now"; `draft` answers "what would happen if this went live", the
question to ask before approving it; a number runs that version.
`404` when there is no such version.

The result carries the final `action`, the `matched_rule` that decided
it (if any), the `evaluated_rules` trace, and the `policy_version` it
ran. Records `authorization.policy_simulated`.

Requires `PolicySet(View)`.

get.description:
Returns the logo, colors, raw custom CSS and email sender settings.
Unset fields are `null`, meaning platform defaults; a tenant with no
customization receives `200`. Sign-in hosts are set through domains.
Requires `Branding(View)` and changes nothing.

patch.description:
Absent fields stay unchanged, `null` restores defaults and values replace
them. An empty patch returns `204` without saving or recording an event.
Requires an HTTPS logo URL, `#RGB` or `#RRGGBB` colors, CSS that retains
renderable content after sanitization, a short sender name without control
characters and a valid sender address (`422` otherwise). An unverified
sender domain returns `403`. Requires `Branding(Update)` and records
one `branding.updated` per save, regardless of how many fields changed.

get.description:
Returns this tenant's **customized** emails: only the ones a tenant
admin has overridden. An email still on the platform's default is not
listed, so an empty page means "nothing customized yet". Sortable by
`template_type`, paginated with `after` / `limit`. Each entry carries
the `locale` it is written for (`null` for every locale without a
version of its own), `is_custom` and the overridden `subject`,
`body_html` and `body_text`, `null` for a part still on the default.
Read-only.

Requires `Branding(View)`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: template_type.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

put.description:
Replaces the customization of the stored `template_type`, optionally for
`?locale=de-DE`. Recipients use their locale, language, all-locales version,
then platform default, in that order. This `PUT` is idempotent; omitted
parts use platform defaults. Requires a short, control-free `subject` and
nonempty, bounded `body_html` and `body_text`. Bodies accept text and their
declared bare `{{ name }}` placeholders only; filters, tags and unknown
names return `422`. Requires `Branding(Update)`; records `branding.updated`.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description:
The recipients' locale, such as `de-DE`; the version for every
locale when omitted.

delete.summary: Reset an email template to the default
delete.description:
Returns a customized email to the platform's default by removing this
tenant's version of it: the one for `?locale=` when given, else the one
for every locale. The versions for other locales stay.

**State.** `Customized → Default`, the only way back. Returns `404` if
this version is not customized. Records `branding.updated`.

Requires `Branding(Update)`.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description:
The recipients' locale, such as `de-DE`; the version for every
locale when omitted.

post.description:
How one of the tenant's emails reads, filled with sample values and no
working link, exactly as the mailer renders it: its `subject`, `html`
and `text`. With no `draft` it shows the version the tenant keeps for
`?locale=` (or the platform's when it keeps none); with a `draft` it
shows a version not saved yet, checked as a saved one would be. Nothing
is saved or sent.

Requires `Branding(View)`, and `Branding(Update)` to preview a draft.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description:
The recipients' locale, such as `de-DE`; the version for every
locale when omitted.

post.description:
Mails one of the tenant's emails, the version the preview would show,
filled with sample values and no working link, to the caller's own
address, never one they type, through the provider the tenant's mail
goes out through now. An operator has no address to send to (`403`).
A provider that does not take the mail is `502`. Records nothing.

Requires `Branding(View)`, and `Branding(Update)` to send a draft.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description:
The recipients' locale, such as `de-DE`; the version for every
locale when omitted.

502.description: The mail provider did not take it

post.description:
Takes a logo as a `multipart/form-data` upload in its `logo` field and
shows it on the tenant's sign-in pages and in its mail, in place of any
logo before. The image is read from its own bytes, whatever the upload
says it is: a PNG or a JPEG of at most 512 KiB, each side between 16
and 4096 pixels (`422` otherwise). The platform keeps and serves it from
its own host; the answer and the branding's `logo_url` say where.
Records `branding.updated`, naming the logo and its format.

Requires `Branding(Update)`.

422.description: Not a logo the platform takes

get.description:
Which provider the tenant named for its mail (`kind`: `platform`,
`smtp`, `sendgrid`, `ses`, `postmark` or `mailgun`) with where it
points, how the last test send through it went (`check`), and which
provider the mail goes out through now (`delivers_through`): the one
named once a test send through it worked, the platform's until then.
A tenant that never named one reads `platform`. Credentials are never
shown. Read-only.

Requires `Branding(View)`.

put.description:
Selects `provider.kind`: SMTP (public host, port, `starttls` or
`implicit_tls`, username and password), SendGrid, SES, Postmark, Mailgun
or `platform`. Credentials are sealed and never returned. Mail uses the
platform until the selected provider passes a test send.
Requires `Branding(Update)` and fresh sign-in `proof`, because mail carries
sign-in and reset links. API keys and invalid proofs return `403`;
a missing second-factor code is requested. Records only provider kinds
in `branding.mail_provider_changed`.

post.description:
Sends one test mail through the provider the tenant named, to the
caller's own address, and keeps how it went: `delivered`, after which
the tenant's mail goes out through it, or `refused`, after which the
mail stays with the platform, so a mistyped key never stops anyone
getting their reset link. What the provider said is never shown. The
platform's own mail is not tested per tenant (`409`), and an operator
has no address to send to (`403`). Records
`branding.mail_provider_tested`.

Requires `Branding(Update)`.

409.description: The tenant sends through the platform's mail

put.description:
Decides what the tenant's users may give themselves in an emergency,
with nobody else approving: the built-in and custom permissions listed,
or nothing at all when both lists are empty, in which case every
emergency grant needs someone else's approval. A tenant starts letting
nothing.

Letting every user give themselves an access hands it to each of them,
and taking it away takes it from each of them, so the caller must hold
both what was let and what will be (`403` otherwise). Records
`authorization.break_glass_policy_changed`.

get.description:
Maps dot-notation fields to `Public`, `Internal`, `Confidential` or
`Restricted` sensitivity, in ascending order, and `Remove`, `Mask` or
`Hash` redaction. The proxy applies these at or above its configured threshold.
Before the first rule, returns empty `rules` and `null` `id`, not `404`.
Requires `Classification(View)` and changes nothing.

post.description:
Creates the set on its first rule. Each path has one rule until removed;
duplicates return `409`, so use `PUT` to change level or redaction in place.
Paths have at most 256 ASCII characters and 10 dot-separated segments,
each `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*`, without empty segments or edge dots.
Levels are `Public`, `Internal`, `Confidential`, `Restricted`; redactions
are `Remove`, `Mask`, `Hash`. Unsupported `Encrypt` and invalid fields
return `422`. Returns `201` with the rule's edit/delete `id`.
Requires `Classification(Update)`; records `proxy.classification_rule_added`.

409.description: The field path is already classified

put.description:
Sets a rule's sensitivity `level` and `redaction` strategy in place. The
rule keeps its `id` and its `field_path`, and the field is never sent
unredacted between the old rule and the new, as removing and adding
again would allow.

Returns `404` if no rule has this `id`. **Field validation** (`422`):
`level` is one of `Public`, `Internal`, `Confidential`, `Restricted`;
`redaction` is `Remove`, `Mask` or `Hash`. `Encrypt` parses but is
refused, because nothing behind it encrypts yet. Records
`proxy.classification_rule_changed` with the level and redaction before
and after. Requires `Classification(Update)`, as adding a rule does.

delete.description:
Deletes a single rule from this tenant's classification set by `id`.

**State.** The rule goes `present -> absent`; the rule set itself stays,
and the field it classified reaches callers unredacted. Returns `404` if
no rule has this `id`. To change a rule rather than drop it, `PUT` it.
Records `proxy.classification_rule_removed`. Requires
`Classification(Update)`.

get.description:
Where the tenant's data must stay (`data_residency`, `null` for
anywhere), how many days its audit records are kept, and whether
operators may act as its users. Read-only.

Requires `Compliance(View)`.

put.description:
Full replace: where the tenant's data must stay (`null` for anywhere),
how many days audit records are kept, and whether operators may act as
its users, plus `proof`, the caller's own sign-in typed again. A
retention outside the deployment's range, a residency the deployment
does not allow or the tenant's data is not placed in, or a closed
tenant, is `422`. A change made with an API key, or with a proof that
does not hold, is `403`; a proof missing the code of the caller's
second factor is `403` asking for a step-up. Records
`tenant.compliance_changed` with the posture before and after.

Requires `Compliance(Update)`.

get.description:
Returns this tenant's connectors: each one's scope, whether it is
`Active` or `Revoked`, and whether its agent has enrolled. Read-only.
Requires `Routing(View)`.

post.description:
Adds a private-network connector awaiting enrollment: an agent run
inside the tenant's network that the gateway reaches upstreams with no
public address through. Its `scope` names the networks and domains it
may be asked to dial; nothing else is dialled through it. Answers the
one-time `enrollment_code` the agent enrolls with, shown this once and
good for an hour; only its hash is kept. Checked against the plan's
connector limit. Records `routing.connector_created`. Requires
`Routing(Create)`.

201.description: Created, with the one-time enrollment code

403.description: Forbidden, or at the plan's connector limit

post.description:
Called by the agent inside the tenant's network, with no session or
key: it presents the one-time `code` an administrator was shown, and a
PEM signing request `csr` for the key it holds its link with. The
request's signature shows the agent holds that key; only the key is
taken from it. An unknown, spent, expired or revoked code is `403`
alike, and says no more. The code is spent, the key is pinned, and the
answer holds a certificate for that key signed by the platform's
connector authority, good for a day, with the authority's own
certificate to check the gateway's connector listener by. Limited per
client address. Records `routing.connector_enrolled`.

200.description: Enrolled, with the connector's first certificate

422.description: The signing request does not read, or its signature does not hold

429.description: Too many attempts from this address

get.description: Returns one connector by `id`. Read-only. Requires `Routing(View)`.

delete.description:
Removes a revoked connector. It is revoked first, so its tunnel is
closed before its record goes, and every service reached through it is
moved off first. Records `routing.connector_deleted`. Requires
`Routing(Delete)`.

409.description: A service is still reached through it

post.description:
Called by the agent with no session or key: it sends a new PEM signing
request `csr` for the key it enrolled with, which shows it still holds
that key. In the certificate's last eight hours, or once it ran out,
the answer is a certificate good for a day from now, and
`routing.connector_renewed` is recorded. Asked earlier, the answer is a
certificate ending when the one held now ends, and nothing is
recorded. A connector this tenant does not have, a revoked or
unenrolled one, and a request for any other key are `403` alike.
Limited per client address.

403.description: No such connector, revoked, not enrolled, or another key

422.description: The signing request does not read, or its signature does not hold

429.description: Too many attempts from this address

post.description:
Refuses the connector's tunnel for good: the gateway closes it, and
every service reached through it is unreachable until moved to another
connector. A connector whose certificate may have leaked is replaced,
never trusted again.

**State.** `Active -> Revoked`. Records `routing.connector_revoked`.
Requires `Routing(Update)`.

put.summary: Change what a connector may dial
put.description:
Replaces the connector's scope. A narrower scope leaving out a service
still reached through the connector is refused until the service moves,
so no service is cut off without a word. Records
`routing.connector_updated`. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

422.description: Revoked, or a service reached through it falls outside the new scope

get.description:
Returns this tenant's consumers, sortable and paginated. Each entry
carries the name, credential hint, clearance and lifecycle `status`
(`Active` or `Disabled`). Read-only. Requires the right to view
consumers.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, updated_at, name, status.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Registers an `Active` machine caller with a `name`, optional `description`,
`clearance` (default `Internal`), `credential_kind` (`api_key`, `client_cert`
or `jwt_bearer`), optional `expires_at` and request `quota`.
Returns its `id` and records `consumers.consumer_created`.

The platform generates `api_key` and returns it once, storing only its prefix
and keyed digest. Certificate and token consumers receive `api_key: null`.

Access starts empty and comes from role assignments, as for a person.

`422` for an invalid name or credential. `403` when the caller may not
create consumers, clears it for more than they may see themselves, names
the tenant's own token issuer, or the plan's consumer limit is reached.
Requires the right to create consumers.

get.description:
Returns a single consumer by `id`: name, description, credential hint,
clearance and lifecycle `status`. `404` if it does not exist under this
tenant. Read-only. Requires the right to view consumers.

delete.description:
Removes a consumer for good. It must be `Disabled` first: an active
consumer cannot be deleted, since that would cut live machine traffic
unannounced (`403`). Records `consumers.consumer_deleted`. `404` if the
consumer does not exist. Requires the right to delete consumers.

patch.description:
Gives the consumer a new display `name`. Its credential, clearance and
status stay as they were. Records `consumers.consumer_renamed` with both
names. `404` if the consumer does not exist, `422` for an invalid name.
Requires the right to update consumers.

put.description:
Sets the most sensitive data the consumer may receive and answers the
consumer as saved. Raising it lets the consumer subscribe to topics it
could not reach before, so nobody clears a consumer for more than they
may see themselves (`403`). A change records
`consumers.clearance_changed`; setting the clearance it already has
records nothing. `404` if the consumer does not exist. Requires the full
right over consumers.

Gives the consumer a new `description`, or clears it (`null`). A change
records `consumers.description_changed`; the description it already has
records nothing. `404` if the consumer does not exist, `422` for an
invalid description. Requires the right to update consumers.

post.description:
Disables an `Active` consumer: every request presenting its credential
is denied until it is enabled again. Use this to revoke a machine
identity for a while without deleting it. Records
`consumers.consumer_disabled`. `404` if the consumer does not exist,
`422` if it is already disabled. Requires the right to update consumers.

Enables a `Disabled` consumer again, so its credential is accepted.
Records `consumers.consumer_enabled`. `404` if the consumer does not
exist, `422` if it is already active. Requires the right to update
consumers.

Stops the credential the last rotation replaced from working now,
before its overlap runs out: every caller has moved over, or the old
credential leaked. Records `consumers.credential_overlap_ended`. `404`
if the consumer does not exist, `422` when no old credential is still
working. Requires the right to update consumers.

put.description:
Sets when the consumer's current credential stops working
(`expires_at`), or that it never does (`null`), and answers the consumer
as saved. Records `consumers.credential_expiry_changed`. `404` if the
consumer does not exist, `422` for an instant already passed. Requires
the right to update consumers.

Sets the consumer's own request allowance (`quota`: `requests` per
`minute`, `hour`, `day` or `month`), or removes it (`null`), and answers
the consumer as saved. The gateway counts the consumer's requests in the
current calendar period and refuses the ones past it with `429`; route
rate limits apply either way. Requests already counted in the current
period count against the new quota. A change records
`consumers.quota_changed`; the quota it already has records nothing.
`404` if the consumer does not exist, `422` for an allowance of zero or
above a billion. Requires the full right over consumers.

post.description:
Replaces the consumer's credential with a new one (`api_key`,
`client_cert` or `jwt_bearer`), working until `expires_at` or for good.
The old one stops working at once, or keeps working beside the new one
for `overlap_seconds` (at most seven days) so callers can move over; a
credential kept from an earlier rotation is dropped. Whoever sets the
credential can sign in as the consumer, so the caller must hold
everything the consumer holds (`403` otherwise). Records
`consumers.credential_rotated`. `404` if the consumer does not exist,
`422` for an invalid credential, an expiry already passed or an overlap
too long. Requires the right to update consumers.

A new API key is made by the platform and answered once as `api_key`;
only its prefix and a keyed digest are kept. Rotating to a certificate
or a token issuer answers `api_key: null`.

200.description: Rotated: the new API key, shown once

get.description:
Returns every signing key for this tenant with its `kid`, `algorithm`
(`RS256`, `ES256`, `EdDSA`), `status`, and timestamps. `active` keys
sign new tokens; `rotated` keys no longer sign but stay in JWKS through
the grace period so existing tokens keep verifying; `revoked` keys are
terminal and absent from JWKS. Returns `404` when the tenant has no key
set yet. Records nothing. Requires `Crypto(View)`.

post.description:
Mints a new key in the given `algorithm` and demotes the current active
key to `rotated`. The old key stays in JWKS for verification during the
grace period; the new key becomes the sole `active` signer. If the
tenant has no key set yet, this creates one. Returns the new key's
`key_id`. Rotation never revokes; use the revoke endpoint for that.

Records `crypto.key_rotated` (or `crypto.key_created` for a first key).
Requires `Crypto(Update)`.

Permanently revokes a key by `id` (its `kid`): it goes
`active | rotated -> revoked` (terminal) and is removed from JWKS, so
tokens it signed can no longer be verified by relying parties.

Returns `404` if no key set exists or the `kid` is unknown, `409` if the
key is already revoked, and `409` if it is the only active key: a tenant
must always keep a key that can sign. Records `crypto.key_revoked`.
Requires `Crypto(Update)`.

409.description: Already revoked, or the only active key

get.description:
Returns the tenant's current algorithm migration: source and target
algorithms, source and target key ids, `status`, and timestamps. There
is at most one active migration per tenant; `status` is one of
`planned`, `in_progress`, `validating`, `completed`, `rolled_back`,
`cancelled`. Returns `404` when no migration is active. Records nothing.
Requires `Crypto(View)`.

post.description:
Discards a migration before any keys are created. Once a migration has
started, use rollback instead; cancel refuses from `in_progress`.

`planned -> cancelled` (terminal). Returns `404` if no migration is
active, or `422` if it is not `planned`. Records
`crypto.migration_cancelled`. Requires `Crypto(Update)`.

Finalizes the migration: the source key is revoked if it is still
published, and the target key is the only active signer.

`validating -> completed` (terminal). Returns `404` if no migration is
active, or `422` if it is not `validating`. Records
`crypto.migration_completed`. Requires `Crypto(Update)`.

Schedules a migration from the active key's algorithm to the given
`target_algorithm`, starting in `planned` status. No keys are created
yet; that happens at `start`. Returns `404` if there is no key set or
active key, `409` if a migration is already active (one at a time per
tenant), and `422` if the target algorithm is the current one.

Records `crypto.migration_planned`. Requires `Crypto(Update)`.

409.description: A migration is already under way

post.summary: Promote the new key to primary
post.description:
Makes the migration's target key the sole signer and rotates the source
key out. Relying parties should refresh their JWKS cache.

`in_progress -> validating`. Returns `404` if no migration is active,
or `422` if it is not `in_progress`. Records
`crypto.migration_promoted`. Requires `Crypto(Update)`.

422.description: The migration is not in progress

post.description:
Aborts an active migration: the target key created during the migration
is revoked and the migration ends. A `reason` is required and is
recorded on the audit event.

`in_progress | validating -> rolled_back` (terminal). Returns `404` if
no migration is active, or `422` if it already ended. Records
`crypto.migration_rolled_back`. Requires `Crypto(Update)`.

422.description: The migration already ended, or no reason

post.description:
Generates the target-algorithm key and adds it to the key set: both
keys now sign (dual-signing), while the old key remains the primary
signer. Returns the new key's `key_id`.

`planned -> in_progress`. Returns `404` if no migration is active, or
`422` if it is not `planned`. Records `crypto.migration_started`.
Requires `Crypto(Update)`.

post.summary: Take over a domain another tenant offered
post.description:
The second step of a handover: this tenant takes the `domain` that
`source_tenant_id` offered it, keeping its verification and certificate.
The zone of a delegated domain moves with it, and the name keeps
answering across the move. Records `tenant.domain_transferred`.

Returns `404` if either tenant, the offer or the domain does not exist;
`403` if the offer was made to another tenant or the plan's domain limit
is reached; `409` if the offer was accepted already or ran out, the
tenants belong to different organizations, or the domain became the
giving tenant's primary domain; `422` if either tenant is closed.

Requires `Domains(Update)` on the tenant taking the domain.

get.description:
Returns the domains this tenant has registered, paginated and sortable
(see the `sort` parameter for allowed fields). Each entry carries its
`connection`, DNS `verification_status`, `tls_status`, the challenge
record to publish, `verified_at`, and the records that bring its
traffic here. Read-only.

Requires `Domains(View)`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, domain, verification_status, verified_at.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Defaults to `SelfManaged`: the tenant keeps DNS and receives TXT proof
(`dns_record_name` / `dns_record_value`) and `traffic_records.subdomain`
or `.bare_domain`. Publish these, then verify; traffic follows the records.
`Delegated` hands over the hostname using registration-specific NS records
in `traffic_records.delegation`, with automatic DNS-01 certificate renewal.
Without deployment nameservers and an answer address, it uses `SelfManaged`.
Starts `Pending`, except under an operator-vouched parent or for a wildcard.
Wildcards must be under this tenant's verified, delegated domain and are
always delegated (`422` otherwise). Conflicting names, ancestors, descendants
or externally held zones return `409`; exhausted domain capacity returns
`403`; invalid names or unknown connections return `422`.
Requires `Domains(Create)`; records `tenant.domain_registered`.

get.description:
Returns one of this tenant's domains, in the shape the list answers,
with the `certificate` it serves: where it came from (`Acme` or
`Uploaded`), who renews it, its issuer and names when uploaded, and when
it was issued and runs out. `certificate` is `null` when the domain was
never given one or the tenant removed it. The private key is never
answered. `404` if the domain does not exist under this tenant.
Read-only.

Requires `Domains(View)`.

delete.description:
Deletes a domain registration, and the zone we held for it when it was
delegated. Returns `404` if the domain does not exist under this tenant.
Removing the domain frees it for another tenant to claim and stops it
being used for routing or email federation; when it was the tenant's
primary domain, the tenant lets go of it too. Records
`tenant.domain_removed`, and `tenant.primary_domain_changed` when it was
primary.

Requires `Domains(Delete)`.

put.summary: Upload or replace a domain's certificate
put.description:
Serves a certificate the tenant brings itself on a verified domain: the
chain, leaf first, and the leaf's private key, both PEM. It takes the
place of whatever serves the name now, issued through ACME or uploaded
before, and the replaced one is dropped so nothing renews over it. The
tenant renews an uploaded certificate by uploading another, and is
warned as it nears its end.

Answers what the certificate says about itself (issuer, names, validity)
and never the key, which is sealed when stored. `409` when the domain is
not `Verified`, or the certificate does not name it or is not valid now;
`422` when the chain or key cannot be read or do not belong together.
Records `tenant.domain_certificate_uploaded`, or
`tenant.domain_certificate_replaced` when one was serving already.

Requires `Domains(Update)`.

409.description: Domain not verified, or the certificate does not name it or is not valid now

422.description: Unreadable chain or key, or a key that is not the certificate's

delete.description:
Stops serving the certificate the tenant uploaded for the domain. The
name then serves none, and its `tls_status` reads `NoCertificate`, until
the tenant uploads another or asks for one through ACME
(`provision-tls`). A certificate issued through ACME is the platform's
to replace (`409`). `404` when the domain is missing or serves no
certificate. Records `tenant.domain_certificate_removed`.

Requires `Domains(Update)`.

404.description: No such domain, or it serves no certificate

409.description: The certificate serving was issued through ACME

get.summary: List a delegated domain's DNS records
get.description:
Returns every record set in the zone, ordered by name and then type. A
set is one name and one type with all its values, which is what DNS
resolves and what a resolver caches, so it is the unit both read and
written here.

Sets carrying `is_managed_by_ianua` are ours: the address routing the
hostname to the proxy, and the `_acme-challenge` names a certificate is
issued through. They are listed because hiding records that exist would
make the zone look wrong, but writing or removing them is refused.

Not paginated: a zone is bounded by the plan's record-set limit and is
read whole. Returns `409` if the domain is tenant-managed, its records
living at the tenant's own provider. Read-only.

Requires `Domains(View)`.

put.description:
Replaces every answer the zone gives for one name and type. `PUT`
because it is idempotent and total: a set sent with one value leaves
exactly one, whatever was there before.

Values are spelled as a zone file spells them: `203.0.113.10` for `A`,
`10 mail.acme.com` for `MX`, `10 5 443 sip.acme.com` for `SRV`,
`0 issue "letsencrypt.org"` for `CAA`. A `CNAME` takes exactly one
value; every other type may take several.

**Refused with `422`:** a name outside the zone; a `CNAME` at the zone
apex; a `CNAME` beside any other type on the same name, or any type
beside an existing `CNAME`; the address on the delegated hostname
itself, which routes traffic to the proxy; and any `_acme-challenge`
name, which is written during certificate issuance. A new set beyond
the plan's record-set limit is `403`, though a set that already exists
may always be corrected.

Returns `409` if the domain is tenant-managed. Records
`tenant.dns_record_set_changed`, carrying both the new values and the
ones replaced.

Requires `Domains(Update)`.

delete.description:
Stops the zone answering for one name and type. The set is named in the
body rather than the path, because a record name contains dots and may
be the zone apex, neither of which survives a path segment cleanly.

Removing a set that is not there returns `204` and records nothing: the
caller wanted the zone to stop answering, and it does not.

**Refused with `422`:** a name outside the zone; the address on the
delegated hostname; and any `_acme-challenge` name. Returns `409` if the
domain is tenant-managed. Records `tenant.dns_record_set_removed`,
carrying what the set used to answer.

Requires `Domains(Delete)`.

post.summary: Offer a domain to another tenant
post.description:
The first of two steps that move a domain registration to a different
tenant **of the same organization**: this tenant offers it, and the
target tenant takes it with `POST …/domain-handovers/accept`. Nothing
moves until then, and nothing is recorded: the domain stays this
tenant's. A new offer of the same domain replaces an earlier one.
Answers when the offer runs out (`expires_at`).

Returns `404` if the domain or either tenant does not exist; `409` if
the target is this tenant, belongs to a different organization, or the
domain is this tenant's primary domain; `422` if either tenant is
closed.

Requires `Domains(Update)` on the tenant the domain is leaving.

202.description: Certificate requested; issued in the background

409.description: Domain not verified, or certificate already active

post.description:
Checks the stored TXT challenge at `_ianua-verify.{domain}` for
`SelfManaged` connections, or delegation to our nameservers for `Delegated`.
A match sets `Verified` and `verified_at`, requests a certificate and
records `tenant.domain_verified`. Returns the resulting status.
Missing proof changes and records nothing: DNS may still be cached,
and background checks retry. Only health checks can move a verified
domain to `Failed`. Requires `Domains(Update)`; missing domains return `404`.

Deletes an `Archived` tenant at once, before its grace has run, for
abuse or a legal order, and says why on the record: `reason` is `abuse`
or `legal_order`, `note` what happened or which order it was. This
cannot be undone.

**State.** `Archived → Deleted` (terminal). Returns `404` if the tenant
does not exist, or `422` if it is not `Archived`. Records
`tenant.status_changed`, `tenant.deleted` and `tenant.deleted_early`.

Requires an operator.

get.description:
Every egress policy of the tenant: the service each is for, where it may
go and its data ceiling. Read-only. Requires `Routing(View)`.

post.summary: Give a service a way out
post.description:
The egress gateway lets the service, identified by its client
certificate, reach exactly these hosts and ports and nothing else. A
service with no policy reaches nothing. Wildcards are refused: over a
public suffix they would be the whole internet. Records
`routing.egress_policy_created`. Requires `Routing(Create)`.

403.description: Forbidden, or at the plan's limit

409.description: The service already has a policy

get.description: One egress policy by `id`. Read-only. Requires `Routing(View)`.

delete.summary: Take away a service's way out
delete.description:
The service reaches nothing from its next connection on. Records
`routing.egress_policy_deleted`. Requires `Routing(Delete)`.

patch.summary: Change where a service may go
patch.description:
Renames the policy, or replaces its destination list or data ceiling; an
omitted field is left as it is. Records `routing.egress_policy_updated`.
Requires `Routing(Update)`.

put.description:
Labels the tenant as the `production`, `staging` or `development`
stage of the product it serves. The label is shown with the tenant
(`environment`) and changes nothing else about it. A closed tenant is
refused (`422`), and so is a name that is no stage. Records
`tenant.environment_changed` with both labels.

Requires the right to change the tenant's settings.

get.description:
Returns this tenant's identity provider connections, optionally filtered
by `status` (`Active` / `Disabled`), sortable and paginated. Each entry
carries its `protocol` (`Saml` / `Oidc`), `status`, provisioning, allowed
domains, trust, group mapping and SAML settings. Records nothing.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by status (`Active` or `Disabled`). Omit to return all.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, provider_name, status.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Registers an `Active` external identity provider named `provider_name`, with `config`:

- `{"Saml": {...}}`: the `entity_id`, `sso_url`, `certificate` and
  `name_id_format`, with an optional `slo_url` for single logout, a
  `next_certificate` while the provider rolls its key over, and
  `sign_requests` to sign the sign-in requests sent to it;
- `{"SamlMetadata": {"url": ...}}` or `{"SamlMetadata": {"document": ...}}`:
  the same settings from publicly fetched or pasted metadata;
- `{"Oidc": {...}}`: the issuer, client id, client secret (in
  `encrypted_client_secret`, sealed before it is stored) and scopes.

`allowed_domains` are the email domains the provider may sign in; a
connection with none signs in nobody. Each must be tenant-verified. The plan's connection limit applies. Records
`federation.connection_created`. Returns the new connection's `id`.

403.description: Forbidden, or the plan's connection limit is reached

422.description: Validation error, or the provider's metadata cannot be read

get.description:
Returns a single connection by `id`, as the listing shows it. Returns
`404` if the connection does not exist under this tenant. Records
nothing.

delete.description:
Permanently removes a federation connection. Returns `404` if it does
not exist. Records `federation.connection_deleted`.

patch.description:
Partial update: send any of `provider_name`, `config`,
`allowed_domains`, `provisioning` (`{"enabled": bool,
"default_role_id": ...}`), `domain_hint` (`null` clears it),
`attribute_mapping` (claim to `display_name`, `locale` or `timezone`),
`email_trust` (`Unverified` / `Authoritative`) and `assurance_trust`
(`Untrusted` / `Trusted`); omit a field to leave it. A new `config` must
name the same provider. Anything that lets the provider speak for more
people or be believed more needs the full federation right.

No status change: use the activate and disable endpoints for that.
Records `federation.connection_updated`.

404.description: No such connection, or no such role

409.description: The config names another provider, the hint is not an allowed domain, or a domain is not verified

post.description:
Enables a `Disabled` connection again so people can sign in through it.
`Disabled -> Active`. Returns `404` if the connection does not exist,
or `422` if it is already `Active`. Records
`federation.connection_activated`.

post.summary: Roll a SAML connection over to its next certificate
post.description:
Once the provider signs with its new key, the `next_certificate` set in
the connection's configuration becomes its only one, and the old
certificate signs nobody in any more. Records
`federation.connection_updated`.

409.description: Not a SAML connection, or no next certificate is set

post.description:
Turns a connection off: nobody signs in through it until it is enabled
again. `Active -> Disabled`. Returns `404` if the connection does not
exist, or `422` if it is already `Disabled`. Records
`federation.connection_disabled`.

put.description:
Makes the SAML connection refuse readable assertions and take only ones
its provider encrypted to this platform, so the browser they pass
through cannot read them. The key pair is made here (an empty body `{}`)
or brought by the tenant (`certificate` and `private_key`, PEM); the
private key is only ever stored sealed and never shown. Returns the certificate to give the
provider; it replaces any key the connection held. Records
`federation.connection_updated`.

200.description: The certificate to give the provider

422.description: The certificate is not PEM, or the private key does not match it

delete.description:
Makes the SAML connection take readable assertions and drops its
decryption key. Assertions then pass through the browser readable, so
this needs the full federation right. Records
`federation.connection_updated`.

put.description:
Replaces the connection's group mapping: the `claim` the provider sends
its groups in, and one rule per provider group naming the role
(`{"role": "<id>"}`) or group (`{"group": "<id>"}`) it gives here. At
each sign-in a person gets what their groups map to, and loses what a
group they left gave. Every role and group mapped is checked as a grant
by the caller. Records `federation.connection_updated`.

403.description: Forbidden, or a mapped role or group carries a permission the caller may not hand out

404.description: No such connection, role or group

422.description: No rule, more than 200, one twice, or the top group mapped

delete.description:
Turns the mapping off, so the provider hands out no more roles or
groups; the update right is enough, as in an incident. What people were
given through it stays until their next sign-in takes it back. Records
`federation.connection_updated`.

delete.summary: Unlink my account from an identity provider
delete.description:
Takes the provider the connection reaches off the signed-in person's
own account, so it no longer signs them in; it only takes a way in
away. Returns `404` if the connection does not exist or their account
is not linked through it. Records `federation.account_unlinked`.
Requires a tenant user's own session.

404.description: The account is not linked through this connection

post.summary: Confirm my link to an identity provider again
post.description:
After a provider's signing key changed, a link waits for its holder to
confirm it before the provider signs them in again. The signed-in
person proves who they are once more, the way they sign in: their
`password` (with a `code` from their second factor when they have one),
a sign-in link mailed to them (`mailbox`), or a `passkey` answer. The
`proof` is `{"method": "password" | "mailbox" | "passkey", ...}`.

Returns `404` if their account is not linked through the connection.
Records `federation.link_reconfirmed`. Requires a tenant user's own
session.

403.description: What was typed again does not prove who they are, or a second factor is needed

404.description: The account is not linked through this connection

429.description: Locked after too many wrong codes

delete.summary: Unlink a user's account from an identity provider
delete.description:
An admin takes the provider the connection reaches off another user's
account, so it no longer signs them in. Refused (`403`) when the admin
may not change that account's sign-in. Returns `404` if the connection
or the user does not exist, or the user is not linked through it.
Records `federation.account_unlinked`, so the person can be told.

404.description: No such user, or not linked through this connection

get.description:
Public (no session). The "Sign in with ..." button links here. Sends the
browser (`303`) to the connection's identity provider, OIDC or SAML, and
hands it a short-lived `ianua_sso` cookie: only the browser holding it
may finish the sign-in. `state` is a random value the dashboard keeps
and sends again with the one-time code, so only this dashboard can swap
it.

`404` if the connection doesn't exist; `403` if it is disabled or the
tenant does not accept its protocol.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description:
A random value of at least 32 characters the dashboard made and
keeps (in `sessionStorage`), sent again with the one-time code. The
code works only with it, so a code sent to someone else's browser is
of no use there.

403.description: The connection is off, or the tenant does not take its protocol

422.description: No state, or one too short

get.summary: SAML service provider metadata of a connection
get.description:
The document an administrator imports into their identity provider so
it knows this platform's entity id, where to post its answers and send
logouts for this connection, the certificate its sign-in requests are
signed with when the connection signs them, and the certificate to
encrypt assertions to when it takes only encrypted ones. It asks for the
persistent `NameID` format. Public: an identity provider fetches it
before any trust exists. Records nothing.

404.description: No such tenant or connection, or no signing key for signed requests

get.summary: SAML single logout with a provider, HTTP-Redirect binding
get.description:
Where a SAML connection's provider sends logouts, as the connection's
service provider metadata names. Its logout request sends the browser
on (`302`) to the dashboard's `.../federation/connections/{id}/saml/slo`
page with `binding=redirect` and the query as it arrived; the page posts
it to `.../saml/slo/answer` under the connection. Its answer to a
logout sent from here is taken at once, and the browser goes to the
dashboard's sign-in page with `logout=success`, `partial` or `failed`.
Public, limited per address.

parameters.name: SAMLRequest
parameters.description: The provider's logout request

parameters.name: SAMLResponse
parameters.description: The provider's answer to a logout request sent from here

parameters.name: RelayState
parameters.description: What the provider wants back

parameters.name: SigAlg
parameters.description: The signature algorithm

parameters.name: Signature
parameters.description: The signature over the query

302.description: On to the dashboard's logout page, or its sign-in page saying how the logout went

403.description: The workspace is not available, or the answer does not hold

409.description: Not a SAML connection, or the answer came too late

422.description: No message, or a malformed one

post.summary: SAML single logout with a provider, HTTP-POST binding
post.description:
As the redirect binding, for a provider that posts its logout request
or answer in a form. Public, limited per address.

302.description: On to the dashboard's logout page, or its sign-in page saying how the logout went

403.description: The workspace is not available, or the answer does not hold

409.description: Not a SAML connection, or the answer came too late

422.description: No message, or a malformed one

post.description:
The dashboard's `.../federation/connections/{id}/saml/slo` page posts
the provider's request as it received it, with the person's session
when the browser holds one. When the request names the subject and
provider session the session was opened with, the session ends and
`authentication.session_revoked` is recorded. Either way the answer is
the signed logout response for the browser to post as `parameter` to
`destination`.

200.description: The answer, for the browser to post to the provider

403.description: The request is unsigned, signed by a certificate the connection does not take, or names another issuer

404.description: No such connection, or no signing key set

409.description: Not a SAML connection, or its provider has no logout endpoint

422.description: Not a logout request, or a malformed one

post.summary: Find where an address signs in
post.description:
The sign-in page asks with the address a person typed. When its domain
is the domain hint of an active connection, the answer names that
connection (`routed: true`), and the page sends the person to its
`.../connections/{id}/login`; otherwise `routed` is `false` and they sign
in here. Public, limited per address; the address travels in the body so
it stays out of logs. Records nothing.

get.description:
The identity providers linked to the signed-in person's own account,
oldest first: the connection, the id the provider knows them by, and
when the link was made and last confirmed. Requires a tenant user's own
session. Records nothing.

401.description: Unauthenticated, or not a tenant user's own session

get.description:
Public endpoint the identity provider sends the browser back to. Checks
the `state` and the browser's `ianua_sso` cookie, exchanges the `code`,
and opens a session. Always answers `303` to the dashboard: to its
`/sso?code=...` page with a one-time code on success, or to the sign-in
page with `?sso=failed` otherwise. The session's token never appears in
an address.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Authorization code from the provider.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The state this deployment sent, echoed by the provider.

post.description:
Public endpoint the identity provider posts its answer to, as a form with
`SAMLResponse` and `RelayState`. Accepts only an answer to a request sent
from here, brought back by the browser holding its `ianua_sso` cookie.
Answers `303` to the dashboard like the OIDC callback.

get.description:
Whether SCIM was ever set up (`configured`) and takes requests now
(`enabled`), when a directory last synced, the SCIM base path to give the
directory, and the settings once set up. Never the token. Records
nothing.

post.description:
Turns on the tenant's SCIM endpoint. The first time, it returns the
bearer token an identity provider or HR system uses to push users in:
the raw token is shown once, only its hash is stored, so store it
immediately. Switched on again later, the endpoint keeps the token it
had and `bearer_token` is `null`; rotate the token to get a new one.
Returns `422` if SCIM is already on. Records `federation.scim_enabled`.

delete.description:
Turns off the SCIM endpoint: incoming SCIM requests are refused. The
configuration and token hash are kept, so it can be switched on again.
Returns `404` if SCIM was never set up, or `422` if it is already off.
Records `federation.scim_disabled`.

post.description:
Issues a new SCIM bearer token and invalidates the old one at once. The
new token is shown once; store it right away and update the external
system. Returns `404` if SCIM was never set up. Records
`federation.scim_token_rotated`.

put.description:
Sets the role every SCIM-created user starts with, whether those users
are active at once, and whether a user the identity provider removes is
deactivated or deleted. An address SCIM sends is never verified: the
person confirms it by link. Records `federation.scim_settings_updated`.

404.description: SCIM is not set up, or the role does not exist

get.description:
The identity providers linked to another user's account, oldest first,
for an admin who may view users. Records nothing.

Returns one page of the tenant's agent flows, newest first, each with
where it stands, as reading the flow shows it: its `status`, the first
stage with a run still going (`current_stage`, from 0), and each run's
`status`, agent run, answer and error. Data above the caller's
clearance is withheld. A flow whose run was never kept is listed as laid
out, without `status` or `current_stage`. Read-only. Requires the right
to view workflows.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.summary: Make and start an agent flow
post.description:
Lays out `stages` of agent runs (the runs of each stage start together,
once every run of the stage before has answered, and are handed those
answers) and starts the flow at once, acting for the caller, with
`input` (an empty object when left out) of `exposure` (default
`internal`). Each run names its agent, model provider, goal, purpose,
tools, approval classes and step cap (`max_steps`, 10 when left out).
Answers the flow with every run pending. Records
`workflows.flow_created` and the run's start. A flow counts against the
plan's workflows, and making one needs the rights to create and to run
workflows.

`422` for a stage without runs, a run an agent step does not allow, or
too many steps.

403.description: Forbidden, or the plan's workflow limit is reached

422.description: The stages do not make a flow

get.description:
Returns one flow and where it stands: its `status` (`Running`,
`Completed`, `Failed` or `Canceled`; a run that ran out of time failed),
the first stage with a run still going (`current_stage`, from 0), and
each run's `status` (`Pending`, `Dispatched`, `Completed` or `Failed`),
agent run, answer and error. Data above the caller's clearance is
withheld: a withheld run shows only its status and how sensitive its
data is. Read-only. Requires the right to view workflows.

delete.description:
Deletes a flow whose run has ended, with that run (`409` while it is
still going). Records `workflows.flow_deleted`. Its maker may always
delete it; anyone else needs the right to delete workflows.

post.description:
Stops the flow's run and every agent run it leaves going, and answers
the flow as reading it would, its `status` now `Canceled`. A maker who
may not view workflows is answered the flow as laid out with its
`status` alone. `409` when it ran out of time, which leaves it timed
out; `422` when it already ended. Records the run's end. Its maker may
always stop it; anyone else needs full control of workflows.

get.description:
Returns the tenant's services, pipelines, routes, stream routes, egress
policies and consumers as one document, keyed by name and carrying no
ids, so it can be checked into a repository and applied to another
tenant. Nothing secret is written down: no client key, no API key or its
hash, only what tells a credential apart. Send `Accept:
application/yaml` for YAML, which is what a document meant to be read in
a pull request usually wants to be. A route whose service or pipeline has
gone missing, or a stream route naming a consumer that is gone, is left
out: it could not be recreated from the document. Read-only. Requires
`Routing(View)` and `Pipeline(View)`.

post.description:
Accepts JSON or, with `Content-Type: application/yaml`, YAML; answers in
whichever format `Accept` names.

Returns ordered create/update/delete/unchanged results for services, pipelines,
routes, consumers, stream routes and egress policies. Defaults to `plan: "dry_run"`
and non-deleting `mode: "merge"`; `mode: "replace"` matches the document exactly.

Refuses the whole document if a route's service or pipeline would be absent.
Writes and their audit record commit or roll back together.
Records `routing.gateway_config_imported` when it writes; a dry run, or a
document that changes nothing, records nothing. Requires `Routing(View)`
and `Pipeline(View)`, and the right for each change the plan holds.

200.description: What the import did, or would do

403.description: Forbidden, or a create would exceed the plan

409.description: A name or sign-in host is taken, or something to delete is in use

post.description:
Accepts JSON or, with `Content-Type: application/yaml`, YAML, which is how
most specs are written.

Answers with the gateway configuration the spec describes: one service
from its server URL, one route per path carrying that path's methods, and
the pipeline you name. It writes nothing and reads only the document you
supplied: review it, fill in what a spec cannot say, and post it to the
configuration endpoint like any other. Requires a session or key of the
tenant.

get.description:
Every place the tenant ships request records to, with what it ships and
whether it is `Active` or `Paused`. A credential is never shown, only
whether one is set. Read-only. Requires the right to view the tenant's
routing.

post.description:
Names a place the tenant's request records are shipped to: an HTTPS
collector, an object store bucket or a Datadog site, which records
(`all`, `denied_only` or a sample) and in which `format`. A bucket and
Datadog need a `credential`; it is sealed at once and never shown again.
The target starts `Active`.

`422` for an address that is not public HTTPS or a destination missing
the credential it needs, `409` for a name the tenant already uses.
Records `proxy.log_target_created`, without the credential. Requires the
right to change the tenant's routing.

403.description: Forbidden, or the plan's limit is reached

get.description:
One target by `id`, without its credential. `404` if the tenant has no
such target. Read-only. Requires the right to view the tenant's routing.

put.description:
Sets where, what and how the target ships, given whole, and optionally
its `name`. The `credential` left out keeps the one it has, `null`
removes it and a value replaces it, sealed at once. Whether it is
paused does not change. Answers the target as changed, without its
credential. Records `proxy.log_target_changed`. Requires the right to
change the tenant's routing.

delete.description:
Stops shipping to it and forgets it, sealed credential and all. Records
`proxy.log_target_deleted`. Requires the right to change the tenant's
routing.

post.description:
Stops sending records to the target until it is resumed; its settings
are kept. Records the gateway decides meanwhile are not sent later.
**State.** `Active -> Paused`. Records `proxy.log_target_paused`.
Requires the right to change the tenant's routing.

Sends records to the target again, from the next batch on. **State.**
`Paused -> Active`. Records `proxy.log_target_resumed`. Requires the
right to change the tenant's routing.

get.description:
Finds the requests the gateway decided for this tenant, newest first by
default, sortable by `occurred_at`, `status` or `duration_ms` and paged
by cursor (`after`, `limit` 20 by default, at most 100). Narrow by `decision`
(`allowed` or `refused`), by what refused (`gateway_check`, `stage_id`
or `stage_kind`, one of them), by the policy `rule` and by text in the
`reason`, by `route_id`, by who asked (`user_id`, `agent_id` or
`consumer_id`, one of them) and by time (`since`, `before`, RFC 3339).

Each record says who asked, what they asked for, what was decided with
the status returned, and for a refusal its reason, the check or stage
that made it and the named rule it was made under. A record never holds
a token or a credential. Read-only. Requires the right to read the
audit log: a record says who called what.

parameters.name: decision
parameters.description:
`allowed` or `refused`. A request that ended undecided counts as
refused: the gateway refuses it too.

parameters.name: gateway_check
parameters.description:
Only refusals by this gateway check, made before any stage ran:
`tenant`, `route`, `app_sign_in`, `body_limit`, `pipeline_off`,
`attack_mode` or `upstream`.

parameters.name: stage_id
parameters.description: Only refusals by this stage of a pipeline.

parameters.name: stage_kind
parameters.description: Only refusals by any stage of this kind, such as `geo_fence`.

parameters.name: rule
parameters.description: Only refusals under the tenant policy rule of this name.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Only refusals whose reason contains this text, ignoring case.

parameters.name: route_id
parameters.description: Only requests that matched this route.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description:
Only requests of this tenant user, directly or through an agent
acting for them.

parameters.name: agent_id
parameters.description: Only requests this agent made.

parameters.name: consumer_id
parameters.description: Only requests this consumer made.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
Only requests finished at or after this RFC 3339 timestamp. Named
`since` because `after` is the page cursor.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only requests finished before this RFC 3339 timestamp.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: occurred_at, status, duration_ms.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

get.summary: List the roles a member can be given in one tenant
get.description:
The names of the tenant's roles, in name order, for choosing what to
pass to `PUT .../users/{user_id}/tenants/{tenant_slug}`. Works from an
organization session in any tenant or in none, and needs the right to
manage tenant access rather than a right inside the tenant.

Returns `404` if the tenant is not in this organization.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

get.description:
Returns the permanent `platform_label` and consent in `readable_address`.
The historical `uuid_subdomain` key carries the random hostname, or an
empty string when platform addresses are off. `slug_subdomain` contains a
name only with readable consent on a nested deployment. Also returns
the `custom_domain` / `primary_domain` when one is primary, and the
`jwt_issuer` when the tenant set one of its own. Read-only.

Requires `TenantSettings(View)`.

post.description:
Links the account you are signed in to in this tenant with your other
accounts in the organization, so you can switch between them without
signing in again. A link lets someone signed in to one account become
another, so you prove both ends with your own sign-in: this request's
session for the account joining, and, to join an existing group, your
session in one of its accounts in `X-Linked-Session`. Without it a new
group starts with this account. Nobody links accounts on someone else's
behalf. Records `organization.identity_linked`.

parameters.name: X-Linked-Session
parameters.description: Bearer token of your session in an account already in the group; omit to start a new group

delete.summary: Take one of my accounts out of its group
delete.description:
The person signed in to one of the group's accounts takes the account in
`tenant_id` out of the group the `email` names. A group left with no
account goes. Returns `404` if no such link exists. Records
`organization.identity_unlinked`.

get.description:
`scope=mine` (the default) lists those naming the caller, as the admin
or as the person, so the person can approve, decline or end one.
`scope=all` lists every one in the tenant and needs full control of
users. Read-only.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `mine` (the default) or `all`.

403.description: Listing every one without full control of users

post.description:
Checks the admin may act through the impersonation now and says how:
every later request made as the person carries the admin's own bearer
and the `ianua-support-impersonation` header naming it. Each such
request is checked again and recorded as the admin's, done as the
person. Call this without the header. Requires the admin's own session.

200.description: The admin may act as the person now

401.description: Unauthenticated, or not a tenant user's own session

403.description: Not its admin, not active, its window is over, or the account may not sign in now

404.description: No such impersonation involving the caller

post.summary: Approve a request to act as me
post.description:
The person it names lets the admin act as them, from now until the
window ends. Records `identity.support_impersonation_started`. Requires
the person's own session.

204.description: Approved; the admin may act until the window ends

401.description: Unauthenticated, or not a tenant user's own session

403.description: It names someone else to act as

404.description: No such request involving the caller

409.description: It waited longer than a day

422.description: It no longer waits for an answer

post.summary: Decline a request to act as me
post.description:
The person it names turns the admin down. Records
`identity.support_impersonation_declined`. Requires the person's own
session.

401.description: Unauthenticated, or not a tenant user's own session

403.description: It names someone else to act as

404.description: No such request involving the caller

422.description: It no longer waits for an answer

post.description:
The admin, or the person they act as, ends it early. The admin's next
request through it is refused at once. Records
`identity.support_impersonation_ended`. Requires the admin's or the
person's own session.

204.description: Ended; the admin's next use of it is refused

401.description: Unauthenticated, or not a tenant user's own session

404.description: No such impersonation involving the caller

422.description: It was already declined or ended

post.summary: Log in as a tenant user
post.description:
Checks a tenant user's email and password; unknown org, tenant, email
and wrong password share `404`. Returns a session and bearer `refresh_token`.
`mfa_required`, `mfa_enrollment_required` and `email_confirmation_required`
restrict it to completing the indicated factor, enrollment or mailed link.
`password_change_required` instead returns no session: change the password
at `…/login/password-change` using its single-use token before `expires_at`.
Reasons are `set_by_admin` or `expired`; an admin-set password needs
`own_factor` proof with `code`, or `mailed_link` proof whose token is mailed
instead of returned. Neither available means `403`; send an invitation.
Under sign-in pressure, an untrusted `fingerprint_hash` needs a challenge
before hashing: `401 challenge_required` names `challenge`; retry with
`challenge_proof`. With no challenge available, only trusted devices or
single sign-on work. These answers reveal nothing about the address.
Busy password hashing returns `429` with `Retry-After`. Sessions start
`Active`, end permanently on revocation, or expire by age or idle time.
Both successful and failed sign-ins are recorded in the tenant's trail.

200.description: A session, or the new password the sign-in owes first (`password_change_required`)

401.description: The tenant's sign-in is under pressure and this device must pass a challenge first (`challenge_required`, naming it in `challenge`)

403.description: The tenant takes no sign-ins now, or a password an admin set cannot be changed here (no factor and no mail server): an admin must send an invitation

404.description: Invalid credentials (unknown org/tenant/email or wrong password)

429.description: Too many requests or failed attempts, or the server is busy checking passwords (with `Retry-After`)

post.summary: Set the new password a sign-in owes
post.description:
When a sign-in answered `password_change_required`, send its
`change_token`, or the token from the mailed link, here with the new
password, and a `code` from the person's own factor when `proof` was
`own_factor` (`403 step_up_required` without one). The password must
meet the tenant's rules and repeat none of the account's recent ones;
each one refused counts against the address's lockout, as a wrong
password does.
Once set, every earlier session of the account ends and the sign-in
finishes: the answer is a session, owing whatever second factor the
sign-in asks (`mfa_required`, `mfa_enrollment_required`). The token works
once, for a few minutes.

200.description: The new password is set and the sign-in finished

403.description: The tenant takes no passwords or no sign-ins now, a code from the person's factor is missing (`step_up_required`) or wrong, or nothing only the person holds can confirm the change

404.description: Unknown org or tenant, or an unknown, used or expired change token

422.description: The new password breaks the tenant's rules or was used recently

429.description: Too many requests or refused passwords (with `Retry-After`)

get.description:
The signed-in tenant user's own account: name, address, status,
preferences and profile. Needs no right to view users. Roles are not
filled in. Read-only. Requires a tenant user's own session.

401.description: Unauthenticated, or not a tenant user's own session

patch.description:
Sets the calling user's own `locale` and `timezone`. Each is applied
when present and left unchanged when omitted or `null`, and overrides
the tenant default. `422` for an unrecognized locale or timezone.
Records `identity.user_preferences_updated`. Requires a tenant user's own
session.

get.summary: List the agents offered to me
get.description:
Returns the agents waiting for the caller to accept or decline them,
