each with when its offer lapses. Lapsed offers are left out. Every
person may read their own.

get.summary: List the apps I may open
get.description:
The caller's start page: each active app whose fixed path a `GET` would
be let through by the gateway's own access decision for them now, or
let through once they prove more. What only a real request shows, such
as their country or device, counts as unknown. Opening an app is
decided again by the gateway. Needs a signed-in tenant session.

get.summary: List the delegation requests asked of me
get.description:
Returns what agents asked of the caller, newest first, answered or not,
so they can grant or refuse each. Every person may read their own.

Returns the delegations the caller granted to agents in this tenant, in
the shape an agent's list answers: the agents they act through, what
each may do, until when, and whether it was revoked. Every person may
read their own.

post.summary: Request a change of my email address
post.description:
Starts moving the calling user's own account to `new_email`. Asking needs
more than an open session: the person proves who they are again with
their `password` (or a sign-in `link` mailed to them just now), and a
`code` from their second factor when they have one, so whoever stole a
session cannot move the address to their own mailbox.

A link to confirm goes to the new address; the current one is warned,
with a link that stops the change. The account keeps its address until
the confirmation is followed at `.../users/email/confirm-change`.
Records `identity.email_change_requested`. Requires a tenant user's own
session.

403.description: What was typed again does not prove who you are

422.description: Validation error, or the address you already have

get.description:
The signed-in person's live sessions on every device, the one this
request came with marked `current`. Read-only. Requires a tenant user's
own session.

401.description: Unauthenticated, or not a tenant user's own session

post.description:
Ends every session the person holds except the one this request came
with. Records `authentication.session_revoked` for each. Requires a
tenant user's own session.

401.description: Unauthenticated, or not a tenant user's own session

delete.description:
Signs the person out on one device, such as a browser they left signed
in elsewhere. Records `authentication.session_revoked`. Requires a tenant
user's own session.

get.description:
The person's own sign-ins and failed attempts, newest first, as the
tenant's audit trail recorded them. Read-only. Requires a tenant user's
own session.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

401.description: Unauthenticated, or not a tenant user's own session

get.description:
Returns the tenant's memories by name, those waiting to be deleted
among them, never their texts. A memory step's form lists them.
Requires the right to view workflows.

post.description:
Makes an empty memory filled by the platform's own embedding server, or
by the embedding model of the tenant's provider `provider_id`. Its
embedding model is asked once for a vector, so the memory keeps the
length its vectors have. Records `workflows.memory_created`. Requires
the right to create workflows.

403.description: Forbidden, the plan's memory limit is reached, or the provider is not cleared for the memory's data

422.description: Validation error, no embedding server here, or a provider offering no embedding model

post.description:
Sets the memory to be deleted once `name` matches its name exactly.
Nothing is kept in or found in it from then on; it and every text it
kept are deleted for good at `deleted_after`, unless brought back first.
Records `workflows.memory_deletion_requested`. Requires the right to
delete workflows.

422.description: The name typed is not the memory's

get.description:
Returns up to 100 of the memory's texts, oldest first, each with how
sensitive it may be and when it was kept, never its vector; `next`
names where the following page starts, passed back as `from`. A memory
waiting to be deleted can still be read, so a copy can be kept before
it is gone. Requires the right to delete workflows.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The `next` of the page before; absent for the first page.

404.description: No such memory, or deleted for good

post.description:
Brings back a memory set to be deleted, with every text it kept, while
its waiting period lasts. Records `workflows.memory_restored`. Requires
the right to delete workflows.

404.description: No such memory, or deleted for good

get.description:
Every channel people opened in the tenant, open and closed, newest
first. `open` says whether it carries messages right now. Requires
`Agents(View)`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.summary: Open a channel between two agents
post.description:
Grants either one-way reads of `topics` in the sender's
`agents.<sender id>.…` area, or shared rights on one `resource` that
either agent may write. Agents exchange data only through these channels.
Sets the highest data sensitivity and a lifetime of one minute to 30 days.
Returns `422` for both or neither channel kinds, topics outside the
sender's area, or identical agents. Requires the sender's owner or
`Agents(Delegate)` because sharing output grants authority.
Records `messaging.channel_opened`.

post.summary: Close a channel between two agents
post.description:
The next read through the channel is refused. A closed channel stays on
record and cannot be reopened; open a new one instead. Records
`messaging.channel_closed`. Requires the person who opened it, the sending
agent's owner, or `Agents(Delegate)`.

get.description:
Returns every event schema the tenant registered, sortable (see the
`sort` parameter) and paginated. Each entry carries its `format`, its
`compatibility` mode and every version, oldest first, with its number,
definition and registration time. The registry is a typed contract for
services and code generation. Read-only. Requires the right to view
messaging.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, updated_at, name, schema_name.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Registers a versioned message schema (first version `1`) for typed
validation and code generation. `format` is `JsonSchema`, `Avro` or
`Protobuf`; `compatibility` says how later versions must relate to the
one before (`None`, `Backward`, `Forward` or `Full`). The creator is the
person calling. Returns the schema's `id`. Records
`messaging.schema_registered`.

`409` if the schema name is taken, `422` for an invalid name or a
definition malformed for its format. Requires the right to create in
messaging.

get.description:
Returns a single event schema by `id`, with its `format`,
`compatibility`, creator and every version, oldest first. The latest
version is the current definition; the history is kept for code
generation and consumer migrations. A schema never evolved still has its
version `1`. `404` if the tenant has no such schema. Read-only. Requires
the right to view messaging.

delete.description:
Removes a schema and every version it holds. Topics keep their own
definitions, so no topic stops it. Records `messaging.schema_deleted`.
`404` if the tenant has no such schema. Requires the right to delete in
messaging.

post.description:
Appends a new `definition` as the schema's next version (2, 3 and on)
and returns its number. The definition must be well formed for the
schema's format, and is checked against its `compatibility` mode: for
JSON Schema, `Backward` and `Full` refuse dropping a required field,
`Forward` and `Full` refuse adding one; `None` and the other formats
skip the check. A schema holds at most 1000 versions of at most 64 KB
each. Records `messaging.schema_evolved`.

`404` if the schema does not exist, `422` if the definition is
malformed, incompatible or too large, or the schema is full. Requires
the right to manage messaging.

get.description:
Returns the subscriptions of one topic (`topic_name`) or of one service
(`consumer_id`); naming neither is `422`, since the list is always about
one topic or one service, never the whole tenant. Sortable and
paginated. Each entry carries the `delivery_mode`, an optional
`consumer_group` and `filter`, and the lifecycle `status` (`Active` or
`Paused`). Read-only. Requires the right to view messaging.

parameters.name: topic_name
parameters.description: The subscriptions to this topic, by topic name.

parameters.name: consumer_id
parameters.description: The subscriptions of this service.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, topic_name, status.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

422.description: Neither a topic nor a service named

post.description:
Subscribes `consumer_id` to a topic using `Push` to a signed public-HTTPS
`push_endpoint`, or `Pull` with per-message acknowledgement.
`ack_deadline_seconds` (5..600, default 30) bounds acknowledgement waits before
redelivery; `max_deliveries` (1..100, default 5) bounds attempts before dead-lettering.
`consumer_group` shares messages among members; without one each subscriber gets all.
An optional `filter` matches message-type prefixes. Returns `id` and, for `Push`,
a one-time `signing_secret`. Records `messaging.subscription_created`.

`404` if the topic or the service does not exist, `409` if the service
is already subscribed, `422` when the topic is archived, a push
endpoint is missing or not public HTTPS, or a value is invalid. `403`
when the service is disabled, the topic carries data it is not cleared
for, or the plan's subscription limit is reached. Requires the right to
create in messaging.

delete.description:
Removes a service's subscription to a topic, with the bus consumer it
reads through and the messages waiting there, so that service stops
receiving the topic. Other subscriptions on the topic are untouched.
Subscribing again later starts fresh, with no memory of what was
delivered. Records `messaging.subscription_deleted`. `404` if it does
not exist. Requires the right to delete in messaging.

get.description:
Returns, oldest first and paginated, the messages the subscription set
aside once their deliveries ran out, each with its `id`, base64-encoded
`payload`, `headers`, how often it was `delivered` and when it was set
aside. They are the topic's messages, so this asks what pulling does:
the right to consume and clearance for the topic's class as it stands
now (`403` otherwise). Read-only.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Puts a dead letter back on this subscription alone, with a fresh count
of deliveries, and removes it from the dead letters; no other
subscription of the topic sees it twice. Records
`messaging.dead_letter_replayed`, since it hands the service a message
it once gave up on. `404` when the subscription holds no such dead
letter. Requires the right to consume in messaging.

404.description: No such subscription or dead letter

get.description:
Polls a `Pull` subscription for waiting messages and returns up to
`max_messages` of them (default `10`, at most `100`), each with its
base64-encoded `payload`, its `headers`, the `receipt` that settles it
and how often it was `delivered`. `Push` subscriptions deliver to the
service instead and are not read here.

Nothing is taken until it is acknowledged: hand each `receipt` to `ack`
once it is handled, or to `nack` to have it delivered again at once. A
message not acknowledged within the subscription's deadline comes round
again, and one whose deliveries ran out is set aside as a dead letter
instead of handed out.

Pulling hands out the service's messages, so it needs the right to
consume, not only to view. The topic's class is checked against the
caller's clearance on every pull (`403` when above it, or while the
subscription is paused). `404` if the subscription does not exist.

parameters.name: max_messages
parameters.description: Most messages to return (default 10, at most 100).

403.description: Forbidden, or the subscription is paused

post.description:
Hands back the `receipt` a pull gave out with a message, once the
service handled it: the message is taken and never delivered again.
`404` when the delivery no longer waits: already settled, past its
deadline (it comes round again), or never this subscription's. Nothing
is recorded: acknowledging is the message flow itself. Requires the
right to consume in messaging.

404.description: No such subscription, or the delivery no longer waits

post.description:
Hands back the `receipt` of a message the service could not handle.
The subscription's `max_deliveries` decides what becomes of it: the
answer's `fate` is `Redeliver` when it comes round again at once, or
`DeadLetter` when its deliveries ran out and it was set aside. `404`
when the delivery no longer waits. Nothing is recorded. Requires the
right to consume in messaging.

200.description: Refused; what became of the message

404.description: No such subscription, or the delivery no longer waits

post.description:
Pauses an `Active` subscription: its messages wait undelivered, and a
pull is refused until it resumes. Records `messaging.subscription_paused`.
`404` if it does not exist, `422` if it is already paused. Requires the
right to manage messaging.

Resumes a `Paused` subscription, so its messages are delivered again.
Records `messaging.subscription_resumed`. `404` if it does not exist,
`422` if it is already active. Requires the right to manage messaging.

post.summary: Rotate a push subscription's signing secret
post.description:
Gives a `Push` subscription a new signing secret. With no body, or no
`overlap_seconds`, the old one stops at once, as after a leak. With
`overlap_seconds` (at most seven days), the old one keeps signing beside
the new one until then: each push carries a signature per secret, so a
service still checking with the old one accepts it while it moves over.
A secret from an earlier rotation stops at once. Returns the new
`signing_secret`, shown this once. Records
`messaging.subscription_secret_rotated`. `409` for a `Pull`
subscription. Requires the right to manage messaging.

requestBody.description: How long the old secret keeps signing; send none to stop it at once

422.description: The overlap is not valid, or over seven days

get.description:
Returns every topic the tenant owns, sortable (see the `sort`
parameter) and paginated. Each entry carries the human-readable `name`,
the machine `topic_name` the publish and stream endpoints address it by,
the `retention` policy, an optional JSON `schema`, its `data_class` and
the lifecycle `status` (`Active`, `Paused` or `Archived`). Read-only.
Requires the right to view messaging.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, updated_at, name, topic_name, status.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Creates a named message channel of the tenant in `Active` status, which
services publish to and subscribe to. `topic_name` is the
machine-readable routing key (such as `orders.created`); `retention`
says how long messages are kept (`{"Duration": seconds}`,
`{"MessageCount": n}` or `"Unlimited"`, never zero); `data_class` is the
most sensitive data it may carry (`Internal` when left out). An optional
JSON `schema` documents the expected message shape. The creator is the
person calling. Returns the new topic's `id`. Records
`messaging.topic_created`.

`409` if the topic name is taken, `422` for an invalid name, topic name,
description, schema or retention. Requires the right to create in
messaging.

get.description:
Returns a single topic by `id`, with its `topic_name`, `retention`,
optional `schema`, `data_class`, lifecycle `status`, creator and
timestamps. The `status` says what the topic accepts: only an `Active`
topic takes messages and live streams. `404` if the tenant has no such
topic. Read-only. Requires the right to view messaging.

delete.description:
Removes a topic for good, with every subscription to it and the bus
consumers they read through. The topic must not be `Active`: pause or
archive it first (`409` while it is). Records `messaging.topic_deleted`.
`404` if it does not exist. Requires the right to delete in messaging.

post.description:
Archives an active or paused topic: it is read-only for good, takes no
new messages or subscriptions, and can then be deleted. Records
`messaging.topic_archived`. `404` if it does not exist, `422` if it is
already archived. Requires the right to delete in messaging.

put.description:
Raises the most sensitive data the topic may carry. A class only goes
up: one below the current class is refused (`403`). Subscribers cleared
below the new class stop hearing it, so
`messaging.topic_data_class_raised` records the class before and after.
`404` if the topic does not exist, `422` when it is archived. Requires
the right to manage messaging.

403.description: Forbidden, or below the current class

post.description:
Pauses an `Active` topic: it refuses new messages until it is resumed,
and its subscriptions are kept. Records `messaging.topic_paused`. `404`
if it does not exist, `422` unless it is active. Requires the right to
manage messaging.

Resumes a `Paused` topic, so it takes messages again. Records
`messaging.topic_resumed`. `404` if it does not exist, `422` unless it
is paused. Requires the right to manage messaging.

put.description:
Replaces how long the topic keeps messages (`{"Duration": seconds}`,
`{"MessageCount": n}` or `"Unlimited"`, never zero). A shorter policy
drops messages subscribers have not read, so
`messaging.topic_retention_changed` records the policy before and after.
`404` if the topic does not exist, `422` when it is archived or the
policy is invalid. Requires the right to manage messaging.

Replaces the JSON `schema` messages on the topic are checked against, or
clears it with `null`. Records `messaging.topic_schema_changed`, naming
the topic but not the schema. `404` if the topic does not exist, `422`
when it is archived or the schema is blank or too large. Requires the
right to manage messaging.

post.summary: Publish a message to a topic
post.description:
Publishes one message to the topic named by `topic_name` in the URL.
`payload` is base64-encoded (so any bytes travel over JSON) and decoded
before delivery; `headers` is an optional list of `{ key, value }` pairs
delivered with the message. The message fans out to every active
subscription (or is shared among the members of each consumer group) and
reaches every open live stream on the topic. Records
`messaging.message_published` with the payload's size, never the
payload.

`204` on success; the answer carries no message id. `404` if the topic
does not exist, `403` if it is not `Active` (paused or archived), `422`
for an invalid topic name, a payload that is not base64 or is larger
than the bus accepts, or a header the platform reserves. Requires the
right to publish in messaging.

403.description: Forbidden, or the topic is not active

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket and streams the messages published to the topic
named by `topic_name` in the URL as they arrive. On connect the server
sends a `{ "type": "connected", "subject" }` frame, then one JSON frame
per message. `Pull` subscriptions are the polling way to the same data.

A live stream hands over what pulling would, so it takes what pulling
takes: the right to consume, an `Active` topic (`403` otherwise) and
clearance for the topic's class. The app is asked again every little
while, and the stream closes on the first refusal: a raised class, a
paused topic or a session that stopped counting ends it. The stream also
ends after its lifetime, and the client connects again. `404` if the
topic does not exist.

101.description: WebSocket upgrade: the topic's messages as they are published

403.description: Forbidden, or the topic is not active

get.description:
Returns aggregate metrics for this tenant over an adjustable window
(`since`/`until`, RFC 3339; the last 30 days by default, 90 at most),
headed by what the dashboard shows of the tenant itself: its slug and
name, primary domain, contact address, timezone, locale, status and
when it was made. Read-only.

Requires `Metrics(View)` in this tenant: the overview is the tenant's
own dashboard, and its own users are who read it.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Window start (RFC 3339). Defaults to 30 days before `until`.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Window end (RFC 3339). Defaults to now.

get.description:
Requests, refusals, upstream failures and latency for each route that
served traffic in the `window`, busiest first. A route deleted since is
still listed, with a null name: its requests happened, and dropping them
would make the totals disagree with the overview. Requests that matched no
route are left out; they belong to the tenant, not to a route. Read-only.
Requires `Metrics(View)`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Window start (RFC 3339). Defaults to 30 days before `until`.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Window end (RFC 3339). Defaults to now.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Routes to return, busiest first. Defaults to 20; the use case clamps
it.

get.description:
Returns this tenant's model backends: kind, endpoint, model, clearance,
and whether a key is stored (never the key itself). Requires
`Agents(View)`.

post.description:
Registers where this tenant's agent reasoning comes from: a self-hosted
OpenAI-compatible endpoint (DeepSeek, Kimi or vLLM in your own
Kubernetes), OpenAI, or Anthropic, the most sensitive data runs may
send it (`clearance`), and what it charges (`pricing`), which runs'
spend is counted at. Paste an `api_key` to bring your own OpenAI or
Anthropic key, or leave it out for a keyless self-hosted endpoint. The
key is encrypted at rest and never returned. The person connecting it
may use it from then on. Records `agents.model_provider_connected`.
Requires `Agents(Manage)`.

delete.description:
Removes a model provider for good. It must be disabled first. Records
`agents.model_provider_deleted`. Requires `Agents(Delete)`.

patch.summary: Enable or disable a model provider
patch.description:
Sets a provider's status. A disabled provider is kept but can no longer
be chosen for new runs. Records `agents.model_provider_status_changed`.
Requires `Agents(Update)`.

put.description:
Sets the most sensitive data runs may send the provider (`Public`,
`Internal`, `Confidential` or `Restricted`); runs send it nothing above
it. Records `agents.model_provider_clearance_changed`, naming both
levels; clearing it for what it already has records nothing. Requires
`Agents(Manage)`.

put.summary: Set a model provider's embedding model
put.description:
Has the provider offer an `embedding_model` beside its chat model, such
as `text-embedding-3-small`, served at the same endpoint with the same
key, so the tenant's memories may be filled through it; `null` offers
none. A memory filled with another model stops taking texts. Records
`agents.model_provider_embeddings_changed`. Requires `Agents(Manage)`.

409.description: The provider offers that embedding model already

422.description: Validation error, or an Anthropic provider, whose API has no embeddings endpoint

put.summary: Change a model provider's model and price
put.description:
Points the provider at another `model`, at the `pricing` it charges, so
runs started from then on reason with it and their spend is counted at
its price. Leave `pricing` out when the price is unknown: a run held to
a spend limit then stops after its first model call. Records
`agents.model_provider_model_changed`, naming both models. Requires
`Agents(Manage)`.

409.description: The provider asks for that model at that price already

post.summary: Rotate a model provider's API key
post.description:
Replaces the key sent to the provider, for one that leaked or one the
backend retires. The new key is encrypted at rest and never returned;
the old one is no longer sent. Leave `api_key` out to remove the key of
a keyless self-hosted endpoint; OpenAI and Anthropic always take one
(`422`). Records `agents.model_provider_key_rotated`, without the key.
Requires `Agents(Manage)`.

409.description: The provider holds that key already

422.description: The provider always takes a key

post.description:
Sends a trivial completion to confirm the endpoint is reachable and
answering: the check to run before wiring agents to a freshly
self-hosted model. Returns the start of the model's reply, and keeps the
outcome as the provider's last test. Records
`agents.model_provider_tested`. Requires `Agents(Update)`.

get.summary: Get the tenant's mTLS trust anchor
get.description:
Returns the tenant's mTLS mode and trusted CA certificates. A tenant
that never configured this returns `Disabled` with an empty CA list.
Read-only. Requires `Mtls(View)`.

patch.summary: Replace the tenant's mTLS trust anchor
patch.description:
Full replace, not a partial update: send the complete `mode` and
`trusted_ca_certs` list, the `revocation_lists` to check client
certificates against (none to check no revocation), plus `proof`, the
caller's own sign-in typed again. Each certificate must be a well-formed
PEM X.509 certificate and each list a well-formed PEM `X509 CRL`
(`422` otherwise); lists with `mode` `Disabled` are `422` too. Once
lists are given, a client certificate is refused in the handshake when
revoked, when no list covers its issuer, or once a list is past its
next update, so replace them before they expire. A change made with an
API key, or with a proof that does not hold, is `403`. Records
`tenant.mtls_config_updated`.

Requires `Mtls(Update)`.

get.description:
Returns the calling user's notifications in the tenant's inbox. Sortable
and paginated; `unread_only=true` returns only unread ones. Only
notifications whose category the user may see are listed, so nobody
learns of an area they cannot reach. Same entry shape as the other
inboxes. Requires a tenant user's session or key.

parameters.name: unread_only
parameters.description: If true, only return unread notifications.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, severity, category.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

get.description:
The calling user's delivery channel for each category, as
`{ category, channel }` pairs. A channel is `InApp` (the inbox and live
dashboard only), `InAppAndEmail` (also emailed) or `Disabled` (not
delivered). A category the user never set is `InApp`. Only tenant users
have preferences. Requires a tenant user's session.

patch.description:
Sets the calling user's delivery channel for the categories listed, as
`{ category, channel }` entries; the other categories keep theirs.
Answers the whole set after the change. Records one
`notifications.preferences_updated` per entry in the tenant's trail.
Requires a tenant user's session.

post.description:
Marks every one of the calling user's notifications read, including
ones in categories they can no longer see, and says how many changed
(`marked`). Records `notifications.all_notifications_read` in the
tenant's trail. Requires a tenant user's session or key.

get.description:
How many of the calling user's notifications are unread, counting only
the categories they may see, so the badge matches the list. Requires a
tenant user's session or key.

post.description:
Marks one of the calling user's notifications read. `404` when the
notification is not in their inbox. Records
`notifications.notification_read` in the tenant's trail. Requires a
tenant user's session or key.

get.description:
Returns this tenant's API keys, sortable and paginated. Each entry
carries the display `name`, `created_at`, and `last_used_at` and
`last_used_ip` (both `null` for a key never used); the raw key is never
included, and revoked keys are deleted rather than listed. Records
nothing. Requires `ApiKeys(View)`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, name, expires_at, last_used_at.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Generates a new API key for this tenant under a display `name` with the
given `scopes`. The raw key is returned once; only its hash is stored,
so copy it immediately. With `expires_at` the key stops working at that
moment, signing in no one from then on, like a wrong key; without it the
key never ends. A key made with a key ends no later than that key.
Checked against the tenant plan's API key limit. Returns `422` for an
invalid name or an end that is not ahead of now. Records
`oauth.api_key_created`. Requires `ApiKeys(Create)`.

403.description: Forbidden, or the plan's key limit is reached

get.description:
Returns a single API key by `id`: its `name`, `created_at`, and when and
from which address it was last used (`last_used_at`, `last_used_ip`,
both `null` for a key never used), never the raw key. Returns `404` if the key does not exist under this tenant
(revoked keys are deleted). Records nothing. Requires `ApiKeys(View)`.

patch.description:
Partial update: send `name` and/or `scopes` to change just those; omit
either to leave it. This edits metadata only: it does not rotate the
key. Returns `404` if the key does not exist. Records
`oauth.api_key_updated`. Requires `ApiKeys(Update)`.

post.description:
Stops an API key signing in, at once, until it is resumed; nothing
about it is lost. `409` if it is paused already. Records
`oauth.api_key_paused`. Requires `ApiKeys(Revoke)`.

Lets a paused API key sign in again. `409` if it is not paused.
Records `oauth.api_key_resumed`. Requires `ApiKeys(Update)` and every
permission the key carries, since resuming gives that access back.

Permanently revokes an API key by deleting it, so it no longer
authenticates and no longer appears in the list. Returns `404` if the
key does not exist, including a second revoke of the same key. Records
`oauth.api_key_revoked`. Requires `ApiKeys(Revoke)`.

get.summary: Start the authorization code flow in a browser
get.description:
The OIDC-discovered authorization endpoint takes `response_type=code`, `client_id`,
`redirect_uri`, `scope`, `state`, an optional `nonce`, a PKCE
`code_challenge` with `code_challenge_method=S256`, and optionally
`prompt`, `max_age`, `acr_values`, `response_mode` (`query` or
`form_post`), `id_token_hint`, `login_hint` and `ui_locales`. A client
that pushed its request first sends only `client_id` and `request_uri`.

A valid request redirects (`302`) with its parameters to dashboard sign-in and consent, which posts to the
consent step on this path. When the client is unknown or the redirect
is not one it registered, the browser is answered `422` and nothing is
sent to the redirect. Any other fault goes back to the redirect with
`error` (`unsupported_response_type`, `invalid_request`,
`unauthorized_client`, `invalid_scope`), the client's `state`, and
`iss`. Public, limited per address. Records nothing.

parameters.name: response_type
parameters.description: What the client asks to be handed back; only `code`.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: The client asking, by the `client_id` it was issued.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Where the answer goes; one the client registered.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: The scopes asked for, separated by spaces.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The client's own value, handed back with the answer.

parameters.name: nonce
parameters.description: The OIDC nonce, which ties the ID token to this request.

parameters.name: code_challenge
parameters.description: The PKCE challenge made from the client's verifier.

parameters.name: code_challenge_method
parameters.description: How the challenge was made; only `S256`.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description:
How the person is prompted: `none`, `login`, `consent` or
`select_account`, separated by spaces.

parameters.name: max_age
parameters.description: The longest a sign-in may be old, in seconds.

parameters.name: acr_values
parameters.description:
The assurance asked for: `aal1`, `aal2` or `aal3`, separated by
spaces.

parameters.name: response_mode
parameters.description: How the answer is sent back: `query` (the default) or `form_post`.

parameters.name: id_token_hint
parameters.description: An ID token this tenant issued, naming whom the client expects.

parameters.name: login_hint
parameters.description: Who the client expects to sign in; shown on the sign-in page.

parameters.name: ui_locales
parameters.description: The languages the pages should speak, separated by spaces.

parameters.name: request_uri
parameters.description:
A request the client pushed first, instead of every parameter
above but `client_id`.

200.description: For `response_mode=form_post`, a page that posts the `error` to the client

302.description: To the dashboard's sign-in and consent page, or back to the client with an `error`

422.description: The client is unknown, the redirect is missing, malformed or not one it registered, or the `request_uri` is not usable

post.summary: The consent step of the authorization code flow
post.description:
The dashboard's sign-in and consent page posts the authorization request
the browser brought (every parameter as it came, or `client_id` and
`request_uri`) with the signed-in person's `consent`: `not_asked_yet`
to learn what to show, or `given` (the default) once they agreed.

The `outcome` is `issued` (with the `code`, `consent_granted`, and where
to send the browser: `redirect_to`, or a `form_post` for a client that
asked for one), `sign_in` (sign the person in again, or as someone else,
as `prompt`, `max_age`, `acr_values` or `id_token_hint` ask), `consent`
(ask about `scopes`), or `refused` (the `error`, sent to the client the
same way). Records `oauth.consent_granted` when the person agreed to
something new, then `oauth.authorization_code_issued`. Requires a tenant
user's own session.

200.description: What the step came to: a code, sign in first, ask for consent, or a refusal for the client

403.description: The redirect is not one the client registered

422.description: The request is malformed, or its `request_uri` expired or was used

get.description:
Returns this tenant's OAuth clients, optionally filtered by `status`
(`Active` / `Revoked`), sortable and paginated. Each entry carries what
the client is registered with; the client secret is never included.
Records nothing.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Filter by lifecycle status (`Active` or `Revoked`). Omit to return
clients of any status.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, name, status.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Creates an `Active` tenant OAuth2 client with a `name`, allowed `redirect_uris`
(HTTPS, native-app loopback or private-use scheme), `post_logout_redirect_uris`,
the `grant_types` it may use (`AuthorizationCode`, `ClientCredentials`,
`RefreshToken`, `DeviceCode`, `TokenExchange`), its `scopes`, and how it
proves itself (`token_endpoint_auth_method`: `client_secret_basic` by
default, `client_secret_post`, `private_key_jwt` with `jwks` or
`jwks_uri`, `tls_client_auth` with `tls_client_auth_subject_dn`, or
`none` for a public client). `settings` sets token lifetimes, the
consent page's links, first-party consent, JWT access tokens, sign-out
channels and token binding.

Generates `client_id` and, where used, `client_secret`, shown once and kept hashed.
Checked against the tenant plan's OAuth client
limit. Records `oauth.client_created`.

403.description: Forbidden, or the plan's client limit is reached

get.description:
Returns a single client by `id`, with everything it is registered with
but its secret. Returns `404` if the client does not exist under this
tenant. Records nothing.

patch.description:
Partial update: send `name`, `redirect_uris`,
`post_logout_redirect_uris`, `scopes` and any of `settings` to change
just those; omit any to leave it. The three page links, and the two
sign-out channels, are each replaced together when one of them is sent.
This does not change `status` (use revoke) or the secret (use
rotate-secret). Returns `404` if the client does not exist. Records
`oauth.client_updated`.

delete.summary: Withdraw my consent from an OAuth client
delete.description:
Withdraws every scope the signed-in person gave the client, and revokes
the access and refresh tokens it holds for them; its next authorization
request asks the person again. The `id` is the one "my apps" lists.
Returns `404` if the client does not exist or the person gave it no
consent. Records `oauth.consent_revoked`. Requires a tenant user's own
session.

404.description: No such client, or no consent given to it

post.description:
Permanently revokes a client so it can no longer obtain tokens, and the
access tokens it holds stop resolving at once.

`Active -> Revoked` (terminal: a revoked client cannot be reactivated;
register a new one). Returns `404` if the client does not exist.
Records `oauth.client_revoked`.

Replaces the client's secret with a new one, returned once. The old
secret keeps working for `overlap_seconds` (at most thirty days), so
the app's servers can move to the new one without an outage; `0` or
left out ends it at once. Records `oauth.client_secret_rotated`.

409.description: The client is revoked, or holds no secret

422.description: The overlap is longer than thirty days

post.description:
The signed-in person enters the `user_code` shown on the device to
approve the request, binding it to their account. The device's next
poll at the token endpoint collects its tokens. Returns `404` if the
`user_code` is unknown, or `422` if the request expired or was already
answered. Records `oauth.device_authorization_approved`. Requires a
tenant user's own session.

422.description: The request expired or was answered

post.description:
RFC 8628 3.1: the device endpoint the discovery document names. The
device's client proves itself as at the token endpoint (only its
`client_id` for a public client) and asks for a `scope`. Answers a
`device_code` (the device polls the token endpoint with it), a
`user_code`, the `verification_uri` the person visits to type it, the
same with the code filled in (`verification_uri_complete`), the polling
`interval` and `expires_in`. Records
`oauth.device_authorization_requested`.

The signed-in person refuses the request whose `user_code` the device
shows: they did not start the sign-in there, or no longer want it. The
device's next poll is answered `access_denied`. Returns `404` if the
`user_code` is unknown, or `422` if the request expired or was already
answered. Records `oauth.device_authorization_denied`. Requires a tenant
user's own session.

422.description: The request expired or was answered

post.summary: End the session an app asked to end
post.description:
The dashboard's sign-out page posts the app's request, with the
person's session as bearer if they hold one. When the app named them
with an `id_token_hint`, or they `confirmed`, the session ends: its
refresh tokens are revoked and the apps it signed in to are told
(`front_channel_logout_uris` to load in hidden frames; the back channel
is told by the worker). Otherwise the `outcome` is `confirm`, or
`not_signed_in` when no session is held here. `redirect_to` is the
app's registered address with its `state`, or none for the dashboard's
own signed-out page. Records `session.revoked` when the session ends.

200.description: What the sign-out came to, and where the person goes

403.description: The `id_token_hint` was issued to another app, or the session is another plane's

422.description: The `id_token_hint` was not signed by this tenant, or a parameter is malformed

get.description:
The tenant's initial access tokens, each with what it is for, the uses
it has left, when it expires and whether it was revoked; never the
token itself. Records nothing.

200.description: Every initial access token, without the tokens

post.description:
A token that lets apps register themselves as clients, `uses` times
(1 to 1000, one by default) for `expires_in_seconds` (at most thirty
days). The raw token is returned once; only its hash is kept. Hand it
to whoever sets the app up. Records `oauth.initial_access_token_issued`.

201.description: Issued; the token is shown once

422.description: No use or more than a thousand, or longer than thirty days

post.description:
No app registers with it any more; clients already registered with it
stay. Records `oauth.initial_access_token_revoked`.

RFC 7662: a resource server, proving itself as a confidential client
(a public client is refused), asks what an access token says about
itself. A token that works answers `active: true` with its `scope`,
`client_id`, `sub`, `aud`, `iss`, `exp`, `iat`, `token_type`, what it is
bound to (`cnf`) and who acts for its subject (`act`). Anything else
(unknown, expired, revoked, its client or person gone) answers only
`active: false`. Records nothing.

200.description: What the token says about itself

get.description:
The end session endpoint the OIDC discovery document names
(RP-Initiated Logout). An app sends the browser here with an optional
`id_token_hint`, `client_id`, `post_logout_redirect_uri` (one it
registered) and `state`. The browser is sent on to the dashboard's
sign-out page, carrying the request, which ends the session with
`POST .../oauth/end-session`. Records nothing.

parameters.name: id_token_hint
parameters.description: An ID token this tenant issued to the app, naming who signs out.

parameters.name: logout_hint
parameters.description: Who the app expects to sign out; shown on the page.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: The app asking, by the `client_id` it was issued.

parameters.name: post_logout_redirect_uri
parameters.description: Where to send the person afterwards; one the app registered.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The app's own value, handed back with the person.

parameters.name: ui_locales
parameters.description: The languages the pages should speak, separated by spaces.

302.description: To the dashboard's sign-out page, carrying the request

post.summary: Sign out through an app, by form
post.description:
The same as the `GET`, for an app that posts its sign-out request as a
form, as RP-Initiated Logout allows. Records nothing.

302.description: To the dashboard's sign-out page, carrying the request

get.description:
The apps the signed-in person gave consent to, each with its name, its
page links, the scopes they gave and when. Withdraw one with `DELETE
.../oauth/clients/{id}/consent`. Records nothing. Requires a tenant
user's own session.

post.description:
RFC 9126: the client sends its authorization request here first,
proving itself as at the token endpoint, so the parameters never pass
through the browser. The request is screened as the browser's would be.
Answers a `request_uri`, usable once, for sixty seconds, and only with
this client's `client_id`, to send the browser to the authorization
endpoint with. Records `oauth.authorization_request_pushed`.

201.description: Pushed; send the browser on with the `request_uri`

post.description:
RFC 7591: an app registers itself, sending an initial access token the
tenant handed out as `Authorization: Bearer` and its metadata in the
standard's names (`client_name`, `redirect_uris`, `grant_types`,
`scope`, `token_endpoint_auth_method`, `jwks`/`jwks_uri`, `logo_uri`,
sign-out channels, token binding). An app registering itself always
asks people for consent and may not use `client_credentials` or token
exchange. Answers its `client_id`, its `client_secret` when it proves
itself with one, and the `registration_access_token` and
`registration_client_uri` it manages its registration with; both
secrets are shown once. Spends one use of the initial access token.
Records `oauth.client_registered`.

201.description: Registered; the secret and registration access token are shown once

401.description: No initial access token, or one that is unknown, used up, expired or revoked

403.description: The plan's client limit is reached, or the app asks for what only an admin may give

get.description:
RFC 7592 2.1: an app that registered itself reads its registration,
sending its registration access token as `Authorization: Bearer`. The
secret is not shown again. A wrong token and an unknown client answer
the same `401`. Records nothing.

401.description: No registration access token, or not this client's

put.description:
RFC 7592 2.2: an app replaces its registration's metadata: its name,
redirects, sign-out addresses, scopes, page links, sign-out channels and
token binding. What the body leaves out is cleared. Its grants and how
it proves itself stay as registered. Records `oauth.client_updated`.

200.description: The registration as it is now

401.description: No registration access token, or not this client's

403.description: The app asks for what only an admin may give

delete.description:
RFC 7592 2.3: an app deletes its registration. It can no longer sign
anyone in or obtain tokens, and its registration access token stops
working. Records `oauth.client_revoked`.

401.description: No registration access token, or not this client's

post.description:
RFC 7009: a client revokes an access or refresh token it holds, usually
on sign-out; `token_type_hint` (`access_token` or `refresh_token`) says
where to look first. Revoking a refresh token ends its family. The
answer is `200` whether or not the token was found, was already
revoked, or belongs to another client, so it tells nothing about
tokens; only a client that does not prove itself is refused. Records
the revocation when a token was revoked.

Public; accepts form or JSON. Clients use registered Basic/body secrets,
`private_key_jwt` assertions, or only `client_id` for public clients.
`grant_type` selects:
- `authorization_code`: one-use PKCE-bound `code`, `redirect_uri`, `code_verifier`.
- `refresh_token`: rotates `refresh_token`, optionally narrows `scope`; reuse ends its family.
- `client_credentials`: the client acts as itself with optional `scope`.
- `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`: `device_code`; polling can answer
  `authorization_pending`, `slow_down`, `access_denied` or `expired_token`.
- `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`: access-token `subject_token`,
  `subject_token_type`, client-id `audience`, optional `actor_token` and `scope`.
One valid `DPoP` header binds tokens to its key; invalid, duplicate or required-but-missing
proofs give `invalid_dpop_proof`. Required TLS binding gives `invalid_request`: no certificate arrives.
Returns `access_token`, `token_type` (`Bearer`/`DPoP`), `expires_in`, `scope`, and grant-dependent
`refresh_token`/`id_token` (`openid`). RFC 6749 errors use `400`, or `401` plus challenge for `invalid_client`; grant events are recorded.

get.description:
OIDC Core 5.3: an app sends the access token it was handed as
`Authorization: Bearer` and learns about the person it acts for what
the token's scopes let out, as the ID token does: `sub` always,
`email` and `email_verified` with `email`, `name`, `locale` and
`zoneinfo` with `profile`, and `roles` with `roles`. Only a token with
`openid` acting for a person is answered. A `DPoP`-bound token comes as
`Authorization: DPoP` with a `DPoP` proof for this request naming it
(RFC 9449 7); presented any other way, or with a proof that does not
check out, it is refused `401`. Records nothing.

200.description: The claims the token's scopes let out

401.description: No access token, or one that does not work, with a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge

403.description: `insufficient_scope`: a token without `openid`, or one for a machine

post.description:
The same as the `GET`, for an app that posts: the token in the
`Authorization` header, or as `access_token` in a form body (RFC 6750
2.2). Records nothing.

200.description: The claims the token's scopes let out

401.description: No access token, or one that does not work, with a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge

403.description: `insufficient_scope`: a token without `openid`, or one for a machine

get.description:
Every pipeline the tenant holds, oldest first, each with how many routes
run it. The count is what tells you whether one can be deleted: a pipeline
still naming routes is refused, and knowing that before you ask is the
difference between a disabled button and an error. Read-only. Requires
`Pipeline(View)`.

post.description:
Provisions a request-processing pipeline with the mandatory stages
(`Identity`, `Policy`) in `Draft` status: the starting point you then
extend, activate, and point routes at. The returned `id` is what a route's
`pipeline_id` names.

A tenant holds as many as it likes. That is the point: editing a pipeline
means disabling it, and a disabled pipeline refuses every route running it,
so a change is shipped by building the replacement alongside and moving
routes across rather than editing in place.

Returns `409` if the tenant already has a pipeline by this name. Records
`proxy.pipeline_created`. Requires `Pipeline(Manage)`.

Returns a cryptographically random decoy credential value
(`sk-decoy-...`). It is **not** added to any stage: add it to a
`CanaryToken` stage's `tokens` list yourself, with
`PATCH .../stages/{id}` and the updated list. Records `proxy.canary_token_generated`, without the token. Requires
`Pipeline(Update)`.

Stores a tenant-authored WASM module (see "Ianua WASM Stage ABI v1") and
returns its content-addressed `module_ref` (`sha256:<hex>`). Uploading
does not create or change any stage: put the returned ref in a `Custom`
stage's `module_ref` yourself, with `PATCH .../stages/{id}`.

Returns `422` if `bytecode_base64` is not valid base64 or the decoded
module exceeds the platform's size limit. Records
`proxy.wasm_module_uploaded`. Requires `Pipeline(Update)`.

get.description:
Returns one pipeline: its lifecycle `status` (`Draft`, `Active` or
`Disabled`) and the ordered `stages` (kind, position, `enabled`,
`mandatory`). Returns `404` if the tenant has no such pipeline.
Read-only. Requires `Pipeline(View)`.

delete.description:
Refused with `409` while any route still names it. Dropping those routes,
or silently repointing them, would change what runs on live traffic without
anyone asking: move them first. Records `proxy.pipeline_deleted`.
Requires `Pipeline(Manage)`.

patch.description:
Gives the pipeline a new `name`, unique within the tenant. Routes name a
pipeline by id, so none of them changes; a gateway configuration document
names it by the new name from here on. Records `proxy.pipeline_renamed`.
Requires `Pipeline(Update)`.

post.description:
Puts the pipeline live so its stages are enforced on the traffic of every
route running it. Stages cannot be added or removed while it is active:
disable it first.

**State.** `Draft -> Active`, or `Disabled -> Active`. Returns `404` if the
pipeline does not exist, or `422` if it is already `Active`. Records
`proxy.pipeline_activated`. Requires `Pipeline(Update)`.

422.description: The pipeline is not in a state to activate

post.description:
Suspends enforcement: every route running the pipeline is refused (deny
by default), but its configuration is kept. Use this as an emergency kill
switch or to make stage changes.

**State.** `Active -> Disabled`. Returns `404` if the pipeline does not
exist, or `422` if it is not `Active`. Records `proxy.pipeline_disabled`.
Requires `Pipeline(Update)`.

Appends a processing stage of the given `kind` (for example `Waf`,
`RateLimit`, `Redact`, or `Custom` WASM) to the **end** of the pipeline.
Move it with `PUT .../stages/order`, which takes the whole sequence.

Appending keeps the stage after Identity, so filtering cannot run before
the caller is identified. Changing its position requires the complete
stage order.

New stages are added enabled and non-mandatory. Stages can only be added
while the pipeline is `Draft` or `Disabled`, so a newly added stage starts
enforcing the moment the pipeline is next activated; use
`.../stages/{id}/disable` right after adding if you want it present but
inactive. `Identity` and `Policy` cannot be added: every pipeline already
runs them.

Returns `404` if the pipeline does not exist, or `403` if it is `Active`
(immutable while live). Records `proxy.stage_added`. Requires
`Pipeline(Update)`.

403.description: Forbidden, or the pipeline is active

put.description:
Replaces the whole order in one request: send `stage_ids` in the sequence
the stages should run and the pipeline is rewritten to match. A
drag-and-drop is one call, whatever moved: send the list you ended up
with.

`stage_ids` must name every stage exactly once. A partial list is refused
with `422` rather than applied, because the stages it omits would collect
at the front of the pipeline: a security control moving without anyone
asking it to. Duplicates and unknown ids are refused the same way.
`Identity` always runs before `Policy`.

Positions are derived from the sequence, so no two stages can end up
sharing one. Reordering requires the pipeline to be `Draft` or `Disabled`;
an `Active` pipeline returns `403`. Records `proxy.pipeline_reordered`.
Requires `Pipeline(Update)`.

403.description: Forbidden, or the pipeline is active

422.description: The order does not name every stage exactly once

delete.description:
Deletes a stage by `id`. As with add, stages can only be removed while the
pipeline is `Draft` or `Disabled`, and the mandatory stages never.

Returns `404` if no pipeline or stage exists, or `403` if the pipeline is
`Active`. Records `proxy.stage_removed`. Requires `Pipeline(Update)`.

403.description: Forbidden, the stage is mandatory, or the pipeline is active

patch.description:
Gives a stage new settings in place: send its `kind` with the new
configuration, such as a rate limit's new budget or a canary stage's
updated `tokens`. The stage keeps its `id`, its place in the order and
whether it is enabled; its kind cannot change (remove it and add another
for that). `Identity` and `Policy` take no settings here.

Settings can only change while the pipeline is `Draft` or `Disabled`.
Returns `404` if no pipeline or stage exists, `403` if the stage is
mandatory or the pipeline is `Active`, or `422` if the settings are for
another kind of stage or would leave it unable to do its job. Records
`proxy.stage_reconfigured`, naming the stage and its kind but never its
settings. Requires `Pipeline(Update)`.

403.description: Forbidden, the stage is mandatory, or the pipeline is active

422.description: The settings are for another kind of stage, or invalid

post.description:
Turns a non-mandatory stage off in place: it stays in the pipeline at its
configured position but stops being enforced, without the
remove-then-re-add round trip a delete would need. Mandatory stages
(`Identity`, `Policy`) cannot be disabled. Stages can only be disabled
while the pipeline is `Draft` or `Disabled`.

Returns `404` if no pipeline or stage exists, or `403` if the stage is
mandatory or the pipeline is `Active`. Records `proxy.stage_disabled`.
Requires `Pipeline(Update)`.

403.description: Forbidden, the stage is mandatory, or the pipeline is active

post.description:
Turns a disabled, non-mandatory stage back on without
re-adding it (which would lose its configured position). Stages can only
be enabled while the pipeline is `Draft` or `Disabled`.

Returns `404` if no pipeline or stage exists, or `403` if the pipeline is
`Active`. Records `proxy.stage_enabled`. Requires `Pipeline(Update)`.

403.description: Forbidden, or the pipeline is active

post.description:
Lifts a suspension: a `Suspended` tenant returns to `Active` and
sign-ins resume. A tenant the platform holds comes back only through an
operator (`403` for a member).

**State.** `Suspended → Active`. Returns `404` if the tenant does not
exist, or `422` if it is not `Suspended`. Records
`tenant.status_changed`.

Requires a member who may change the organization's tenants, or an
operator.

put.summary: Grant a resource relation to a principal
put.description:
Records that `subject` holds `relation` on `resource` in the
relationship graph. The graph is where resource authority comes from:
delegation reads it to decide whether a caller may hand a resource
capability to an agent, so nothing can be delegated over a resource
until it is granted here.

Authority is passed on, never made up: a caller may grant only a
relation they hold themselves. `Agents(Manage)` is the root that can
seed a relation nobody holds yet. Granting one already held changes
nothing. Records `agents.resource_relation_granted`. Requires
`Agents(Delegate)`.

delete.summary: Revoke a resource relation from a principal
delete.description:
Removes the grant. Held to the same rule as granting: taking away a
relation you could not have given is still a change to authority you do
not hold. Removing a grant that does not exist succeeds. Records
`agents.resource_relation_revoked`. Requires `Agents(Delegate)`.

get.description:
Returns every resource type this tenant has declared, with each
action's ladder already walked: `grants` on an action lists everything
holding it confers, so a client never expands the ladder itself and
cannot disagree with the proxy about what a grant means. This is what a
role editor and a route's permission picker read.

Requires `Roles(View)`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, updated_at, key.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Adds a resource kind, such as `project`, with its actions and `data_class`
to the tenant's permission catalogue. Roles and routes select the same names;
each resource carries the class governing where its data may be sent.

**The ladder.** An action may confer others on the same resource, so
`admin` conferring `write` conferring `read` means granting admin grants
all three. The ladder must not loop, and may only name actions this
resource declares.

The key is unique within the tenant (`409` on collision) and cannot use
the reserved `idp` prefix; the tenant plan's resource-type limit applies
(`403` when reached). Records `authorization.resource_type_declared`.

Requires `Roles(Create)`.

delete.description:
Removes the declaration from the catalogue. Refused with `409` while
any role still grants a permission naming it: deleting under a live
grant would leave roles holding permissions nothing defines. Revoke
those permissions first. Records `authorization.resource_type_deleted`.

Requires `Roles(Delete)`.

patch.description:
Changes the display name, the description, the action ladder or the
data class. The ladder is replaced whole, not merged, and is checked the
same way it was on declaration: a loop or an action conferring something
undeclared is refused and the existing ladder is left alone. Narrowing
the ladder further than the caller could hand out is `403`.

The key cannot change: it is what every role and route already refers
to. Declare a new resource type and retire this one instead. Records
`authorization.resource_type_updated`.

Requires `Roles(Update)`.

post.description:
Brings an `Archived` tenant back to `Active` before it is deleted, and
ends its wait for deletion. A tenant the platform archived comes back
only through an operator (`403` for a member).

**State.** `Archived → Active`. Returns `404` if the tenant does not
exist, or `422` if it is not `Archived`. Records
`tenant.status_changed`.

Requires a member who may restore the organization's tenants, or an
operator.

get.description:
Returns this tenant's routes, optionally filtered by `status` (`Active`
or `Disabled`), sortable and paginated. Each entry carries the name, path
pattern, methods, service, policy, priority and lifecycle status.
Read-only. Requires `Routing(View)`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Filter by lifecycle status (`Active` or `Disabled`). Omit to return
routes of every status.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: priority, created_at, updated_at, name, status.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Defines a route that maps a `path_pattern` (and HTTP `methods`) to a
`service`, evaluated against an authorization `policy`, with a
`priority` (higher wins on overlap) and a `path_rewrite` saying what
path the upstream sees. Created in `Active` status. Checked against the
tenant plan's route limit before creation. Returns the new route's `id`.
Returns `422` for an invalid name, path pattern or host. Records
`routing.route_created`. Requires `Routing(Create)`.

403.description: Forbidden, or at the plan's route limit

404.description: No such tenant, service or pipeline

get.description:
Returns a single route by `id`. Returns `404` if it does not exist under
this tenant. Read-only. Requires `Routing(View)`.

delete.description:
Permanently removes a route. It must be `Disabled` first: an active route
cannot be deleted, since that would cut live traffic. Returns `404` if the
route does not exist. Records `routing.route_deleted`. Requires
`Routing(Delete)`.

patch.description:
Partial update: send `name`, `path_pattern`, `methods`, `service_id`,
`policy`, `priority`, `path_rewrite`, `hosts`, `pipeline_id` or the
declarations to change just those; omit any to leave it. This edits
configuration only; it does not change `status` (use activate and
disable). Returns `404` if the route does not exist, or `422` for an
invalid name or path. Records `routing.route_updated`. Requires
`Routing(Update)`.

404.description: No such route, service or pipeline

post.description:
Re-enables a `Disabled` route so it accepts traffic again.

**State.** `Disabled -> Active`. Returns `404` if the route does not
exist, or `422` if it is already `Active`. Records
`routing.route_activated`. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

post.summary: Start attack mode on a route
post.description:
Checks every request to the route harder for the minutes given, before
its pipeline: an address any tenant's decoys or recon scoring caught is
refused, and each address may send 60 requests a minute, refused with
`429` past that. It ends on its own; starting it again restarts the
time from now.

Records `routing.route_attack_mode_started`. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

delete.description:
Ends attack mode before its time; the route is checked as its pipeline
says from the next request on.

Returns `422` when the route is not in attack mode. Records
`routing.route_attack_mode_ended`. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

post.description:
Stops the tenant's workflows calling the route: from the next request
on, every Protected apps step's call to it is refused at the gateway.

**State.** `open -> closed`. Returns `404` if the route does not exist,
or `422` if it is closed already. Records
`routing.route_closed_to_workflows`. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

put.description:
Replaces the header and cookie conditions a request must all meet for
the route to match it. Two routes on one path can then send requests to
two backends by what they carry: a blue/green switch on a header, or a
canary pinned by a cookie. A value is matched exactly or by its start,
never by a pattern. An empty list matches every request. Records
`routing.route_updated`. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

422.description: More than 16 conditions, or one header or cookie named twice

post.description:
Takes a route out of service: it stops matching and returns `503` to
callers until re-enabled. Use this to drain traffic safely before
deleting.

**State.** `Active -> Disabled`. Returns `404` if the route does not
exist, or `422` if it is already `Disabled`. Records
`routing.route_disabled`. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

Lets the tenant's workflows call the route with a Protected apps step,
as the person each run acts for. The route's own policy still decides
every call, exactly as it would for that person signing in.

**State.** `closed -> open`. Returns `404` if the route does not exist,
or `422` if it is open already. Records
`routing.route_opened_to_workflows`. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

get.description: The tenant's SAML apps, newest first, paginated. Records nothing.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Adds an active app people sign in to with this tenant as their identity
provider: its `entity_id`, the `acs_urls` its assertions may be posted
to (the first is the default), an optional `logout_url` for single
logout, the `name_id_format` (`persistent`, `email_address` or
`transient`), the `attributes` it is sent and under which names, what is
signed (`assertion` or `assertion_and_response`), and optionally the
certificates its assertions are encrypted to and its requests must be
signed with. Checked against the plan's limit. Records
`federation.service_provider_created`.

403.description: Forbidden, or the plan's limit is reached

409.description: Another app has the entity id

get.description: One app with everything it is set up with. Records nothing.

delete.description:
Removes the app; sign-ins to it are no longer answered. Records
`federation.service_provider_deleted`.

patch.description:
Partial update: send any of the fields an app is added with; omit one
to leave it, and send `null` to clear `logout_url`,
`encryption_certificate` or `request_signing_certificate`. A change
that sends the app more of a person, sends it to more places or checks
it less needs the full federation right. Records
`federation.service_provider_updated` once.

post.description:
`Disabled -> Active`: sign-ins to it are answered again. Needs the full
federation right. Records `federation.service_provider_updated`.

`Active -> Disabled`: no more sign-ins to it are answered, which anyone
who may update connections may do in an incident. Records
`federation.service_provider_updated`.

post.summary: Sign in to a SAML app
post.description:
A sign-in started here, such as from an app tile: the signed SAML
response for the signed-in person, to the app's default address, for
the browser to post as `parameter` to `destination`. Requires a tenant
user's own session. Records `federation.saml_assertion_issued`.

200.description: The answer, for the browser to post to the app

401.description: No session of the person's own

404.description: No such app, or no signing key set

409.description: The app names people by address and the person's is not verified

get.description:
Serves the tenant's SAML identity provider metadata (XML) that service
providers fetch to configure trust: the entity id (this tenant's
issuer), the single sign-on and single logout endpoints, the `NameID`
formats offered, and a certificate over the tenant's signing key.
Public: no authentication. Returns `404` if the tenant has no signing
key set yet. Records nothing.

404.description: No such tenant, or no signing keys

get.summary: SAML single logout with an app, HTTP-Redirect binding
get.description:
Where the tenant's SAML apps send logouts, as the identity provider
metadata names. An app's logout request sends the browser on (`302`) to
the dashboard's `.../saml/slo` page with `binding=redirect` and the
query as it arrived; the page posts it to `.../saml/slo/answer` with the
person's session. An app's answer to a logout sent from here is taken
at once, and the browser goes to the dashboard's sign-in page with
`logout=success`, `partial` or `failed`, recording
`federation.logout_response_taken`. Public, limited per address.

parameters.name: SAMLRequest
parameters.description: An app's logout request

parameters.name: SAMLResponse
parameters.description: An app's answer to a logout request sent from here

parameters.name: RelayState
parameters.description: What the app wants back

parameters.name: SigAlg
parameters.description: The signature algorithm, when signed

parameters.name: Signature
parameters.description: The signature over the query, when signed

302.description: On to the dashboard's logout page, or its sign-in page saying how the logout went

403.description: The workspace is not available, or the answer is not one to a request sent from here

422.description: No message, or a malformed one

post.summary: SAML single logout with an app, HTTP-POST binding
post.description:
As the redirect binding, for an app that posts its logout request or
answer in a form (`SAMLRequest` or `SAMLResponse`, `RelayState`). A
request goes on to the dashboard with `binding=post`, the `message` and
the `relay_state`. Public, limited per address.

302.description: On to the dashboard's logout page, or its sign-in page saying how the logout went

403.description: The workspace is not available, or the answer is not one to a request sent from here

422.description: No message, or a malformed one

post.description:
The dashboard's `.../saml/slo` page posts the app's request as it
received it (`{"binding": "redirect", "query": ...}` or `{"binding":
"post", "message": ..., "relay_state": ...}`), with the person's session
when the browser holds one. When the request names the person as the
app knows them, their session ends and `authentication.session_revoked`
is recorded. Either way the answer is the signed logout response for
the browser to post as `parameter` to `destination`.

200.description: The answer, for the browser to post to the app

403.description: No app of the tenant sent it, or its signature does not hold

409.description: The app has no logout address

422.description: Not a logout request, or a malformed one

post.description:
Before the dashboard signs a person out, it asks here for the logout
requests owed to every peer their session reached: each SAML app it
signed in to, then the SAML provider it was opened through. The browser
posts each as `parameter` to `destination`; the answers come back to
the `.../saml/slo` addresses. Requires a tenant user's own session.
Records `federation.logout_request_sent` for each.

200.description: The logout requests, for the browser to post one by one

401.description: No session of the person's own

get.description:
Where an app sends a person's browser with its sign-in request, as the
tenant's identity provider metadata names. The request is held on the
server with when it arrived, and the browser is sent on (`302`) to the
dashboard's `.../saml/sso` page with `binding=redirect`, the query
exactly as it arrived (`query`) and the id it is held by (`request`).
The page signs the person in if needed and posts `request` to
`.../saml/sso/answer` within ten minutes. Public, limited per address.
Records nothing.

parameters.name: SAMLRequest
parameters.description: The app's sign-in request, deflated and base64-encoded

parameters.name: RelayState
parameters.description: What the app wants back with the answer

parameters.name: SigAlg
parameters.description: The signature algorithm, when the app signs

parameters.name: Signature
parameters.description: The signature over the query, when the app signs

302.description: On to the dashboard's sign-in page for the app

422.description: The query carries no request, or half a signature

post.description:
Where an app posts a person's browser with its sign-in request in a
form (`SAMLRequest`, `RelayState`). The request is held on the server
with when it arrived, and the browser is sent on (`302`) to the
dashboard's `.../saml/sso` page with `binding=post`, the `message`, the
`relay_state` and `request`, as for the redirect binding. Public,
limited per address. Records nothing.

302.description: On to the dashboard's sign-in page for the app

post.description:
The dashboard's `.../saml/sso` page, with the person signed in, posts
the id the app's request is held by, as it received it: `request`. The
request and when it arrived are read from the server, so an app that
asked for a fresh sign-in is answered only for a sign-in made after its
request arrived. A request is answered once. The answer is the signed
SAML response and where to post it: the page builds a form posting
`message` as `parameter` (with `RelayState` when there is one) to
`destination`. Requires a tenant user's own session. Records
`federation.saml_assertion_issued`.

200.description: The answer, for the browser to post to the app

401.description: No session of the person's own, or the app asked for a fresh sign-in

403.description: No app of the tenant sent it, the app is off, or its signature or address does not hold

409.description: The app names people by address and the person's is not verified

410.description: No request is held under that id: unknown, answered already, or more than ten minutes old

422.description: The body names no request id, the request is malformed, or asks for another NameID format

get.summary: Start a sign-in to a SAML app here
get.description:
A link that signs a person in to one of the tenant's apps without the
app asking first, such as an app tile. The browser is sent on (`302`) to
the dashboard's `.../saml/apps/{app_id}/sign-in` page, which signs the
person in if needed and asks `POST .../saml/apps/{app_id}/sign-in`.
Public, limited per address. Records nothing.

parameters.name: app_id
parameters.description: The SAML app to sign in to.

302.description: On to the dashboard's page signing the person in to the app

get.description:
Returns the tenant's sandboxes, archived ones among them, sortable and
paginated. Requires the right to view workflows.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: updated_at, name.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Makes a named sandbox for code in `python` or `javascript`, or with
`kind` `image` for the company's own container image, with no version
yet. Its kind and language never change. An image sandbox is made only
where the operator turned companies' images on. Records
`workflows.sandbox_created`. Requires the right to create workflows.

403.description: Forbidden, or the installation runs no company images for an image sandbox

get.description:
Returns the registries image sandboxes may take the company's own
images from, by host, each with how its images are pulled; a password
is never shown. Requires the right to view workflows.

post.description:
Puts `host` on the tenant's list, so image sandboxes may take the
company's own images from it, pulled as `username` with `password`, or
with no login when both are left out. The password is sealed before it
is kept. Records `workflows.image_registry_allowed`. Requires the right
to connect integration accounts.

403.description: Forbidden, or the installation runs no company images

422.description: Validation error: a host that is no DNS name, or a user without a password

delete.description:
Takes the registry off the tenant's list. Versions whose image it keeps
stay as they are but no longer run: their next run fails as not run
until the registry is allowed again. Records
`workflows.image_registry_removed`. Requires the right to connect
integration accounts.

get.description:
Returns the runtimes a new version may pick now, each with the exact
image a version saved now keeps. A runtime the operator retired is left
out; versions saved under it still run. Requires the right to view
workflows.

Returns the sandbox and one page of its versions, newest first, each
with its code, packages, limits and how far building its package
bundle got. Requires the right to view workflows.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Nothing new is saved or picked of it again. Records
