`workflows.sandbox_archived`. Requires the right to delete workflows.

Gives the person's `words` to the tenant's model provider, with the
names of the step's `inputs` (never their values) and the `packages`
the code may use, and answers code in the sandbox's language with what
it does. With `fix`, the model fixes code that failed when tried.
Nothing is saved, run or recorded: save the code as a version and try
it. Requires the right to change workflows.

502.description: The model gave no code to use

get.description:
Returns the trial with its input, and once it ran, what the code gave
back or why it failed. A trial is kept for a day after it ended.
Requires the right to view workflows.

404.description: No such trial of this sandbox, or it was cleared

post.description:
Saves `code`, `packages` and the limits as the sandbox's next version,
under the `runtime` picked and the exact image it is offered in now,
and has its packages fetched, checked against the fingerprints their
registry published and against the runtime, and kept as one bundle.
With `import` instead of `code`, the code is read from a file of a
GitHub or GitLab repository through an account the caller owns or may
manage, and the version keeps the exact commit its `ref` pointed to.
For an `image` sandbox, `image` alone names the company's image instead:
its registry must be on the tenant's list, and the version keeps the
digest the tag points to now, asked of the registry with its login; the
image is then scanned for known vulnerabilities, and one critical
finding fails the version. The version answers with `build.status`
`building`; read the sandbox for `ready` or `failed`. A sandbox keeps at
most 50 versions. Records `workflows.sandbox_version_saved`. Requires
the right to change workflows.

201.description: Saved; its package bundle is being built, or its image scanned

403.description: Forbidden, or the installation runs no company images

404.description: No such sandbox, or the account, repository or file to import from is not there for the caller

409.description: The sandbox is archived, keeps 50 versions already, or another version was saved meanwhile

422.description: Validation error: a runtime not offered or of another language, code, limits, both or neither of code and import, a package that is no exact version of a name its registry takes, or an image from a registry not on the tenant's list, one its registry refuses or one over 2 GiB

502.description: The service keeping the file to import, or the image's registry, refused or could not be reached

post.description:
Sends a copy of the version to `folder` on `branch` of `repository`,
through a GitHub or GitLab account the caller owns or may manage: its
code as `main.py` or `main.js`, and its pinned packages as
`requirements.txt` or `package.json`. The branch must exist. The
version saved here stays the one that runs. Records
`workflows.sandbox_version_pushed` with the commit it became. Requires
the right to change workflows.

404.description: No such sandbox, version or account of the caller's, or the repository or branch is not there for it

422.description: Validation error, or the account's integration keeps no code

502.description: The service refused or could not be reached

post.description:
Runs the built version on `input`, as a code step hands its code its
mapped fields, in a sandbox of its own on a worker. It answers at once
with `status` `running`; read the trial for `succeeded` with the
output, or `failed` with why. A version that names allowed hosts
reaches them as its runs do. Records `workflows.sandbox_trial_started`.
Requires the right to change workflows.

403.description: Forbidden, or the plan's trials running at once are reached

409.description: The sandbox is archived, or the version's bundle is not built

422.description: Validation error: input that is no data a workflow holds

get.description:
Returns this tenant's services, sortable and paginated. Read-only.
Requires `Routing(View)`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, updated_at, name.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Defines a backend that routes forward to: an `upstream` (a URL, or weighted
backends for a canary), and how its backends are probed. Checked against
the tenant plan's service limit. An upstream naming a private or loopback
address is refused: a service is an instruction for the proxy to connect
somewhere on the tenant's behalf. Records `routing.service_created`.
Requires `Routing(Create)`.

403.description: Forbidden, or at the plan's service limit

get.description:
Returns one service by `id`: its upstream, probe settings, sign-in and
lifecycle status. Read-only. Requires `Routing(View)`.

delete.description:
Permanently removes a service. Refused with `409` while any route still
forwards to it: move or delete those first. Records
`routing.service_deleted`. Requires `Routing(Delete)`.

patch.description:
Partial update: send `name`, `upstream` and/or `health_check` to change
just those. Every route pointing at this service forwards differently from
here on, which is the point of a service existing.

Returns `422` if the new upstream targets a private address, or if dropping
its pinned JWT audience would leave a route that requires authentication
accepting tokens minted for any of the tenant's clients. Records
`routing.service_updated`. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

put.description:
Replaces how people sign in on the service's hosts: its own app sign-in
(`app_sign_in`, `null` to turn it off), or another service's that it
accepts instead (`accepts_app_sign_in_of`, with the `delivery` by which
that sign-in reaches it). Each host must be a verified domain of the
tenant that a route of this service answers on, and no sign-in path may
be a route's own path there. Returns `409` if another service already
signs people in, or sets its own cookie, on one of the hosts. Records
`routing.app_sign_in_changed`. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

404.description: No such service, or no such service to accept

409.description: Another service already signs people in on one of the hosts

get.summary: Get a service's live backend health
get.description:
Returns how the service's backends are probed and what the gateway's
probes last saw: each backend `up` or `down`, and when. `state` is
`reported` with the backends, `unknown` when the service is probed but
no gateway reported in the last few probe intervals (never read that as
healthy), or `not_probed` when probing is off and every backend gets
traffic. Read-only. Requires `Routing(View)`.

put.description:
Replaces how the gateway opens TLS to the service's upstream: the CA
bundle its certificate must chain to (`ca_certificates`, the public
roots when omitted), the client certificate and key presented when the
upstream asks for one, and the server name sent as SNI. Verification is
never switched off. The private key is sealed before it is stored, is
never answered back and is in no audit record. Every backend must be
reached over `https://`. Records `routing.service_updated`. Requires
`Routing(Update)`.

422.description: Validation error, a wildcard server name, or a backend reached over plain http

delete.description:
Drops the service's own TLS settings: the gateway checks the upstream
against the public roots again, presents no client certificate and
sends the address's own host as SNI. The stored client key goes with
them. Records `routing.service_updated`. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

get.description:
Returns this tenant's ports, sortable and paginated. Read-only. Requires
`Routing(View)`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, updated_at, name, listen_port.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Forwards a TCP, TLS or UDP port after deciding access, within the plan's stream-route limit.

`mutual_tls` requires `tls_terminate`; passthrough hides the certificate,
and plain TCP/UDP carries none.

`access` selects policy-admitted holders, signed-in `tunnel` clients or named consumers.
Tunnel policy is checked on each connection and refuses errors. Public ports cannot
identify callers and accept only any-holder access. Unknown tenant consumers give `404`.

Returns `409` if the port is already claimed. A listening port belongs to
the deployment, not to a tenant, so another tenant may already hold it.
Records `routing.stream_route_created`. Requires `Routing(Create)`.

403.description: Forbidden, or at the plan's stream-route limit

get.description: Returns one port by `id`. Read-only. Requires `Routing(View)`.

delete.description:
Closes the port and releases it for any tenant to claim. Records
`routing.stream_route_deleted`. Requires `Routing(Delete)`.

patch.description:
Partial update of the name, server names, policy, access, backends or
timeouts. A new policy and access are judged together.
The protocol and the port are not changeable: either is a different socket
on a different listener, so create a new route and delete this one.

Returns `422` if a new policy asks for an identity the route's protocol
cannot carry, or a backend targets a private address. Records
`routing.stream_route_updated`. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

409.description: Another stream route has the name

post.description:
The port starts accepting again. Records
`routing.stream_route_activated`. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

post.summary: Close a stream route to workflows
post.description:
Stops the tenant's workflows reaching the stream route and forgets the
login kept for them: from the next connection on, every Protected data
step reaching it is refused at the gateway.

**State.** `open -> closed`. Returns `404` if the stream route does not
exist, or `422` if it is closed already. Records
`routing.stream_route_closed_to_workflows`. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

The port stops accepting. Established streams are left alone, and the port
stays reserved for this tenant, so taking one out of service briefly does
not risk losing it to somebody else. Records
`routing.stream_route_disabled`. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

post.summary: Open a stream route to workflows
post.description:
Lets the tenant's workflows reach the system behind the stream route
with a Protected data step, as the person each run acts for, signing in
with the login given here. The route's own access still decides every
connection, exactly as it would for that person through the signed-in
tunnel, so only a route that lets people in can be opened. What a step
may do once through is what the login may do, decided by the system
itself. The password is kept sealed for this route and never shown.

**State.** `closed -> open`. Returns `404` if the stream route does not
exist, or `422` if it is open already: close it first to change the
login. Records `routing.stream_route_opened_to_workflows`, naming the
login's user. Requires `Routing(Update)`.

422.description: Already open to workflows, a route that lets no people in, or an invalid login

get.description:
Returns this tenant's signal stream receivers, optionally only those in
one `status` (`Active`, `Paused` or `Disabled`), sortable and paginated.
Each entry carries the endpoint and whether it is verified, the delivery
method, the signal types and the lifecycle status. Read-only. Requires
the right to view signal streams.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Only streams in this status: `Active`, `Paused` or `Disabled`. Left
out for every status.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, status, endpoint.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Registers a receiver of tenant CAEP/RISC tokens with a public-HTTPS `endpoint`,
`delivery_method` (`Push` or `Poll`) and at least one `signal_types` entry.
Optionally the `authorization_header` each push carries (kept sealed,
never shown again) and the `default_subjects` the stream starts with
(`ALL`, the default, or `NONE` until subjects are added). Created in
`Active` status with its endpoint `Pending`: ianua sends the endpoint a
challenge as a verification event, and the stream delivers nothing
until the receiver echoes it to the confirm endpoint. Returns `id` and one-time
`receiver_key`, a bearer for polling, verification requests and subject changes
on this stream only. Records `signals.stream_registered`.

`422` for an endpoint that is not public HTTPS, no signal type, or a
header value that is not 1 to 4096 visible characters. Requires the
right to manage signal streams.

get.description:
Returns a single stream by `id`, with whether its endpoint is verified
but never the challenge the endpoint was sent. `404` if it does not
exist under this tenant. Read-only. Requires the right to view signal
streams.

delete.description:
Removes a signal stream receiver for good. It must be disabled first, so
a stream that may still deliver is never deleted (`409`). Records
`signals.stream_deleted`. `404` if it does not exist. Requires the right
to manage signal streams.

patch.description:
Partial update: send `endpoint`, `delivery_method`, `signal_types`
and/or `authorization_header` (`null` for none) to change just those;
leave any out to keep it. This
edits configuration only, never `status` (pause, resume and disable do
that). A new endpoint is `Pending` again and is sent a fresh challenge.
Records one `signals.stream_updated`; a body that changes nothing
records nothing. `404` if the stream does not exist, `422` for an
endpoint that is not public HTTPS or an empty list of signal types.
Requires the right to manage signal streams.

post.description:
Called by the receiver, not by a person of the tenant: it holds no
session, only the `challenge` ianua sent its endpoint when the endpoint
was set, which it echoes here. When the echo matches, the endpoint is
verified and the stream starts delivering to it. The domain has no event
for a verified endpoint, so nothing is recorded.

`401` when no open tenant has the path's name or the tenant has no such
stream, answered alike so a caller learns nothing of which tenants
exist; `403` when the echo is not the challenge the endpoint was sent
(the endpoint stays pending); `422` when the endpoint is already
verified. Needs no credential.

401.description: No such tenant or stream, or the tenant is closed

403.description: Not the challenge the endpoint was sent

422.description: Already verified, or not a challenge

get.description:
Returns the stream's delivery attempts, one per signal pushed (or
queued, for a poll stream), sortable and paginated: how each ended, the
code the receiver answered with, and how long it took. `404` if the
stream does not exist. Read-only. Requires the right to view signal
streams.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: attempted_at, status.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Disables a stream for good: the receiver gets nothing more through it,
and unlike a pause it cannot be resumed. Delete it to remove it
entirely. Records `signals.stream_disabled`. `404` if the stream does
not exist, `422` if it is already disabled. Requires the right to manage
signal streams.

Pauses an `Active` stream. Signals raised while it is paused are
dropped, not queued. Records `signals.stream_paused`. `404` if the
stream does not exist, `422` if it is not `Active`. Requires the right
to manage signal streams.

RFC 8936 for `Poll` streams: `ack` removes received event `jti`s; `maxEvents`
requests 1..100 events, default 100. Returns the oldest unacknowledged signed
tokens in `sets`, keyed by `jti`, with `moreAvailable` when more wait.
Replies immediately and repeats events until acknowledged, including after lost
responses. Records nothing; each event was recorded when raised.

The stream's receiver polls with the key it was handed at registration
as its bearer, and reaches its own stream only; a person needs the
right to manage signal streams.

requestBody.description: What to acknowledge and how many to take; send none for the largest batch

401.description: Unauthenticated, or not the stream's key

403.description: Forbidden, or the key is another stream's

409.description: The stream is pushed, not polled

post.description:
Resumes a `Paused` stream. Signals raised from now on are delivered;
none from the pause are. Records `signals.stream_resumed`. `404` if the
stream does not exist, `422` if it is not `Paused` (a disabled stream
stays disabled). Requires the right to manage signal streams.

get.description:
Returns whether the stream is `enabled`, `paused` or `disabled`, in the
Shared Signals framework's words. Pause, resume and disable change it.
`404` if the stream does not exist. Read-only. Requires the right to
view signal streams.

post.summary: Add a subject to a signal stream
post.description:
Makes the stream hear about one user or agent: `subject` names it in
the opaque format (`{"format": "opaque", "id": "<uuid>"}`) and `kind`
says which it is (`User`, the default, or `Agent`). A stream that
already hears about it is left as it is. Records
`signals.subject_added` when it changed.

The stream's receiver calls with the key it was handed at registration
as its bearer, and reaches its own stream only; a person needs the
right to manage signal streams.

204.description: The stream hears about the subject

401.description: Unauthenticated, or not the stream's key

403.description: Forbidden, or the key is another stream's

404.description: No such stream, user or agent

422.description: Not an opaque subject, or the stream lists the most it keeps

post.summary: Remove a subject from a signal stream
post.description:
Makes the stream stop hearing about one user or agent, named as for
adding one. A stream that already does not hear about it is left as it
is. Records `signals.subject_removed` when it changed.

The stream's receiver calls with its key as its bearer, and reaches its
own stream only; a person needs the right to manage signal streams.

204.description: The stream no longer hears about the subject

401.description: Unauthenticated, or not the stream's key

403.description: Forbidden, or the key is another stream's

404.description: No such stream, user or agent

422.description: Not an opaque subject, or the stream lists the most it keeps

post.summary: Ask a signal stream for a verification event
post.description:
Sends a verification event down the stream, pushed to its endpoint or
held for its receiver to poll, carrying back the `state` given, if any,
so the receiver can match it to its request. The answer does not wait
on the receiver. Only an active stream with a verified endpoint is sent
one (`409` otherwise), and a stream may be asked only now and then
(`429`). Records `signals.verification_requested`.

The stream's receiver calls with the key it was handed at registration
as its bearer, and reaches its own stream only; a person needs the
right to manage signal streams.

requestBody.description: The state the event carries back; send none for no state

204.description: A verification event was sent down the stream

401.description: Unauthenticated, or not the stream's key

403.description: Forbidden, or the key is another stream's

409.description: The stream is not active, or its endpoint is not verified

422.description: The state is not a short token

post.description:
Freezes an `Active` tenant: every session is signed out and new
sign-ins are refused, but its data is kept for reactivation. When an
operator suspends it, the platform holds it, and only the platform
brings it back.

**State.** `Active → Suspended`. Returns `404` if the tenant does not
exist, or `422` if it is not `Active`. Records `tenant.status_changed`.

Requires a member who may change the organization's tenants, or an
operator.

get.description:
Returns this tenant's registered tools: name, endpoint, input schema,
route, and the action class and data class each carries. Requires
`Agents(View)`.

post.description:
Adds an API agents may call: a model-facing name, description and input
schema bound to an HTTP endpoint on one of the tenant's routes. The tool
takes its action class and data class from that route, so the
orchestration loop offers only the tools inside a run's purpose, and a
run that has read data of a higher class than the tool's is refused it.
The person registering it may use it from then on. Records
`agents.tool_registered`. Requires `Agents(Manage)`.

put.description:
Replaces a tool's whole definition, in the shape it was registered
with: its name, description, input schema, method, path and the route
that serves it. The tool takes its action class and data class from the
route again, so a tool moved to a riskier route waits for approval like
any call of that class. Its status is unchanged. Records
`agents.tool_edited`. Requires `Agents(Manage)`.

422.description: Validation error, or the route does not serve the call

delete.description:
Removes a tool for good. The tool must be disabled first. Records
`agents.tool_deleted`. Requires `Agents(Delete)`.

patch.description:
Sets a tool's status. A disabled tool is kept but no longer offered to
agents. Records `agents.tool_status_changed`. Requires `Agents(Update)`.

get.summary: List the tenant's declared custom fields
get.description:
What a client renders a form, a filter bar or a column chooser from.
Withdrawn fields are left out unless `include_archived=true`. A caller
not cleared for sensitive fields is not told they exist: listing one and
refusing to fill it in would disclose that the tenant records a salary,
which is most of what the setting hides. Read-only.

parameters.name: include_archived
parameters.description:
Include the attributes withdrawn from use. Off by default: a form has
no use for them.

post.summary: Declare a custom field on the tenant's users
post.description:
`kind` is the only choice that has to be made: the control, the valid
values and the comparisons a filter may use all follow from it. The
internal name is derived from the display name when omitted, and is
fixed once declared because every stored value is filed under it.

Nothing is exposed that was not asked for: a new field is not returned
in listings, not filterable and not sortable until it is said to be. A
withdrawn field still holds its name. Records
`identity.attribute_declared`. Requires the right to change the schema.

403.description: Forbidden, or the plan allows no more

get.summary: The kinds a custom field may be declared as
get.description:
Each entry carries everything that follows from the choice: the control
to render, the others it may be rendered with, the comparisons a filter
may use, and whether it needs a list of options, a length limit or a
range. A client builds the "what kind of thing is this?" step from it,
so the list lives in one place. The catalogue is the platform's, the
same for every tenant. Requires a caller of the tenant.

200.description: The kinds a field may be declared as

delete.summary: Discard a field and every value stored under it
delete.description:
The only call here that destroys customer data, and the reason it is
not the first step: a field must already be withdrawn from use before
it can be deleted. The response says how many values went with it.
Records `identity.attribute_deleted`. Requires the right to change the
schema.

patch.description:
Widening is always allowed. Narrowing is allowed only while nothing
already sits outside the new bounds: withdrawing an option somebody
chose, shortening a limit past what somebody wrote, or requiring a field
somebody left empty are each refused, and the refusal says how many
people it concerns. Naming one visibility flag leaves the others as they
are. Making a sensitive field ordinary needs clearance for it.

The internal name and the kind cannot be changed; ask for a new field
instead. Records `identity.attribute_updated`. Requires the right to
change the schema.

409.description: The change would strand stored values

put.summary: Withdraw a field from use, or bring it back
put.description:
Withdrawing takes the field off every form, listing, filter and sort
while keeping every value stored under it, so a mistake costs nothing to
undo. It is also the first of the two steps to deleting, which keeps
"remove this column" and "discard what a thousand people put in it" two
separate decisions. Asking for the state it is already in changes
nothing and succeeds. Records `identity.attribute_archived` or
`identity.attribute_restored`. Requires the right to change the schema.

get.description:
Returns a paginated, sortable page of users, optionally filtered by
`status` (an account status, or `PendingInvitation` /
`InvitationExpired` for an open invitation), an `email` or `name`
substring, a directly held `role_id`, a `group_id`, and when they last
signed in or were created (`last_login_from`/`last_login_until`,
`created_from`/`created_until`, RFC 3339).
Custom attributes filter with `attr=<namespace>.<key>:<operator>[:<value>]`
and order with `sort=attr:<namespace>.<key>`, each only as far as the
attribute was opened for it and the caller is cleared to see it.

Each entry carries its directly assigned roles, an invited user's
invitation state and the role accepting grants, and the custom fields
declared as listed that the caller may read. Read-only. Requires the
right to view users.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Filter by account status, or by the state of an open invitation
(`PendingInvitation` or `InvitationExpired`). Omit to return
everyone.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on email address.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on display name.

parameters.name: role_id
parameters.description: Only users holding this role directly.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: Only members of this group.

parameters.name: last_login_from
parameters.description: Only users who last signed in at or after this time (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: last_login_until
parameters.description: Only users who last signed in before this time (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only users created at or after this time (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: created_until
parameters.description: Only users created before this time (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: attr
parameters.description: Filter by a custom attribute, `<namespace>.<key>:<operator>[:<value>]`, such as `app.department:is:sales`. Repeat to require every filter. A comparison against a list takes comma-separated values.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right, or one custom attribute as `attr:<namespace>.<key>`. Prefix with `-` for descending order. Allowed fields: created_at, updated_at, email, display_name, status, last_login_at.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

403.description: Forbidden, or a sensitive attribute named without clearance

422.description: A filter or order the schema refuses

post.summary: Register a new user in the tenant
post.description:
Creates an end user and mails a link to confirm their address. Without
`auto_verify` the account waits in `PendingVerification` and cannot sign
in until its holder follows the link. With `auto_verify: true` it is
`Active` at once, which needs the right to let accounts in; the address
still stays unconfirmed until the link is followed, since nobody vouches
for an address.

Supply a `password`, or omit it and the platform generates one, returned
as `generated_password`, the only time it is ever shown. A supplied
password is held to the tenant's password policy.

`role_ids` (or the older `role_id`) grants roles at creation, beside the
tenant's defaults; a role carrying something you cannot hand out is
refused. The tenant's user limit is checked before anything is made.
Records `identity.user_registered`. Requires the right to create users.

403.description: Forbidden, or the plan allows no more users

404.description: A named role does not exist

post.description:
Public: no session required. The invitee follows the link in the
invitation email and submits its `token` here with the `password` they
chose. The token is a single-use secret: presenting it proves the
recipient reads the invited address, so this both authenticates and
activates the account.

The `password` is held to the tenant's password policy, which the
invitation-status check returns so the form can show it. A password that
fails it, or a missing one, answers `422` and changes nothing. A tenant
without password sign-in takes no password: one that is sent is never
stored.

Invitation `Pending -> Accepted`; user `Invited -> Active`, address
confirmed, join time recorded, the invited role granted if the sender
still holds what it carries. An unknown token, or one whose invitation
was already answered or revoked, answers `404`; one past its expiry
answers `410`, so the page can offer a new link. A welcome mail follows.
Records `identity.invitation_accepted`.

404.description: Unknown token, or an invitation already answered

410.description: Invitation expired; ask for a new link

422.description: Validation error, including a password the policy refuses

post.description:
Public, matching the accept endpoint: the invitee turns the invitation
down from its link. Invitation `Pending -> Declined` (terminal); the
account that waited on it is closed. Records
`identity.invitation_declined`.

404.description: Unknown token, or an invitation already answered

post.description:
Follows the cancel link mailed to the address the account has now when
someone asked to move it: the change is dropped and its confirmation
link stops working. Records `identity.email_change_cancelled`. Public:
the token is what proves the request came from the current mailbox.

404.description: Unknown token, or a change no longer waiting

post.summary: Replace a dead email change link
post.description:
The way out of the `Expired` screen the change-status endpoint shows.
Submit the same `token` and another confirmation goes to the address the
change waits on, never to one supplied here. A change already confirmed
no longer waits, so its token answers `404`; so does the old token once
this succeeds. `retry_after_seconds` is how long to hold the button
down. Records `identity.email_change_link_resent`. Public, matching the
confirm endpoint.

post.summary: Check an email change link without confirming it
post.description:
Submit the `token` and get back `Valid`, `Expired`, `AlreadyUsed` or
`Invalid`, so the page a link lands on can show the right thing before it
acts. A link for a change whose account is gone reads `Invalid`. Public,
matching the confirm endpoint.

Follows the `token` mailed to the new address and only now applies the
change: the account moves to the new address, marked verified, and the
old address is told where it went. Links mailed to the old address stop
working. Until this succeeds the original address stays in use.

The token alone authorizes it, as for address verification: it applies
to whichever account's change it names. A change is void once the
address moved some other way or the password changed since. `409` if
the new address was claimed by someone else in this tenant meanwhile.
Records `identity.email_changed`. Public.

409.description: The new address was taken meanwhile

post.summary: Cancel an erasure from its emailed link
post.description:
Follows the cancel link mailed when the erasure was asked for: the
request is dropped and the account opens again. Public: the person
cannot sign in while their account is closing, so the token is what
proves the request is theirs. Records `identity.erasure_cancelled`.

404.description: Unknown token, or a request no longer waiting

post.description:
Stops an erasure before it is carried out and opens the account again.
The person themselves cancels from the link mailed to them; this is for
someone who may erase the person. Records `identity.erasure_cancelled`.

409.description: The request can no longer be cancelled

post.summary: Put an erasure under a legal hold
post.description:
A held request is never carried out, whatever its date, until the hold
is released. Records `identity.erasure_held`. Requires the right to
erase the person.

post.summary: Release an erasure from its legal hold
post.description:
The request is due again on its own date. Records
`identity.erasure_released`. Requires the right to erase the person.

A short-lived address of a ready export's file. Only the person the
export is about downloads it, never staff, even one who asked for it.
Records `identity.data_export_downloaded`. Requires a tenant user's own
session.

401.description: Unauthenticated, or not a tenant user's own session

409.description: Not ready, or its week is over

post.description:
Imports exported accounts with their existing password hashes
(Argon2id, bcrypt, scrypt or PBKDF2-SHA256). Every record is checked
first, and a batch with one that does not check out is refused whole.
The import is then kept and answered with its id; a worker opens the
accounts in chunks of 500, each chunk kept whole, and
`GET .../users/imports/{id}` says how far it got. A record whose
address has an account by the time it is reached is set aside and
listed there; the rest go on. Each account waits for its holder to
follow the link mailed to its address once its chunk is kept; the person
then signs in with the password they already have, and that sign-in
replaces the foreign hash. The plan's room for users must hold every
record when the import starts, and is checked again for each chunk as it
runs: a record past the room left by then, say after another import, is
set aside as `user_limit_reached`. Records `identity.user_imported` for each account and
`identity.users_imported` once the import ends. Requires the right to
create users.

202.description: The import is kept and queued

403.description: Forbidden, or the plan has no room for every record

422.description: A record, a hash or the batch is refused

get.summary: Show how an import is going
get.description:
Where an import of users stands (`pending`, `running`, `finished` or
`failed`), how many records it holds, opened and set aside, and for each
record set aside its line in the request and why. It never shows an
address or a password hash. Requires the right to view users.

post.description:
The way out of the `Expired` screen the invitation-status endpoint
shows. Submit the same `token` and another invitation goes to the
address it was sent to, never to one supplied here.

Keyed on the token, so it tells nothing about who has been invited. An
invitation that was accepted, declined or revoked is closed and answers
`404`; an admin inviting again is the only way back from those. The old
link stops working the moment this succeeds, so a second try with the
same token answers `404`. `retry_after_seconds` is how long to hold the
button down. Records `identity.invitation_resent`. Public, matching the
accept endpoint.

403.description: No mail server is set up; ask whoever invited you to send it again

404.description: Unknown token, or a closed invitation

post.summary: Check an invitation link without accepting it
post.description:
Submit the `token` and get back `Valid`, `Expired`, `AlreadyUsed` or
`Invalid`. `AlreadyUsed` covers an invitation accepted, declined or
revoked: all final, and none of them something a new link would fix.

A `Valid` link also returns the tenant's `password_policy`, the rules
accepting will hold the chosen password to. It is left out for a tenant
without password sign-in, and for every other status. Public, matching
the accept endpoint: the invitee has no account yet.

post.summary: Invite a user to this tenant
post.description:
Creates a user in `Invited` status and emails them a single-use link.
The invitee follows it and accepts at `.../users/accept-invitation` to
activate their account, or declines at `.../users/decline-invitation`.
On a deployment with no mail server nothing is mailed: the answer
carries the `accept_link` for you to pass on to the invitee.

The link carries both slugs and its token, needing no session. It expires after the
configured invitation lifetime; to re-issue a lost or expired invitation
use `.../users/{id}/resend-invitation` rather than inviting the same
address again, which answers `409` while an invitation waits.

The `role_id` is granted on acceptance, so it must be a role you could
hand out yourself: one carrying a permission you do not hold is refused
with `403`. An optional personal `message` goes into the email. The
tenant's user limit counts an invited user. Records
`identity.user_invited`. Requires the right to create users.

403.description: Forbidden, a role you cannot hand out, or the plan allows no more users

409.description: The address is taken or already invited

post.summary: Verify an email address with the emailed token
post.description:
Public: the person confirming has no session yet, since an unconfirmed
account cannot sign in, and the emailed token is what proves the address
is theirs. Confirming activates the account and a welcome mail follows.
Records `identity.email_verified`.

post.summary: Request another verification email from an expired or lost link
post.description:
Keyed on the token rather than an address, so only someone who was sent
a link can ask for its replacement; an expired token is as good as a live
one for this. The new link goes to the account's address. Public, for
the same reason the status check is: the caller has no session yet.

200.description: Another verification email is on its way

404.description: Unknown token, or the address is already confirmed

post.summary: Check a verification link without following it
post.description:
Submit the `token` and get back `Valid`, `Expired` or `Verified`, so the
page a link lands on can show the right thing before it acts. Nothing
here spends the token. Public: the page is reached from an email and its
reader is not signed in yet.

get.summary: Get a single user by id
get.description:
Returns one user. Role assignments are not filled in here; use the list
endpoint when you need them. `404` when the id is unknown. Read-only.
Requires the right to view users.

delete.description:
Removes the account for good, after revoking every delegation the user
granted and ending their sessions. Irreversible. `404` when the user does
not exist; the tenant's last administrator cannot be deleted (`409`).
Records `identity.user_deleted`. Requires the right to delete users, and
holding at least everything the user holds.

patch.description:
Patch any of `display_name`, `email` and `email_verified`, each applied
when present. A new display name renames the user (records
`identity.user_renamed`). A new email starts a pending change: a link is
mailed to it, and the user's current address stays in use until it is
followed. `email_verified: true` mails the current address a link that
confirms it: nobody vouches for an address, only the link marks it
verified.

Requires the right to edit the user's profile, or to change their
sign-in for an address, and holding at least everything the user holds.

get.summary: Read one user's custom field values
get.description:
Keyed by `<namespace>.<key>`. A person reads all of their own declared
values. Someone else needs the right to view users, and sees a sensitive
value only with clearance for it; a value the caller may not see is left
out rather than nulled, so its absence says nothing about whether the
person holds one.

delete.summary: Clear every custom value a user holds
delete.description:
Deletes the user's values in both namespaces at once. Records
`identity.metadata_deleted`. Requires the right to edit the user's
profile, and holding at least everything the user holds.

put.summary: Set one of a user's custom values, or clear it
put.description:
The value is checked against the declaration: a field nobody declared is
refused rather than stored, and so is a value of the wrong type, outside
the declared range, longer than the declared limit, or not among the
declared options. Sending `null` clears the value, which a required
field refuses.

A person keeps their own `user` fields from their own session; every
other write, `app` fields included, needs the right to edit the person's
profile. The record names who changed which field, never the value.
Records `identity.metadata_updated`.

422.description: No such field, or the value does not suit it

post.description:
Records a decision on one set of terms (`consent_type` and `version`).
Only the person gives their own consent, from their own session.
Withdrawing is as easy as giving: the person does it, or someone who may
record it for them does, since withdrawing only lowers what is done with
their data. Records `identity.consent_granted` or
`identity.consent_revoked`.

403.description: Forbidden, or consent given for someone else

post.description:
Switches the account off: every delegation the user granted is revoked
and their sessions end. A deactivated user can be let in again through
the status endpoint. The tenant's last administrator cannot be shut out
(`409`). Records `identity.user_status_changed`. Requires the right to shut
users out, and holding at least everything the user holds.

put.description:
Sets the given and family name, the name they go by, their picture and
their phone number, all at once: a field left out is cleared. A person
changes their own with their session; anyone else needs the right to
edit the user's profile and to hold at least everything the user holds.
A phone number here is the person's word and nothing sends codes to it.
Records `identity.user_profile_updated`, naming the fields that changed.

403.description: Forbidden, or the user holds more than the caller

post.description:
Asks for the person's data to be erased once the grace period passes.
The person asks from their own session, or someone who may erase them
asks for them. The account closes at once, its sessions and delegations
end, and a link to cancel goes to its address: the person cannot sign
in meanwhile, so the link is how they change their mind. Records
`identity.erasure_requested`.

409.description: An erasure is already under way, or the tenant's last administrator

502.description: The mail service refused the cancel link; the request stands

get.description:
Every copy of their data asked for, and where each stands. A person
reads their own; anyone else needs the right to view users. Read-only.

post.summary: Ask for a copy of a user's data
post.description:
Starts gathering a copy of what is kept about the user (`access`, GDPR
article 15) or what they gave the service themselves, in a form another
service reads (`portability`, article 20). The file never holds a
secret. The person is mailed when it is ready, and only they download
it, for a week. A person asks for their own; staff need the right to
view users. Records `identity.data_export_requested`.

409.description: An export is already being gathered

post.summary: Ask to act as a user for support
post.description:
A tenant admin asks to act as one of the tenant's people for a short
while, with a reason, to see what they see and put it right. Where the
tenant has the person approve, they are mailed and it waits for them;
where the admin decides, it starts at once. The admin needs full control
of users and must hold what the person holds. Records
`identity.support_impersonation_requested`. Requires a tenant user's own
session.

201.description: Asked; started at once where the admin decides

401.description: Unauthenticated, or not a tenant user's own session

403.description: The caller may not act as this user, holds less, or names themselves

409.description: The user may not sign in now

422.description: Validation error, or a window outside 5 to 60 minutes

put.description:
Sets what the company's directory records about a user: the id another
directory knows them by, their department, their manager and their
employee number, all at once: a field left out is cleared. These are the
company's records, so the person alone never changes them. Records
`identity.user_profile_updated`. Requires the right to update users, and
holding at least everything the user holds.

403.description: Forbidden, or the user holds more than the caller

404.description: The user, or the manager named, is not in the tenant

422.description: Validation error, or the user named as their own manager

post.description:
Re-issues the invitation email for an invited user. The previous link
stops working at once and a fresh expiry window opens: use this when an
invitation was lost or has expired, instead of inviting the same address
again. The invitation stays `Pending` and the user `Invited`.

On a deployment with no mail server nothing is mailed: the answer is
`200` with the new single-use `accept_link`, for you to pass on to the
invitee. Whoever holds it joins as the invited account.

`404` when the user has no waiting invitation (they already answered,
or it was revoked). Records `identity.invitation_resent`. Requires the
right to create users.

200.description: No mail server is set up: the new accept link to pass on

404.description: No waiting invitation for this user

post.summary: Clear a user's second factor and passkeys
post.description:
For someone who lost their device and their recovery codes: turns off
their second factor, in force or being set up, and removes their
passkeys, so they can sign in with their password and set up new ones.
Their sessions end. Records `authentication.factors_reset`. Requires the
right to change the user's sign-in, and holding at least everything the
user holds.

403.description: Forbidden, or the user holds more than the caller

post.description:
Admin reset: sets a new password for another member and returns it once
for the admin to relay. Omit `password` and one meeting the tenant's
policy is generated. `password_breach` says what the breach lookup found;
a tenant that blocks breached passwords refuses one with `422`. The user
must change the password at their next sign-in. Every session the user holds ends, and devices they
remembered stop skipping the second factor. Records
`identity.password_reset`. Requires the right to change the
user's sign-in, and holding at least everything the user holds.

422.description: The password breaks the tenant's policy

post.description:
Cancels an outstanding invitation so its link can no longer activate
the account: to undo an invitation sent to the wrong person, or to clear
one that will never be accepted. Invitation `Pending -> Revoked`
(terminal); the account that waited on it is closed. An expired
invitation can still be revoked.

`404` when the user has no waiting invitation. Records
`identity.invitation_revoked`. Requires the right to shut the invited
account out.

404.description: No waiting invitation for this user

post.summary: Mail a user a password reset link
post.description:
The alternative to choosing a password for someone: the user is mailed a
link and sets their own, so the admin never learns it. Records
`authentication.password_reset_requested`. Requires the right to change
the user's sign-in, and holding at least everything the user holds.

204.description: The link is on its way

403.description: Forbidden, or the user holds more than the caller

429.description: A link went to this address moments ago

post.description:
Mails a user a one-time link that confirms they read their address; they
follow it at `.../users/verify-email`. This changes no status: the
address is marked verified only when the link is followed. Allowed for
the user themselves, or someone who may change their sign-in. `429`
when a link went out very recently. Records
`identity.verification_email_sent`.

429.description: A link went out moments ago

post.description:
Mails the user that their account exists and where to sign in, carrying
no password: whoever made the account relays that, or the user takes the
forgotten-password route. A user who is gone, or a mail the mail service
refuses, is no error. Records `identity.welcome_email_sent` once the
mail is accepted. Requires the right to create users.

get.description:
The user's live sessions on every device. A person reads their own with
their session; anyone else needs the right to view users. Read-only.

delete.description:
Signs the user out on one device. Records
`authentication.session_revoked`. A person ends their own with their
session; anyone else needs the right to shut users out, and to hold at
least everything the user holds.

403.description: Forbidden, or the user holds more than the caller

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
`Active` unlocks a locked account and lets any other one in, a
deactivated one included. `Locked` and `Deactivated` first revoke every
delegation the user granted and end their sessions. `Invited`,
`PendingVerification` and `Closing` are reached only through their own
flows (`403`). Records `identity.user_status_changed`. Requires the right to let
users in or shut them out, and holding at least everything the user
holds.

403.description: Forbidden, or a status no admin moves a user into

409.description: Shutting out the tenant's last administrator

422.description: The status rules refuse the move

get.description:
Returns this tenant's webhook subscriptions, optionally only those in one
`status` (`Active`, `Paused` or `Disabled`), sortable and paginated. Each
entry carries the URL, event types, description and lifecycle status,
never the signing secret. Read-only. Requires the right to view webhooks.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Only subscriptions in this status: `Active`, `Paused` or `Disabled`.
Left out for every status.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, updated_at, status, url.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Registers a webhook: ianua posts matching events to `url` (HTTPS on the
public internet), signed as Standard Webhooks lays it out
(`webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature`) with a secret
of the subscription's own. Choose the `event_types` to receive (empty
means every event the creator may see now), an optional `description`
and how hard failed deliveries are retried (`retry`: `Standard` when
left out, `Aggressive` or `Patient`). Created in `Active` status.
Returns the subscription `id` and the `signing_secret`, shown this once:
keep it to verify deliveries. Records `webhooks.subscription_created`.

`422` for a URL that is not public HTTPS, an invalid description, or the
webhook delivery event named. `403` when the caller names an event they
may not see, or the plan's webhook limit is reached. Requires the right
to update webhooks.

get.summary: List the events a webhook may receive
get.description:
Returns every event the caller may subscribe a webhook to, each with the
`event_type` a subscription lists, its dotted `name` and what it means.
Only events the caller's rights let them see are listed, and never the
record of a webhook's own delivery. Read-only. Requires the right to
view webhooks.

Returns a single subscription by `id`, never its signing secret. `404`
if it does not exist under this tenant. Read-only. Requires the right to
view webhooks.

delete.description:
Removes a subscription and its delivery history for good; nothing more
is delivered to its URL. An active subscription is paused or disabled
first (`409` otherwise). Records `webhooks.subscription_deleted`. `404`
if it does not exist. Requires the right to update webhooks.

patch.description:
Partial update: send `url`, `event_types`, `description` (or `null` to
clear it) and/or `retry` to change just those; leave any out to keep
it. A new URL starts with no failures counted. New event types are held
to what the caller may see, like at creation. Returns the subscription
as it now stands. Records one `webhooks.subscription_updated` naming
what changed; a body that changes nothing records nothing.

`404` if the subscription does not exist, `422` for a URL that is not
public HTTPS, the webhook delivery event named, or a disabled
subscription (it is replaced, not changed). `403` when the caller names
an event they may not see. Requires the right to update webhooks.

get.description:
Returns the subscription's delivery attempts (how each ended, the code
the receiver answered with, how long it took, when), sortable and
paginated, for working out why events are not getting through. `404` if
the subscription does not exist. Read-only. Requires the right to view
webhooks.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: attempted_at, status, attempt_number.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Sends the message of an earlier attempt again, under its own message id
(`webhook-id`), so a receiver that already handled it drops it, signed
with every secret the subscription signs with now. Returns the new
attempt, which is kept in the history, counted on the endpoint's
failure streak and recorded as `webhooks.delivery_attempted`. It is not
retried. Only an event the subscription's creator may still see is
sent again (`403` otherwise). Each webhook may be sent to only now and
then (`429`). Requires the right to update webhooks.

200.description: Sent again; how the new try ended

403.description: Forbidden, or the webhook no longer receives the event

404.description: No such subscription, attempt or message

422.description: The URL resolves to an address deliveries may not reach

post.description:
Pauses an `Active` subscription. Events raised while it is paused are
not delivered, then or later. Records `webhooks.subscription_paused`.
`404` if the subscription does not exist, `422` if it is already paused
or disabled. Requires the right to update webhooks.

Resumes a `Paused` subscription and clears its failure count. Events
raised during the pause are not sent. Records
`webhooks.subscription_resumed`. `404` if the subscription does not
exist, `422` if it is active or disabled (a disabled subscription is
never resumed). Requires the right to update webhooks.

Gives the subscription a new signing secret. With no body, or no
`overlap_seconds`, the old one stops at once, as after a leak. With
`overlap_seconds` (at most seven days), the old one keeps signing beside
the new one until then: each delivery carries a signature per secret,
so a receiver still on the old secret accepts it while it moves over. A
secret from an earlier rotation stops at once. Returns the new
`signing_secret`, shown this once. Records `webhooks.secret_rotated`.
`404` if the subscription does not exist. Requires the right to manage
webhooks.

422.description: Overlap not valid, or over seven days

post.summary: Send a test event to a webhook
post.description:
Sends the subscription a sample of one of the events it lists
(`event_type`), marked `"test": true` and holding none of the tenant's
data, signed and bounded like any delivery, so its owner can check the
endpoint receives and verifies deliveries. Returns the attempt, which
is kept in the history and recorded as `webhooks.delivery_attempted`,
but never counted on the failure streak, so testing an endpoint that is
down never switches it off. It is not retried. Each webhook may be sent
to only now and then (`429`). Requires the right to update webhooks.

422.description: The subscription does not list the event, or its URL may not be reached

get.description:
Returns the latest version of each of the tenant's workflows, sortable
and paginated. Each carries its `graph`, `trigger`, `status` (`draft`,
`published` or `archived`) and the `revision` a publisher hands back.
Requires the right to view workflows.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, updated_at, name.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Drafts version 1 of a new workflow with a `name`, its `graph` of steps
and edges, the `trigger` that starts it and `run_limit_seconds`, how long
one execution may run (at most 31 days). Each step is named by `kind`:
`agent_run`, `action`, `condition`, `transform`, `approval` or `wait`.
An action step's `effect` and `ceiling` are checked against the
integration catalog when the workflow is published. Records
`workflows.workflow_created`. Requires the right to create workflows,
within the plan's workflow limit.

403.description: Forbidden, or the plan's workflow limit is reached

get.description:
Returns the tenant's integration accounts, oldest first, paginated. Each
entry names its `integration`, its `owner`, who it is shared with
(`sharing`), the `operations` it may be used for (`null` for every one)
and its `status`. A credential is never returned. Requires the right to
view workflows.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Connects an account of an installed `integration` for the caller, who
owns it. The `credential` is sealed before it is kept and never shown
again. `sharing` is `owner_only` (the default) or `tenant`; `operations`
limits it to some of the integration's operations. `404` when no such
integration is installed.

Checks connection rights before asking the integration's service to verify the
credential. Refusal (`422`) or unavailability (`502`) saves nothing. The HTTP
request integration has no service to ask and stores credentials unchecked.

Records `workflows.account_connected`. Requires the right to connect
accounts.

422.description: Validation error, or the integration's service refused the credential

502.description: The integration's service could not be asked whether the credential works

post.summary: Begin connecting an account by signing in
post.description:
Starts a caller-owned `integration` account connection, returning `connection_id`
and browser `address`. The service returns to `/api/v1/integrations/callback`,
then `/integrations/connected` receives the connection and one-time code to finish.
`name`, `sharing` and `operations` match credential-based connections.
Services with several spaces expose `sign_in_asks_for`, such as Azure DevOps `organization`;
`place` names it, such as `contoso`, and each organization is
connected as an account of its own.

`422` for absent service sign-in or deployment app registration (`connecting: credential`),
or missing/unexpected `place`. Expires after ten minutes without completion.
Records `workflows.account_connection_started`.
Requires the right to connect accounts.

422.description: Validation error, or the integration cannot be connected by signing in here

post.description:
Finishes the connection the service answered, with the one-time `code`
the browser brought back to the dashboard, and connects the account it
was begun for, owned by the caller. The credential the service issued
is tried first, as when connecting with a credential.

Only the person who began it may: anyone else is refused with `403`,
the connection is spent and the refusal recorded, so a link sent to
someone else never lands their account in another tenant. Records
`workflows.account_connected`, or `workflows.account_connection_refused`.
Requires the right to connect accounts.

403.description: Forbidden, a wrong code, or not the person who began it

409.description: It ran out, the service has not answered, or it was finished already

422.description: The integration's service refused the credential

502.description: The integration's service could not be asked whether the credential works

patch.description:
Makes one change, named by `change`: `enable`, `disable`,
`replace_credential` (with `credential`), `share_with_tenant`,
`keep_to_owner`, `limit_to` (with `operations`, `null` for every one) or
`rename` (with `name`). Answers the account as saved. `422` when it is
already enabled or disabled. A replacement credential is tried as
connecting tries one, once the caller is known to be the owner: `422`
when the service refuses it and `502` when it cannot be asked, the
account keeping the credential it had. Records `workflows.account_enabled`,
`workflows.account_disabled` or `workflows.account_changed`. Requires being its owner, or the right to connect accounts for changes
that are not the owner's alone.

422.description: Validation error, already in that state, or the integration's service refused a replacement credential

502.description: The integration's service could not be asked whether a replacement credential works

get.description:
The `address` to give a service whose events reach one address per
account, how the channel gets ready (`setup`) and where it is
(`status`). No channel exists until a workflow starting on that
service's events is published. Nothing secret is returned. Requires
owning the account or the right to connect accounts.

404.description: No such account, or no channel yet

post.summary: Confirm an event channel's token was pasted back
post.description:
Puts the channel live once its owner has pasted the token back at the
service. Until then the address reads nothing. Records
`workflows.channel_ready`. Only the account's owner may do it.

404.description: No such account, or no channel yet

post.summary: Paste in an event channel's key
post.description:
Keeps the key the service signs its deliveries with, sealed, and puts
the channel live. Pasting again replaces it. The key is never returned.
Records `workflows.channel_ready`. Only the account's owner may do it.

404.description: No such account, or no channel yet

409.description: This service's channel takes no key

422.description: The key is too short or too long

post.description:
Returns the token the service sent the address, to paste back at the
service. A `POST` because reading it is on the record: records
`workflows.channel_token_shown`. Only the account's owner may do it.

404.description: No such account, or no channel yet

get.summary: List the apps a workflow may call
get.description:
Returns every active route the tenant opened to workflows, in the order
the gateway tries them, each with the `id` a Protected apps step names
in its `route` input, its `name`, the `path_pattern` a step's `path`
must fit, the `methods` it answers and the `hosts` it answers on. Each
call is still decided by the route's own policy for the person the run
acts for. Read-only. Requires the right to view workflows.

get.summary: List the systems a workflow may reach
get.description:
Returns every active stream route the tenant opened to workflows, by
name, each with the `id` a Protected data step names in its `route`
input and its `name`. Each connection is still decided by the stream
route's own access for the person the run acts for, and the login kept
for it is never shown. Read-only. Requires the right to view workflows.

get.summary: List the service events a workflow may start on
get.description:
Returns every event the installed integrations' services send that may
start a workflow, each with its `title`, a `description` of when it
happens, the `filters` a trigger may set to narrow which of these
events start it, and the `outputs` it gives the workflow at their paths
in the trigger's output. A `service` trigger names one of these with
the account it registers through; publishing registers it at the
service. Read-only. Requires the right to view workflows.

Returns one page of the tenant's executions of every designed workflow,
newest first, each as the execution endpoint shows it, with data above
the caller's clearance withheld. Agent flows are listed as flows. Real
runs by default; `kind=tests` lists tests of drafts instead, so a test
never shows among real runs. Read-only. Requires the right to view
workflows.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: `runs`, the default, for real runs, or `tests` for tests of drafts.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

get.description:
Returns one execution: its `status`, the data it started with and where
each step stands. Data above the caller's clearance is withheld.
Requires the right to view workflows.

Returns the data an approval step lets through, as `shown`, for the
caller to decide on. Approving counts only for exactly this data, so it
is sent back as it came. `422` when the step is not waiting for
approval. Requires the right to approve workflow steps and clearance
for the data.

409.description: The execution ran out of time

422.description: The step is not waiting for approval

post.description:
Approves an approval step for exactly the data the caller was shown,
sent back as `shown`. A step before a high-risk action needs two
different people, each with a fresh second-factor `mfa_code`; the first
approval is recorded and the step keeps waiting. Neither the person the
execution acts for nor an author of a high-risk step may approve.
Answers only the execution's `execution_id` and `status`. Records
`workflows.approval_granted`. Requires the right to approve workflow
steps and clearance for the data.

403.description: Forbidden, or a second factor is needed

409.description: The data is not what the step lets through, or the execution ran out of time

422.description: The step is not waiting for approval, or its window closed

post.description:
Refuses an approval step, which fails the execution, or a loop's
approval of every item, which fails the loop before any pass runs.
Answers only its
`execution_id` and `status`. Records the step's failure and the
execution's end. Requires the right to approve workflow steps and
clearance for the data the step shows.

409.description: The execution ran out of time

422.description: The step is not waiting for approval

get.summary: List the items a loop asks to approve
get.description:
Returns one page of the items a loop will act on, in the order its
passes take them, for a loop whose first step asks one approval for
every item. The items were fixed when the approval opened. Each page
served is kept as opened by the caller, and `shown` says how many of the
`total` items they have been shown so far. Requires the right to approve
workflow steps and clearance for the data.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

409.description: The execution ran out of time

422.description: The loop is not waiting for an approval of its items

post.summary: Approve every item of a loop
post.description:
Approves every item a loop will act on. The yes counts only once every
item was on a page the caller opened through the items endpoint; before
that it is refused. A loop before a high-risk action needs two different
people, each with a fresh second-factor `mfa_code`; the first approval
is recorded and the loop keeps waiting. The approval that completes it
starts the passes. Records `workflows.approval_granted` with how many
items were shown and when the last was. Deny it through the step's
`deny` endpoint. Requires the right to approve workflow steps and
clearance for the data.

403.description: Forbidden, or a second factor is needed

404.description: No such execution, or the loop asks nobody

409.description: Not every page was opened, the list changed, or the execution ran out of time

post.description:
Stops a running execution and the agent runs it started. Answers only
its `execution_id` and `status`. `409` when it ran out of time, which
leaves it timed out; `422` when it already ended. Records
`workflows.execution_ended`. Requires being the person it acts for, or
full control of workflows.

get.description:
Returns the passes the execution's loop steps started, newest first,
paginated. Each pass is an execution of the loop's own steps for one
item, and its `pass` names the loop step and the item. Data above the
caller's clearance is withheld. An execution without loops has none.
Requires the right to view workflows.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Starts a failed or timed-out execution again from its trigger, every
step running again, as a new execution acting for the caller. Answers
the new `execution_id` and `status`. Records its start. Only the person
the failed run acted for may, with the right to run workflows.

403.description: Forbidden, or not the person it acted for

409.description: It did not fail, or its version is no longer in service

post.summary: Retry a failed execution from its failed steps
post.description:
Starts a failed or timed-out execution again from the steps that did
not finish, keeping what the finished ones produced, as a new execution
acting for the caller. Answers the new `execution_id` and `status`.
Records its start. Only the person the failed run acted for may, with
the right to run workflows.

403.description: Forbidden, or not the person it acted for

409.description: It did not fail, or its version is no longer in service

get.summary: List the integrations a workflow may use
get.description:
Returns every integration installed in this deployment, each with the
`key` its operations and accounts name, its `title`, a `description` of
what it lets a workflow do, and the name of its `icon`, such as `github`
or `slack`. An icon name is lowercase letters, digits and dashes; the
dashboard draws the icon for it and a plain one for a name it does not
know. `connecting` says how an account is connected to it: `sign_in`
at its service through `.../accounts/connections`, where the deployment
registered an app with that service, or `credential` handed to
`.../accounts`; `sign_in_asks_for` names what signing in asks for
besides the account's name, such as `organization` for Azure DevOps. What each integration offers is listed by
`.../operations`, and the events that may start a workflow by
`.../events`. Read-only. Requires the right to view workflows.

get.summary: List the operations a workflow may use
get.description:
Returns every operation the installed integrations offer, each with its
`title` and a `description` of what it does, its inputs with what each
means, the `outputs` it gives back at their paths in the step's output
(such as `json.number` for the number of an issue GitHub opened),
whether it acts through an account, the most sensitive data it may be
handed, and the kind of action it takes as the tenant counts it: a risk
the tenant raised shows here, never only what the integration declared.
An action step's `effect` and `ceiling` are checked against this when
its workflow is published; the titles and descriptions only explain.
Read-only. Requires the right to view workflows.

post.summary: Fill a picker in a step's form
post.description:
Lists the options a `picker` or `multi_picker` input offers now, such
as the repositories an account can reach or the labels of the chosen
one, read live through the integration's own read operation and the
account in `account_id`. Only the account's owner, or someone who may
manage accounts, fills a picker through it. The read never changes
anything at the service: an operation that is not declared as a read is
refused before any call. When the service gives no list,
`unavailable` says what it said and the builder types the value
instead. Requires the right to update workflows.

404.description: No such picker, or the account is not the caller's to use

get.description:
Returns every operation the tenant raised, oldest first: its
`integration`, `operation` and the `effect` it counts as. Requires the
right to view workflows.

post.description:
Makes the tenant treat one `operation` of an `integration` as `effect`:
`undeclared` or a high-risk action class. From then on a workflow
calling it needs an approval step right before it. `409` when it is
raised already; change that one instead. `422` when the effect raises
nothing. Records `workflows.operation_risk_raised`. Requires the right
to change workflows.

422.description: Validation error, or the effect raises nothing

delete.description:
Lets the operation count as its integration declares again. Records
`workflows.operation_risk_override_removed`. Requires full control of
workflows.

patch.description:
Sets what a raised operation counts as: `undeclared` or a high-risk
action class. `422` when the effect raises nothing. Records
`workflows.operation_risk_raised`. Requires the right to change
workflows.

422.description: Validation error, or the effect raises nothing

post.description:
Gives the person's `words` to the tenant's model provider and answers
the steps it proposes: a whole new workflow, or with `after` the steps
that follow one step of a draft. Every step is checked against what the
integrations offer now; one that fits nothing is left out with a note.
Nothing is saved or recorded: the builder places what it keeps and saves
it as a draft. Requires the right to update workflows.

502.description: The model gave no answer to use

post.description:
Starts the version in service of the workflow whose webhook secret
`trigger_id` names, acting for its publisher, with the request's JSON
body as its data and `exposure` (default `internal`) as the most
sensitive class in it. The secret travels in the `Ianua-Trigger-Secret`
header; it is checked against the digest kept for it, and is never
logged or answered. Answers `202` with `status` `started` and the
`execution_id`, or `refused` with the `reason` the publisher may not
have it start now (also recorded), or `chain_too_long`.

`401` for every call that is not admitted, alike: an unknown webhook, a
wrong or missing secret, no version in service, or one someone other
than the secret's issuer published. Needs no session.

parameters.name: exposure
parameters.description:
The most sensitive data the call carries, such as `confidential`;
`internal` when left out.

parameters.name: ianua-trigger-secret
parameters.description: The secret issued for the webhook

requestBody.description: The data the execution starts with: any JSON value

202.description: Started, or refused for the publisher

401.description: No such webhook, a wrong or missing secret, or nothing in service

422.description: The data or the class is not valid

get.description:
Returns the workflow's latest version, draft or not. Requires the right
to view workflows.

post.description:
Drafts the version after the workflow's latest one, starting as a copy
of it. `409` when the latest version is still a draft. Records
`workflows.version_drafted`. Requires the right to create workflows.

409.description: The latest version is still a draft

patch.description:
Makes one change to the workflow's latest version, which must be a
draft, named by `edit`: `rename` (with `name`), `replace_steps` (with
`graph`), `change_trigger` (with `trigger`), `change_run_limit` (with
`run_limit_seconds`), `describe` (with `description`),
`change_failure_alert` (with `failure_alert`) or `arrange` (with
`layout`). Answers the draft as saved, with its new `revision`; moving
steps with `arrange` keeps the revision and records nothing. `409` when
the latest version is not a draft. Records `workflows.draft_renamed`,
`workflows.draft_steps_replaced`, `workflows.draft_trigger_changed`,
`workflows.draft_run_limit_changed`, `workflows.draft_described` or
`workflows.draft_failure_alert_changed`. Requires the right to update
workflows.

409.description: The latest version is not a draft

get.description:
Returns the cases its versions are evaluated against and whether
publishing waits on an evaluation. A case whose input is above the
caller's clearance shows only its `name` and `exposure`. Requires the
right to view workflows.

404.description: No sample cases were saved for the workflow

put.description:
Replaces the cases its versions are evaluated against: each an input,
how sensitive it is, and up to ten checks of the results. A check reads
a path the way a step reads its input, such as `summarise.answer`, and
expects the value there to equal a value, contain a text, or match a
short pattern. `publish_gate` `must_pass` holds publishing back until
