the draft's last evaluation passed every case; it is `off` unless set.
Records `workflows.evaluation_set_saved`. Requires the right to change
workflows.

422.description: Validation error: more than 50 cases, two of one name, too much data, a check that is not valid, or `must_pass` with no case

get.description:
Returns its latest 20 evaluations, newest first; the first is the one
a publishing gate reads. What is above the caller's clearance is
withheld. Requires the right to view workflows.

post.description:
Tries the workflow's latest version, its draft before it is published,
against every saved case. Each case runs as a test run, so nothing
outside changes, at most five at a time. It answers at once with
`status` `running`; read the evaluation for each case's `outcome`:
`passed`, `failed` with what differed, or `not_run` with why. It ends
within an hour, `passed` only when every case passed. Records
`workflows.evaluation_started` and, at the end,
`workflows.evaluation_ended`. Requires the rights to change and run
workflows.

202.description: Started; a worker runs its cases

403.description: Forbidden, or the plan's evaluations running at once are reached

404.description: No such workflow, or no sample cases were saved for it

422.description: The workflow has no sample case

get.description:
Returns what each case came to so far. A failed case whose run held
data above the caller's clearance shows that it failed and its run, but
not what differed. Ended evaluations are kept for 30 days. Requires the
right to view workflows.

404.description: No such evaluation of the workflow, or it was cleared

get.description:
Returns the executions of every version of the workflow, newest first,
paginated. Each shows where it and its steps stand; data above the
caller's clearance is withheld, and a withheld step shows only its
`phase` and `exposure`. Real runs by default; `kind=tests` lists its
tests instead. Requires the right to view workflows.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: `runs`, the default, for real runs, or `tests` for tests of drafts.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Starts the published version of a workflow that starts by hand, acting
for the caller, with `input` as its data and `exposure` the most
sensitive class in it, such as `internal`. Answers the new execution's
`execution_id` and `status`; read it through the execution endpoint.
`404` when no version is published. Records
`workflows.execution_started`. Requires the right to run workflows.

404.description: No version of the workflow is published

422.description: Validation error, or the workflow does not start by hand

post.description:
Publishes the draft as the version in service, archiving the one it
replaces. `revision` is the draft's revision as the publisher reviewed
it; `409` when the draft changed since. Every action step is checked
against what the integration catalog offers now, as the tenant's raised
risks treat it, and a high-risk action needs an approval step right
before it. Records `workflows.version_published`, and
`workflows.version_archived` for the version replaced. Requires the
right to update workflows, and to see the event it starts on.

409.description: The draft changed since it was reviewed, or another version was published

422.description: No draft, or an action no longer offered or fitting, or a high-risk action without an approval before it

get.summary: Read what each step may read
get.description:
Returns, for each step of the workflow's latest version, what it may
read: the trigger's data first, then each step that can come before it,
with every value at the full path a step's input names, such as
`trigger.issue.title`. A value marked `whole` is everything at its path,
whose shape only a run shows. Requires the right to view workflows.

post.description:
Runs the workflow's latest version, its draft or the one in service, on
`input` as example data, acting for the caller. Nothing outside changes:
every step that writes, sends, deletes or is undeclared, every agent
run, approval and wait, and code that may reach the network answers at
once with a stand-in whose output says `stood_in` and what it
`would_use`. Reads, conditions, transforms and code with no network run
for real. A test is listed apart from real runs (`kind=tests`), may not
be started again, and tells nobody when it fails. Records
`workflows.execution_started` with mode `test`. Requires the rights to
update and to run workflows.

422.description: Validation error, or a step reads one that cannot come before it

post.description:
Makes the secret the workflow's webhook is called with, for a workflow
whose trigger is its webhook. Answers the `trigger_id` the webhook's
address names (`POST .../workflows/triggers/{trigger_id}`) and the
`secret`, shown this once, which the caller sends in the
`Ianua-Trigger-Secret` header; only its digest is kept. A webhook that
already has a secret is rotated or revoked instead (`409`). Records
`workflows.trigger_secret_issued`. Requires the right to edit
workflows.

409.description: Its webhook already has a secret

422.description: The workflow does not start on its webhook

delete.description:
Deletes the webhook's secret, so no call starts the workflow until a
new one is issued. Records `workflows.trigger_secret_revoked`. Requires
the right to edit workflows.

404.description: No such workflow, or its webhook has no secret

post.description:
Replaces the webhook's secret; the old one stops working at once.
Answers the new `trigger_id` and `secret`, shown this once. Records
`workflows.trigger_secret_rotated`. Requires the right to edit
workflows.

404.description: No such workflow, or its webhook has no secret

get.description:
Returns one version of the workflow by its number. Requires the right
to view workflows.

post.description:
Archives one version for good: a published one stops starting. `422`
when it is already archived. Records `workflows.version_archived`.
Requires the right to delete workflows.

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket and streams the calling user's notifications in
the tenant as they are sent: one JSON frame per notification, the same
items as the tenant inbox. Only notifications whose category the user
may see when the stream opens are sent, and any other update is held
back; after a new role the dashboard connects again to see more. The
stream asks again from time to time what the user may still see: a
category whose right they lost stops, and the stream closes (`1008`)
once no category is left or on the first refusal. An organization
member reads their notifications in the organization, so is `403` here.
Requires a tenant user's own session or key.

101.description: WebSocket upgrade: live tenant user notification stream

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket and streams what happens in one run, real or a
test, as it happens: it starting, each step starting, succeeding,
failing, standing in, being skipped or approved, and how it ended. On
connect the server sends a `{ "type": "connected", "subject" }` frame,
then one `run_moment` frame per moment. A frame names steps, never
data: the run is read again for what the caller may see. The stream
asks again from time to time whether the caller may still read the run
and closes (`1008`) when not. Requires the right to view workflows.

101.description: WebSocket upgrade: live moments of one workflow run

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket and streams each change someone makes to the
workflow's draft: renamed, steps replaced, trigger, run limit,
description or failure alert changed. On connect the server sends a
`{ "type": "connected", "subject" }` frame, then one `draft_changed`
frame per change, naming its `event_type`, so the builder reads the
draft again instead of working on a stale copy. Moving steps on the
canvas records nothing and sends nothing. The stream closes (`1008`)
once the caller may no longer read the workflow. Requires the right to
view workflows.

101.description: WebSocket upgrade: live changes to one workflow's draft

get.description:
What the organization uses now, counted fresh, next to the limits it
works under: its plan's, or those negotiated for it. Users and tenants
are counted across the organization; every other count is the most any
one tenant holds, as those limits apply per tenant. Read-only. The app
decides whether the caller may read the bill.

The organization's team members, optionally filtered by `status`
(`Invited` / `PendingVerification` / `Active` / `Locked` /
`Deactivated`, or the invitation-derived `PendingInvitation` /
`InvitationExpired`) and/or `email` substring, sortable and paginated.
Each entry carries the email, display name, lifecycle `status`, role and
timestamps. Read-only. The app decides whether the caller may view
members.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Filter by account status, or by the state of an open invitation
(`PendingInvitation` / `InvitationExpired`). Omit to return everyone.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on email address.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-separated sort fields, applied left to right. Prefix a field with `-` for descending order (default ascending). Allowed: created_at, updated_at, email, display_name, status.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The `next_cursor` of the page before; absent for the first page. A
cursor only works with the sort it was given out for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most items to return, from 1 to 100 (default 20).

post.description:
Opens an account in `Invited` status and emails the invitee a single-use
link, with the optional personal `message`. The invitee follows the link
and accepts at `.../users/accept-invitation`, choosing their own
password. The link carries the organization slug and the token, so it
works on a cold open, and expires after the invitation lifetime. Use
`.../users/{user_id}/resend-invitation` for a lost or expired one; an
address with an invitation already waiting is `409`. On a deployment
with no mail server nothing is mailed: the answer carries the
`accept_link` for you to pass on to the invitee.

An address whose account in the organization was closed gets that same
account back, opened again, with none of its old tenant access, second
factor or passkeys. Only an owner invites an owner. Records
`organization.org_user_invited`, after `organization.org_user_reopened`
for a reopened account.

post.summary: Accept an org invitation and set a password
post.description:
Public endpoint, no session required. The invitee follows the link in
the invitation email and submits its `token` together with a chosen
`password`. The token proves the recipient controls the invited address,
so this sets the password and activates the account in one step, and
mails the member that joining worked.

**State transitions.** Invitation: `Pending -> Accepted` (terminal).
Member: `Invited -> Active`, with `joined_at` recorded. The password is
checked against the organization's rules before any state changes.

Returns `404` if the token is unknown or already accepted or revoked,
`410` if it is past its expiry, and `422` if the password is too weak.
Records `organization.org_user_invitation_accepted` and
`organization.org_welcome_email_sent`.

410.description: Invitation expired; ask an admin to resend it

post.description:
Creates a team member with a password the owner chose, bypassing the
invite flow, for accounts the owner provisions. The member is active at
once, but their address counts as unverified until they follow the
confirmation link mailed there: nobody adding an account vouches for a
mailbox they do not hold. The `password` is checked against the
organization's password rules.

Returns `409` if the address belongs to another account, or `422` for an
invalid email, display name or weak password. Only an owner makes an
owner. Records `organization.org_user_created` and, once the mail is
accepted, `organization.org_verification_email_sent`.

Public endpoint, no session required. The invitee follows the link in
the invitation email and turns the invitation down with its `token`;
the account that waited on it is closed. Returns `404` if the token is
unknown or the invitation is no longer pending. Records
`organization.org_user_invitation_declined`.

404.description: Unknown token, or a closed invitation

post.summary: Cancel my erasure from the mailed link
post.description:
The member whose erasure was asked for changes their mind: submit the
`token` from the link mailed to them, and the erasure stops and the
account opens again. Public: the member cannot sign in while the
erasure waits. Records `organization.org_user_erasure_cancelled`.

403.description: The member left the address the link went to

422.description: Malformed token, or a request past cancelling

post.description:
Stops an erasure before it is carried out and opens the account again.
The member themselves cancels from the link mailed to them; this is for
someone who may remove the member. Records
`organization.org_user_erasure_cancelled`.

422.description: The request can no longer be cancelled

post.description:
Puts a pending erasure under legal hold: it waits, past its grace
period, until the hold is lifted, and the member may still cancel it
meanwhile. Records `organization.org_user_erasure_held`.

post.summary: Release a member's erasure from hold
post.description:
Lifts a legal hold, so the erasure goes ahead as it was asked for.
Records `organization.org_user_erasure_released`.

post.summary: Renew an invitation from its link
post.description:
For an invitee holding a link that ran out: submit its `token` and a
new link goes to the invited address, never one the caller names.
Only a link that ran out is renewed, and only while the invitation
stands as it was sent. The answer says how long before another may be
asked for. Records `organization.org_user_invitation_resent`. Public
within the organization: the invitee has no account yet.

200.description: A new link went to the invited address

403.description: The member left the invited address, or no mail server is set up and the inviter must send it again

409.description: The link still works, or the member no longer waits to join

422.description: Malformed token, or the invitation was answered or revoked

post.summary: Check an invitation link without accepting it
post.description:
Submit the `token` and get back `Valid`, `Expired`, `AlreadyUsed`, or
`Invalid`. `AlreadyUsed` covers an invitation that was accepted,
declined, or revoked: all terminal, and none of them something a
replacement link would fix. A `Valid` link also returns the
organization's `password_policy`, the rules accepting will enforce.
Nothing is spent. Public within the organization, matching the accept
endpoint: the reader has no account yet.

post.summary: Resend a member's email verification link
post.description:
Public endpoint, no session required, because an unverified account is
refused at sign-in and so could never call an authenticated one. Send
the address; a fresh link is emailed and the previous one stops working.

Always returns `204`, whether or not the address belongs to an account,
whether it is already verified, and whether the last link is still
within its resend wait: the response must not reveal which. Records
`organization.org_verification_email_sent` when a mail goes out.

Public endpoint: the recipient submits the `token` from their
verification email. The token is single-use: presenting it proves
control of the address, which marks it verified and lets the account
sign in, and the member is mailed that it worked. Returns `404` if the
token is unknown or already used, and `410` if it ran out of time.
Records `organization.org_user_email_verified` and
`organization.org_welcome_email_sent`.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a team member: every session of theirs ends and
every delegation they granted, in any tenant of the organization, is
revoked before the record goes. Irreversible. Nobody removes themselves,
and the organization always keeps an active owner. Records
`organization.org_user_deleted`.

409.description: Would leave the organization without an owner

get.description:
The org role plus every tenant the member can reach and the permissions
they hold in each. An `Owner` lists every tenant in the organization
with the full permission set; a `Member` lists only granted tenants.
Any member reads their own; another member's needs the right to view
members.

post.summary: Give or withdraw a member's consent
post.description:
Records a decision on one set of terms (`consent_type` and `version`).
Only the member gives their own consent, from their own session.
Withdrawing is as easy as giving: the member does it, or someone who
may record it for them does, since withdrawing only lowers what is done
with their data. Records `organization.org_user_consent_granted` or
`organization.org_user_consent_revoked`.

403.description: Forbidden, or consent given for someone else

404.description: No such member, or no consent was given before

get.description:
Every consent decision the member made, given and withdrawn. A member
reads their own; reading another member's is the app's to allow.
Read-only.

patch.description:
An owner moves another member to a new `email`. The address changes at
once and counts as unverified until the member confirms it through the
link mailed there; links mailed to the old address stop working. A
member moving their own address goes through the email change flow,
which proves them first. Records `organization.org_user_email_changed`
and `organization.org_verification_email_sent`.

post.description:
Asks for the member's data to be erased once the grace period passes.
The member asks from their own session, or someone who may remove them
asks for them. The account closes at once, its sessions and what it
granted end, and a link to cancel goes to its address: the member
cannot sign in meanwhile, so the link is how they change their mind.
Records `organization.org_user_erasure_requested`.

409.description: An erasure is already under way, or the member is the last active owner

502.description: The mail service refused the cancel link; the request stands

post.description:
For a member who lost both their authenticator and their recovery codes.
Turns their second factor off, ends every session and remembered device
they have, and emails them, so they sign in with their password and set
up a new one. You cannot reset your own: turn it off from your account
settings, with a code. Returns `404` if the member does not exist or has
no second factor. Records `organization.org_member_mfa_reset`.

Sends the invitation again with a fresh link and expiry; the previous
link stops working at once. Use this when an invitation was lost or
expired, instead of inviting the same address again. The invitation
stays `Pending` and the member `Invited`. Returns `404` if the member
has no pending invitation. Records
`organization.org_user_invitation_resent`.

On a deployment with no mail server nothing is mailed: the answer is
`200` with the new single-use `accept_link`, for you to pass on to the
invitee. Whoever holds it joins as the invited member.

200.description: No mail server is set up: the new accept link to pass on

post.description:
An owner sets a new password for another team member: the one sent, or
one drawn to the organization's rules when omitted, returned for the
owner to relay. Every session the member has ends. Use the password
change endpoint for your own account. Returns `404` if the user does not
exist. Records `organization.org_user_password_reset`.

Withdraws an outstanding invitation so its link can no longer be used,
and closes the account that waited on it. Use this to undo an invite
sent to the wrong person. An owner or the platform may withdraw one.

**State transitions.** Invitation: `Pending -> Revoked` (terminal).
Returns `404` if the member has no pending invitation. Records
`organization.org_user_invitation_revoked`.

patch.description:
Moves a member to another org role. `Owner` governs the organization and
inherits every permission in every tenant under it; `Admin` runs it day
to day with every tenant, but does not close it or change what it pays;
`Member` carries no org-level authority on its own, tenant access coming
from per-tenant roles; `Billing` runs the subscription and `Viewer`
reads the organization, and neither reaches any tenant. Only an owner
makes or unmakes one; handing ownership on in one step is
`…/users/{user_id}/transfer-ownership`.

The change takes effect immediately: the member's sessions end, so
their next sign-in carries the new role. Returns `404` if the user is
not a member of this organization, and `409` if the change would leave
the organization with no owner. Records
`organization.org_user_role_changed`.

409.description: Would leave the organization without an owner

patch.description:
Moves a team member between `Active`, `Locked` and `Deactivated`. Only
the transitions the lifecycle allows are accepted. A member locked or
deactivated is signed out everywhere at once, and every delegation they
granted is revoked with them.

Returns `404` if the user does not exist, `409` if it would shut out the
last active owner, and `422` for an unknown status or an illegal
transition. Records `organization.org_user_status_changed`.

409.description: Would shut out the last active owner

put.summary: Set a member's roles in one tenant
put.description:
Replaces the tenant roles an org `Member` holds in `{tenant_slug}` with
exactly the ones named, so narrowing `["Editor","Viewer"]` to
`["Viewer"]` removes Editor. An empty list withdraws access to the
tenant entirely. Roles are named the way they appear in that tenant.
Owners are refused with `422`: their access is implicit in the org role.

Returns `404` if the user or tenant is not in this organization, `422`
for an unknown role name. Records
`organization.org_user_tenant_access_granted`, or
`organization.org_user_tenant_access_revoked` for an empty list.

post.description:
The calling owner makes the member `{user_id}` an owner in their place,
in one step, and steps down to `Admin`: the organization is never left
without an owner along the way. The heir must be an active member who
is not an owner yet. Both members' sessions end, so their next sign-in
carries the new roles. Records `organization.org_user_role_changed` for
each and `organization.ownership_transferred`. Requires the owner's own
session.

409.description: The member is not active, or already an owner

post.description:
Mails a member of the organization a notice that an account was made for
them, with a link to sign in and no secret: an account let in at once is
one its holder has never heard of. A member who is gone is no error,
since the account was made a moment ago: nothing is mailed. Records
`organization.org_welcome_email_sent` once the mail is accepted.

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket and streams the calling member's notifications
in their organization as they are sent: one JSON frame per notification.
Requires a member's own session or organization API key that still
counts.

101.description: WebSocket upgrade: live organization notification stream

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket and streams live progress of the provisioning
run for the tenant named by `{reference_id}`: stage changes, completion
and errors. On connect the server sends a `{ "type": "connected",
"subject" }` frame, then one JSON frame per update. Requires a member
who may view the organization's tenants; `404` for a tenant of another
organization.

101.description: WebSocket upgrade: live progress of one tenant's provisioning

404.description: No such tenant in the organization

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket and streams the progress of every tenant
provisioning run the member can see, so one connection drives a whole
list of tenants; each frame names its `reference_id`. On connect the
server sends a `{ "type": "connected", "subject" }` frame. The tenants
followed are the ones the member sees when they connect (every tenant
of the organization, or those granted to them), up to 100; a tenant
added later appears on reconnect. Requires a member's own session or
organization API key.

101.description: WebSocket upgrade: live progress of every provisioning run the caller can see

post.description:
Begins a passwordless sign-in for an organization user on the flat
management login plane: the same plane as `POST /api/v1/login`, no
organization in the URL.

**Anti-enumeration.** An unknown email, or a known user with no
registered passkeys, returns a decoy challenge of the same shape and
records nothing, so the response cannot be used to probe which accounts
exist. Records `organization.org_passkey_sign_in_started` otherwise.
Public.

Completes a passwordless management-plane sign-in. The response is the
same shape as the password login at `POST /api/v1/login`; the
authenticator already proved possession and user verification, so no
MFA step-up follows, and a passkey that falls short of the assurance the
organization requires is refused (`403`). The ceremony is spent before the answer is
checked, so a failed answer burns it. Records
`organization.org_login_succeeded`, or `organization.org_login_failed`
once the member is known and the sign-in is refused. Public.

Begins a usernameless sign-in on the flat management login plane: no
email, no organization. The browser offers a saved passkey from the
empty email field, and the credential the user picks names its own
account and organization. Complete at the org login-confirm endpoint.
Records `organization.org_passkey_challenge_issued` on the platform,
since nobody is known yet. Public.

Public endpoint: submit the `token` from the reset email and the new
`password`. The token identifies the account by itself, so no
organization is needed. A member with a second factor also sends
`mfa_code` from it (`403 step_up_required` without one). Every existing
session is signed out.

Returns `404` if the token is unknown, expired, or already used, and
`422` when the password breaks the organization's rules. Records
`organization.org_user_password_changed`.

post.summary: Ask for a password reset link
post.description:
Public endpoint taking only an email address: no organization slug,
because a locked-out user has no way to know one. The organization is
resolved from the address and carried in the emailed link so the
browser lands in the right place. A new link supersedes earlier ones.

Always returns `204`, whether or not the address belongs to an account,
so this cannot be used to discover who has one. Records
`organization.org_user_password_reset_requested` for a known address.

204.description: No content: sent whether or not the address is known

post.description:
Submit the `token` from an expired reset link to mail a replacement that supersedes it.

Keyed on the token, not an address, so it reveals nothing about who has
an account: only someone who was sent a link can ask for its
replacement, and the replacement goes where the first one did. An
expired or already-spent token is exactly what this expects; it only has
to name its user.

The response carries `retry_after_seconds`, the cooldown before another
is accepted, measured from the member's newest link. Asking again inside
it returns `429` with the seconds still to wait in the message.

Public, because the reader of a reset email is by definition signed out.

post.summary: Check a reset link without following it
post.description:
Submit the `token` and get back `Valid`, `Expired`, `AlreadyUsed`, or
`Invalid`, so the page a link lands on can show the right thing before
the reader types a password. Nothing here spends the token.

`AlreadyUsed` means the password was changed on this link: offering the
form again would be wrong. `Expired` means it was not, and another link
can be requested.

A `Valid` link also returns the organization's `password_policy`: the
rules the reset will enforce. The route names no organization; the link
itself says whose rules apply. Other statuses carry no policy.

Public, because the reader of a reset email is by definition signed out.

get.description:
Every plan on sale, in the order the pricing page shows them (Free,
Starter, Business, Custom), with its price in `currency` cents and the
limits it enforces. A negotiated plan has no `price`. Public: anyone
may read what is for sale.

post.description:
While a flood of failed sign-ins puts sign-in under pressure, a sign-in
from a device nobody trusted answers `401 challenge_required` with
`challenge` set to `proof_of_work`. Ask here for a puzzle, find a
decimal counter whose SHA-256 of `challenge:counter` starts with
`difficulty_bits` zero bits, and send `challenge.counter` as the
sign-in's `challenge_proof` before `expires_at`. A puzzle is bound to
the address that asked for it and lets one sign-in through. Public: the
answer is the same whether sign-in is under pressure or not.

404.description: This deployment's challenge is Turnstile, which sets no puzzle

get.description:
Public. `open` is `false` on a self-hosted installation, which refuses
every signup, so a sign-in page can leave out its "Sign up" button.

post.summary: Sign up: ask for an organization
post.description:
Public. Mails `admin_email` a link; `POST /api/v1/signup/confirm` creates the
organization, first tenant and owner. Names become `org_slug`/`tenant_slug`;
the owner receives `admin_display_name` and hashed `admin_password`.

Always answers `202` with `status: "check_inbox"`, whether or not the
address has an account, in the same time either way. An address with an
account is mailed a notice to sign in instead. Returns `403` on a
self-hosted installation; `409` if the derived organization slug is taken
(organization names are public, as every sign-in address shows them);
`422` for an invalid email or display name, a weak password, or an
unslugifiable name. Rate-limited per address (`429`), and at most one
mail a minute goes to an address. Records nothing: nothing exists yet.

202.description: A link, or a notice, went to the address

403.description: This installation does not accept signups

post.summary: Sign up: confirm and create the organization
post.description:
Public. Takes the `token` from the link a sign-up mailed, once, within
the day it works. Creates the organization, its first tenant and the
owner, whose address the link proved, so they can sign in at once. The
tenant starts in `Provisioning` and moves to `Active` once its setup,
started by the `tenant.provisioned` event, completes.

Returns the `org_slug`, `tenant_slug`, `admin_user_id`, and
`status: "provisioning"`. Returns `404` for a link that is not valid or
was used, `410` once it has run out, and `409` if the company name or
the address was taken since the sign-up. Rate-limited per address
(`429`). Records `organization.created`, `tenant.provisioned`,
`organization.tenant_created` and `organization.org_user_created`.

404.description: The link is not valid, or was used already

409.description: The company name or the address was taken meanwhile

get.description:
Returns every IANA timezone identifier the platform accepts, such as
`Europe/Berlin` or `America/New_York`: the exact set a user's `timezone`
preference is checked against. Useful for a timezone picker. Static,
public data, needing no sign-in.

post.description:
Public endpoint for a fresh self-hosted installation. The person who
ran the install submits the one-time setup `token` it printed; that
confirms the first owner's address without a mail server, so they can
sign in the first time. Returns the owner's `id`. Records
`organization.org_user_email_verified`.

200.description: The first owner's address is confirmed

post.description:
Public endpoint taking only an email address. An unverified account
cannot sign in, so the person asking has no way to know their
organization's slug. Sending again supersedes the previous link rather
than leaving both live. Always returns `204`, also while the last link
is within its resend wait. Records
`organization.org_verification_email_sent` when a mail goes out.

204.description: No content; sent whether or not the address is known

post.description:
Public endpoint: submit the `token` from the verification email. The
token identifies the account, so no organization is needed. Confirming
activates an account that was waiting on it, which is what lets it sign
in, and the member is mailed that it worked.

Returns `404` if the token is unknown or already used, and `410` with
`error: "link_expired"` if it ran out of time: the holder can ask
for a replacement at `/api/v1/users/verify-email/resend`. Records
`organization.org_user_email_verified` and
`organization.org_welcome_email_sent`.

Public endpoint for the page shown when a verification link has expired.
Submit the same `token` from the dead link and another email goes out,
superseding it. Keyed on the token, not an address, so it reveals
nothing about who is registered. An already-confirmed address is `404`.

The response carries `retry_after_seconds`, the cooldown before another
request is accepted; asking again inside it returns `429`. Records
`organization.org_verification_email_sent`.

post.summary: Check a verification link without following it
post.description:
Public endpoint for the page a verification link lands on. Submit the
`token` and get back `Valid`, `Expired`, or `Verified`, so the page can
show the right thing before it acts. Nothing here spends the token or
changes the account. `Expired` covers a link that ran out of time and
one a newer link superseded. An unknown token is `404`.

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket for the live platform security dashboard, which
streams what happens across the deployment. On connect the server sends
a `{ "type": "connected", "subject" }` frame, then one JSON frame per
update. Every operator sees it. Requires an operator's own key that
still counts.

101.description: WebSocket upgrade: live platform security dashboard

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket and streams the calling operator's notifications
as they are sent: one JSON frame per notification, the same items as the
platform inbox. The connection stays open until the client closes it.
Requires an operator's own key that still counts.

101.description: WebSocket upgrade: live operator notification stream

get.description:
The logo at the top of the platform's own mail. Mail clients strip
embedded images, so they fetch it by address. Public and cached for a
week: it changes only with a new build.

200.description: The platform's mail logo, kept for a week

get.description:
Answers `200` with `ok` while the server is up. Public, and asks nothing
of anyone: no dependency is asked, so calling it costs the platform
nothing and says nothing of the deployment. The orchestrator's probes
are on the internal listener.

The groups the directory keeps, with their members, as SCIM `Group`
resources, a page at a time (`startIndex`, `count`), optionally filtered
on `displayName` with `eq`, `co` or `sw`, joined by `and` and `or`.
Groups are listed in one order, so a `sortBy` is refused. Groups a
person keeps in the dashboard are not listed. Records nothing. Requires
the tenant's SCIM token while SCIM is switched on.

200.description: A SCIM ListResponse of Group resources

400.description: A filter this service does not read (`invalidFilter`), or a `sortBy` (`invalidValue`)

401.description: No token, or not the tenant's current one

post.description:
Makes a group the directory keeps, under `displayName`, with the users
in `members`. Checked against the plan's group limit. Records the group
and each membership in the tenant's trail. Requires the tenant's SCIM
token while SCIM is switched on.

400.description: A value that is not valid, or a member who is not a user of the tenant (`invalidValue`)

401.description: No token, or not the tenant's current one

403.description: The plan's group limit is reached

get.description:
One group the directory keeps, with its members. Its `meta.version` is
sent as the `ETag`; a directory sending it back in `If-None-Match` is
answered `304` while the group, its name and its members, is unchanged.
A group a person keeps in the dashboard is not found. Records nothing.
Requires the tenant's SCIM token while SCIM is switched on.

200.description: A SCIM Group resource, its version as the `ETag`

304.description: The `If-None-Match` names the group's version: unchanged

401.description: No token, or not the tenant's current one

put.description:
Gives a group the directory keeps the name and the members it sends,
and only those members. Records each change in the tenant's trail.
Requires the tenant's SCIM token while SCIM is switched on.

200.description: The SCIM Group resource after the change

400.description: A value that is not valid, or a member who is not a user of the tenant (`invalidValue`)

401.description: No token, or not the tenant's current one

delete.description:
Deletes a group the directory keeps. Its members lose what the group
gave them. Records the deletion in the tenant's trail. Requires the
tenant's SCIM token while SCIM is switched on.

401.description: No token, or not the tenant's current one

patch.description:
Applies a SCIM patch: renaming the group, and adding, removing or
replacing its members, including Entra ID's `members[value eq "id"]`
form of removal. Records each change in the tenant's trail. Requires the
tenant's SCIM token while SCIM is switched on.

200.description: The SCIM Group resource after the change

400.description: A value that is not valid, or a member who is not a user of the tenant (`invalidValue`)

401.description: No token, or not the tenant's current one

get.description:
RFC 7644 section 3.11 lets a service answer `/Me` with the resource of
whoever signed in. The SCIM token names the tenant's directory, not a
person, so every method on `/Me` is answered `501 Not Implemented` in
SCIM's error format, as the RFC says for a service without it. Records
nothing.

501.description: `/Me` is not offered, for any method

get.description:
The resource types this service provisions: `User`, with the enterprise
extension, and `Group`. Public. Records nothing.

200.description: A SCIM ListResponse of ResourceType resources

get.description:
The attributes this service reads and returns for users, their
enterprise extension, and groups.
Public. Records nothing.

200.description: A SCIM ListResponse of Schema resources

get.description:
What this service supports: patch, filtering, sorting and ETags; no
bulk or password changes; and the tenant's bearer token as the one
authentication scheme. The extension
`urn:ianua:params:scim:schemas:extension:limits:2.0:ServiceProviderConfig`
gives `maxMembersPerOperation`, the most members one group write names
across all its operations; a write naming more is answered `400` with
`scimType` `tooMany`. Public. Records nothing.

The tenant's users as SCIM `User` resources, a page at a time
(`startIndex`, `count`). A `filter` compares `userName` (or `emails`),
`displayName`, `externalId`, `name.givenName`, `name.familyName`, and
the enterprise `department` and `employeeNumber` with `eq`, `co` or
`sw`, joined by `and` and `or` and grouped in parentheses; `externalId`
and `employeeNumber` compare with case, the rest without. `sortBy` names
one of those attributes, `sortOrder` is `ascending` (the default) or
`descending`, and users with no value come last.

A comparison on an attribute this service does not keep matches nobody,
so a provider looking a user up that way goes on to create it. Records
nothing. Requires the tenant's SCIM token while SCIM is switched on.

200.description: A SCIM ListResponse of User resources

400.description: A filter this service does not read (`invalidFilter`), or a `sortBy` or `sortOrder` it does not know (`invalidValue`)

401.description: No token, or not the tenant's current one

post.description:
Opens an account for the person the directory sends: `userName` (an
email address, or the primary one in `emails`), a display name, the
name's parts, `externalId`, the enterprise extension's `department`,
`manager` (a user of the tenant, by id) and `employeeNumber`, and
whether the account is `active`. The account starts with the tenant's
default roles and the role SCIM's settings name. The address always
stays unverified and is mailed a confirmation link. Checked against the
plan's user limit. Records the account's opening in the tenant's trail.
Requires the tenant's SCIM token while SCIM is switched on.

201.description: The SCIM User resource created, its version as the `ETag`

400.description: A value that is not valid (`invalidValue`)

401.description: No token, or not the tenant's current one

403.description: The plan's user limit is reached

get.description:
One of the tenant's users as a SCIM `User` resource. Its `meta.version`
is sent as the `ETag`; a directory sending it back in `If-None-Match` is
answered `304` while the user is unchanged. Records nothing. Requires
the tenant's SCIM token while SCIM is switched on.

200.description: A SCIM User resource, its version as the `ETag`

304.description: The `If-None-Match` names the user's version: unchanged

401.description: No token, or not the tenant's current one

put.description:
Replaces the user's record with the one the directory sends: address,
display name, the name's parts, `externalId`, the enterprise fields and
whether the account is active. A profile field left out is cleared.
Records each change in the tenant's trail. Requires the tenant's SCIM
token while SCIM is switched on.

200.description: The SCIM User resource after the change, its version as the `ETag`

400.description: A value that is not valid (`invalidValue`)

401.description: No token, or not the tenant's current one

delete.description:
Removes the person the directory no longer keeps: their account is
deactivated and kept, or deleted, as the tenant's SCIM settings say.
Their sessions and the authority they lent their agents end. Records
the removal in the tenant's trail. Requires the tenant's SCIM token
while SCIM is switched on.

401.description: No token, or not the tenant's current one

patch.description:
Applies a SCIM patch: `active`, `userName`, `displayName`, `name` and
its parts, `emails`, `externalId` and the enterprise extension's
`department`, `manager` and `employeeNumber`, in the `path` form or the
pathless one, by short or fully qualified path. `remove` clears a
profile field. Attributes this service does not keep are ignored.
Switching an account off ends its sessions and the authority it lent its
agents. Records each change in the tenant's trail. Requires the tenant's
SCIM token while SCIM is switched on.

200.description: The SCIM User resource after the change, its version as the `ETag`

400.description: A value that is not valid (`invalidValue`)

401.description: No token, or not the tenant's current one

AcceptHandoverBody.description: The domain a tenant takes over, and the tenant giving it.

source_tenant_id.description: The tenant that offered the domain.

AcceptInvitationBody.description: Accepts an invitation from its emailed link.

password.description:
The password the invitee chooses. Required when the tenant signs
users in with a password; ignored, and never stored, when it does
not.

token.description: The single-use token from the invitation email.

AcceptOrgInvitationBody.description:
Accepting an invitation: the token from its link and the password the
invitee chooses.

password.description: The password the invitee chooses for their account.

token.description: The token from the invitation email.

oneOf.description: The subject may.
The subject may not.

reason.description:
`unknown_resource_type`, `undeclared_action`, `not_held` or
`too_deep`.

AccessDecisionResponse.description: The answer to one access check.

AccessQuestionBody.description:
One question: may the subject do `action` on `resource_type`, or on the
object of it keyed `object_key`.

object_key.description:
The object's key in the app. Left out, the question is about any
object of the type: whether the subject holds the permission itself.

resource_type.description: The declared resource type, such as `document`.

AccessRequestPolicyResponse.description: The tenant's limit on how long one may ask for access.

longest_seconds.description: The longest a request may ask for, in seconds.

AccessRequestResponse.description: An access request and where it stands.

answer_by.description: When it runs out if nobody answers.

answered_at.description: When it was answered, absent until then.

oneOf.description: The account that approved or denied it, absent until answered.

asked.description: The role or group asked for.

length_seconds.description: How long it is needed, in seconds from the approval.

reason.description: Why it is needed.

AccessReviewResponse.description: The scope, reviewers and progress of an access recertification.

holder_count.description: The number of holders captured when the review started.

pending_count.description: The number of holders without an explicit decision.

remove_count.description: The number explicitly marked for removal, excluding unanswered holders.

scope.description: The role or group it covers.

unanswered.description: What happens to an undecided holder at the due date.

AccessTokenForm.description:
An access token sent in a form body rather than the header (RFC 6750
2.2).

access_token.description: The bearer credential presented to authorize this request.

AccountAttributeBody.description: One of a person's attributes an app can be sent.

AccountResponse.description: One integration account of the tenant.

integration.description: The integration it is for, such as `google-sheets`.

operations.description: The operations it may be used for; `null` for every one.

sharing.description: Who may have workflows act through it.

ActedThroughResponse.description: Whom or what an actor acted through, with the ids its kind names.

as_user_id.description: The person acted as, for either impersonation.

kind.description:
`impersonation` (an operator acting as a user),
`support_impersonation` (a tenant admin acting as one of its people)
or `workflow_run` (a workflow run acting as the person it is for).

ActingAsResponse.description: What the admin acts through, and until when.

ends_at.description: When the window closes and requests through it stop counting.

header.description: The header that names it, beside the admin's own bearer.

impersonation_id.description: The impersonation to name on each request made as the person.

ActionBody.description: One verb a resource type accepts, and what holding it confers.

display_name.description: What an operator sees in place of the key.

implies.description: Other actions on the same resource this one confers.

key.description: The action key, as it appears right of the colon in `resource:action`.

ActionResponse.description: One declared action, as the API returns it.

display_name.description: What an operator sees in place of the key.

grants.description:
Everything holding this action confers, the action itself included,
with the ladder already walked, so a client cannot disagree with the
proxy about what a grant means.

implies.description: Other actions this one directly confers.

ActiveSessionResponse.description: An active session with where it signed in from.

country_code.description: The country inferred from the sign-in address, when known.

ip_address.description: The client network address observed when the session began, when known.

latitude.description: The estimated north-south location of the sign-in address, when known.

longitude.description: The estimated east-west location of the sign-in address, when known.

session_id.description: The handle used to identify and revoke this signed-in session.

ActivityCalendarResponse.description: A contribution calendar: how many audit events happened each day.

days.description: One entry per day, oldest first; quiet days included with count 0.

max_count.description: Event count of the busiest day, 0 when the window is empty.

ActivityDayResponse.description: One day of the contribution calendar.

by_category.description:
Per-category breakdown. Re-grade against one category's window
maximum to recolor the heatmap for it without a new request.

count.description: Total events on this day, across every category.

level.description:
Heatmap intensity from 0 (none) to 4 (busiest quarter), graded
against the whole series.

ActorClaim.description:
Who acts for a token's subject (`act`, RFC 8693 4.1): the current actor,
with those before it nested inside.

act.description: The actor before it, if any.

sub.description: The actor: a person's id, or a client's id.

AddClearanceRuleBody.description:
A clearance rule to add: holding `permission` clears for data up to
`up_to`.

connection.description:
Who runs the DNS: `SelfManaged` or `Delegated`. Defaults to
`SelfManaged`, the choice that takes nothing over.

domain.description: The domain to register, such as `acme.com`.

AddGroupMemberBody.description:
Who to add to a group.

The kind is required rather than assumed. A consumer or an agent in a
group holds its roles at the proxy exactly as a person does, so the
request has to say which of them it means, and a UUID alone does not.

until.description:
When the membership stops counting (RFC 3339). Left out, it lasts
until the member is taken out.

AddOrgProviderBody.description:
Request body adding the organization's identity provider. Holds an OIDC
client secret, so it has no `Debug`.

config.description:
How it is reached: `{"Saml": {...}}` or `{"Oidc": {...}}`, as a
tenant's connection is configured.

name.description: The name members see on the sign-in page.

AddRuleBody.description: Request body for adding a classification rule.

field_path.description: The dot-notation path of the field, such as `user.ssn`.

name.description: What the rule is called, such as `payments-vs-approvals`.

second_role_id.description: The other role, which nobody may hold beside the first.

AddStageBody.description: Request body for adding a stage.

kind.description:
What the stage does, with its configuration, such as
`{"RateLimit": {...}}`.

Carries no position. A new stage always goes on the end, and is moved
with `PUT .../stages/order`. This used to take one, and a client
choosing a number without knowing the ones already in use would put
its stage ahead of Identity, filtering traffic before anything had
worked out who sent it.

AgentActivityEntryResponse.description: One record of an agent's activity.

details.description:
What happened: named values, each a scalar, an entity reference
(`{ kind, id, label }`), or a change (`{ change: { from, to } }`).

event_type.description: The stable name identifying which action was recorded.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the event occurred in.

oneOf.description:
The attestation policy accepted for secret-zero bootstrap, if
configured.

offer_expires_at.description: When the standing offer lapses unanswered.

oneOf.description: The person the agent was offered to, while the offer stands.

re_attest_every.description:
Maximum interval between re-attestations in seconds, when a policy
is configured.

standing.description:
Whether it may act right now. An `Active` agent that owes a
re-attestation is `MustReattest` until it proves what it is again.

trusted_methods.description: Trusted attestation methods, when a policy is configured.

updated_at.description:
When the agent was last changed: its details, status, attestation
policy, or a recorded attestation.

AllowRegistryBody.description: Request body for allowing an image registry.

host.description:
The registry's host, with an optional port, such as
`registry.acme.example`.

password.description:
The password or token images are pulled with. It is sealed before
it is kept and never shown again.

username.description:
The user images are pulled as; left out, with `password`, for a
registry that serves its images to anyone.

oneOf.description: An app permission the subject holds, such as `document:read`.

permission.description: An app permission the subject holds, such as `document:read`.

oneOf.description:
A relation the subject holds on the object, or on an object above
it.

relation.description:
A relation the subject holds on the object, or on an object above
it.

object.description: The object the relation is held on.

AnotherOrganizationBody.description:

AttestationChallengeResponse.description: A challenge to sign before bootstrapping.

and `body`), the GCP identity token or the TPM quote, or for a token
method the workload token itself (a Kubernetes service account
token, a GitHub Actions OIDC token, an OIDC issuer's token). Every
payload carries the binding of the nonce and the enrolled public
key: SHA-256 of `ianua-attestation-binding-v1`, a zero byte, the
nonce, a zero byte and the key's DER, in lower-case hex. A workload
token carries it as its only audience (`aud`).

nonce.description:
The challenge nonce this bootstrap answers, from
`POST .../bootstrap/challenge`.

signature.description:
For SPIFFE, the base64url (unpadded) signature over
`ianua-attestation-proof-v1:` and the binding in hex, made with the

the other methods.

allowed_origins.description: The accounts, projects or workloads the agent may attest from.

reattest_interval_seconds.description: Maximum interval between re-attestations, in seconds.

workload_trusts.description: The workload tokens that prove the agent, for the token methods.

values_discarded.description: How many stored values went with the field.

required.description: Whether every user must hold a value.

sensitive.description: Whether it needs more than the right to view the directory.

sortable.description: Whether a directory may be ordered by it.

AuditChainVerificationResponse.description:

The sequence number of the last record verified; `null` when none

Only events whose type starts with this, such as

Only events in this tenant. A tenant's own export is always of its
own log, whatever this says.
