The name it binds as, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, such as
`jira`.

scope.description: What it may reach.

CreateServiceBody.description: Request body for creating a service.

oneOf.description: How this service's backends are probed. Omit for the platform default.

name.description: Service name, unique within the tenant.

oneOf.description:
How the gateway opens TLS to the upstream. Omit to check it against
the public roots with no client certificate.

upstream.description:
Where requests go, and how they are addressed: its backends,
retries, balancing, circuit breaker, assertion audience, and
`reach` (`"direct"`, or `{"connector": <id>}` to be dialled through
one of the tenant's connectors). It carries no TLS; that is `tls`.

CreateServiceResponse.description: The id of a newly created service.

CreateStreamRouteBody.description: Request body for opening a port.

access.description:
Who by name may pass: `"any_holder"` (whoever the policy lets
through), `{"people": <route policy>}` for people signed in through
the tunnel, or `{"consumers": [<id>, ...]}`. Omit for `any_holder`.

backends.description: Where accepted streams go. At least one.

listen_port.description: The port to listen on. Must be 1024 or above.

sni.description: Which handshakes to answer. Defaults to every one on the port.

timeouts.description: How long a stream may take to start, and stay silent.

CreateStreamRouteResponse.description: The id of a newly opened port.

CreateSubscriptionBody.description: Request body for creating a webhook subscription.

event_types.description:
Event types to subscribe to, such as `{"Tenant":"StatusChanged"}`.
Empty means every event the creator may see now.

url.description: The HTTPS URL on the public internet to deliver events to.

CreateSubscriptionResponse.description: Answer to creating a subscription, with its signing secret.

signing_secret.description:
The raw signing secret. It is shown this once; store it to verify
deliveries.

CreateTopicBody.description: Request body for creating a topic.

retention.description:
How long messages are kept: `{"Duration": seconds}`,
`{"MessageCount": n}` or `"Unlimited"`. Never zero.

schema.description: Optional JSON schema documenting the messages.

topic_name.description:
Machine-readable topic name (such as `"orders.created"`), which the
publish and stream endpoints address the topic by.

CreateWorkflowBody.description: Request body for drafting a new workflow.

description.description: What it does, in up to 500 characters.

failure_alert.description:
Who is told when one of its runs fails: `administrators`, the
default, or `also_authors`.

layout.description: Where its steps sit on the canvas.

name.description: Label people will use to find the new workflow.

run_limit_seconds.description: How long one execution may run, in seconds, at most 31 days.

CreatedOrgApiKeyResponse.description: A key just minted, with the raw key shown this once.

raw_key.description: The raw key: shown once, never again.

CreatedServiceAccountResponse.description: A service account just made, the only time its secret is shown.

secret.description: The secret it binds with. Store it now: it is not shown again.

CreatorKind.description: The kind of principal that made something.

CreatorResponse.description: Who made something: a kind and an id.

CredentialAttestationResponse.description: The verified attestation a credential is bound to.

subject.description:
The attested workload identity: a SPIFFE ID, instance id, or TPM
subject (e.g. `spiffe://northwind/ns/prod/sa/invoice-triage`).

oneOf.description:
An API key the platform makes. The answer carries it once as
`api_key`; only its prefix and a keyed digest are kept.
An X.509 client certificate, known by its fingerprint.
A JWT the consumer signs itself, with a known issuer and subject.

issuer.description: The expected `iss` claim. Never the tenant's own issuer.

jwks_uri.description: Where the consumer publishes the keys its tokens are signed with.

CredentialBody.description:
The credential a consumer signs in with, as a create or rotate body
names it.

CredentialResponse.description:
An agent identity credential: public metadata only, never a private
key.

oneOf.description:
The attestation this credential is bound to, for one issued by
bootstrap. `null` for an enrolled credential, which attests nothing.

expires_at.description: When it expires.

grace_ends_at.description:
When a rotated credential stops verifying: the countdown's end.
`null` for an active credential and for a revoked one, whose
retirement is immediate rather than graceful.

grace_period_seconds.description:
The grace window's full length in seconds, the countdown's
denominator. Set exactly when `grace_ends_at` is.

kid.description: The key id (JWT `kid`) the agent stamps on its assertions.

public_key.description: PEM-encoded public key used to verify the agent's assertions.

rotated_at.description: When rotation retired this credential. `null` unless it was rotated.

CycleBody.description: How often a plan is billed.

DataResponse.description: One stream route open to workflows.

id.description:
The stream route, which a Protected data step names in its `route`
input.

DeadJobResponse.description:
A job that used up its tries, as an operator reads it. Its payload is
left out: only its handler reads it, and it may name what only its
tenant should see.

job_type.description: What kind of work it was, such as `mail.deliver`.

reason.description: Why its last run failed, as its handler reported it.

tenant_id.description: The tenant it worked for, or `null` for the platform's own work.

DeadLetterResponse.description: A message set aside after its deliveries ran out.

delivered.description: How many times it was delivered before it was set aside.

id.description: The dead letter's id, which a replay names.

message_type.description: What kind of message it is, when it was published with a type.

DecideAccessReviewBody.description: A reviewer's decision on one holder.

holder_kind.description: Distinguishes a user, organization member, agent or consumer by UUID.

kind.description:
`gateway` for one of the gateway's own checks, `stage` for a stage
of the route's pipeline.

name.description:
The check's or the stage kind's name, such as `pipeline_off` or
`geo_fence`.

stage_id.description: The stage, `null` for a gateway check.

oneOf.description: An app asked through the access check.

object_key.description: The object asked about, absent for a question about any object.

oneOf.description: The tenant's policy decided a request at the gateway.

matched_rule.description: The rule that decided, absent when the default action did.

version.description: The number of the policy version that decided.

DecisionBasisResponse.description: What a recorded decision was about and what decided it.

asked_by.description: Who asked: the app's caller, or the gateway, as an audit label.

basis.description: What it was about and what decided it.

DeclareAttributeBody.description:
Declares a custom field on the tenant's users.

`kind` is the only choice that has to be made. Everything else follows
from it and may be left out: the control, the comparisons a filter may
use, and what counts as a valid value.

description.description: Help text shown beside the control.

display_name.description: What to call the field.

filterable.description: Whether a directory may be narrowed by this field.

key.description:
The internal name. Derived from `display_name` when omitted, and
fixed once declared: every stored value is filed under it.

listed.description: Whether the field is returned with each user in a listing.

max_length.description: Longest permitted text, for the free-form text kinds.

maximum.description: Highest permitted value, for the number kinds.

minimum.description: Lowest permitted value, for the number kinds.

options.description: The options to choose from, for the kinds that draw from a list.

required.description: Whether every user must hold a value.

sensitive.description:
Whether the field holds information needing more than the right to
view the directory, such as a salary or a health note. Filtering and
sorting are held back the same way as reading, because narrowing a
list and reading off the count discloses the value.

sortable.description: Whether a directory may be ordered by this field.

DeclareResourceTypeBody.description: A resource type to declare in the tenant's catalogue.

description.description: What the resource is, in the operator's words.

display_name.description: What an operator sees in place of the key.

key.description:
The key used left of the colon in `resource:action`. Unique per
tenant.

DeclareResourceTypeResponse.description: The id of a newly declared resource type.

DefaultActionBody.description: What happens to a request no rule matched.

default_action.description:
`Deny` refuses anything no rule allowed; `Allow` means only the rules
refuse anything.

DefaultSubjectsBody.description:
Whom a new stream starts hearing about, as the Shared Signals framework
names it.

DelegationLimitsDto.description:
The limits a delegation is held to: its lifetime and depth, and every
option that narrows it further.

apps.description:
The apps (service ids) the agent may call through the gateway. The
token names each one's audience; without any, the agent reaches no
app that requires sign-in.

oneOf.description: Optional request budget: caps how many times the token may be used.

requires_approval.description: Whether actions under this delegation pause for a person's approval.

resource_scope.description:
Optional resource scope: URL path prefixes the token is confined to
(e.g. `["/accounts/4821"]`).

sender_constrained.description:
Sender-constrain the token (DPoP): the proxy requires a proof of
possession of the agent's credential key on every request.

DelegationRefDto.description: A delegation and when it expires.

expires_at.description: When the delegation expires.

DelegationRequestResponse.description: Where a request for a delegation stands.

decided_at.description: When it was answered, once it was.

delegation_id.description: The delegation it became, once approved.

expires_at.description: When a request still pending lapses unanswered.

reason.description:
Why the agent asks, in its own words. The agent wrote it: show it as
text, never as markup.

ttl_seconds.description: The lifetime asked for, in seconds.

DelegationResponse.description: The authority granted to an agent, including its limits and chain position.

apps.description:
The apps (service ids) the agent may call through the gateway, if
any.

oneOf.description: The request budget, if any.

depth.description:
This delegation's own distance from the root of its chain (`0` for a
root delegation), not the ceiling `max_depth` still allows below it.

expires_at.description: When the delegation expires.

oneOf.description: The bound intent and drift policy, if any.

max_depth.description: Maximum sub-delegation depth this authority may travel.

name.description: The title people see, if one was set.

parent.description: The parent delegation, for a sub-delegation.

renewed_at.description: When it was last renewed, or `null` if it never was.

requires_approval.description: Whether actions under this delegation pause for a person's approval.

resource_scope.description: The URL path prefixes the token is confined to, if any.

task.description: The task the token is bound to, if any.

DeleteMemoryBody.description: Request body for deleting a memory: its name, typed to confirm.

replacement_role_id.description:
Role to move every current holder to before deletion. When omitted,
the delete is refused while anyone still holds the role.

attempt_number.description: Which try this is (0 is the first).

duration_ms.description: How long the request took, in milliseconds.

event_type.description: The event type that caused the delivery.

message_id.description:
The message sent: the same on every attempt to deliver it, and on a
resend, so a receiver handles it once. Sent as `webhook-id`.

response_status.description: The HTTP status code the receiver answered with, if it answered.

subscription_id.description: The subscription this delivery was for.

DescribeConsumerBody.description: Request body for changing or clearing a consumer's description.

description.description: The new description; `null` or left out clears it.

DestinationAddedResponse.description:
A destination just added. A webhook's signing secret is shown this
once.

signing_secret.description:
The secret a webhook's posts are signed with, or `null` for Slack
and Teams, whose address carries its own key. It is never shown
again.

DestinationBody.description:
A destination to add, or the whole of one to change. A Slack or Teams
address is itself the key that posts to the channel, so the body has
no `Debug`.

name.description: What the organization calls it, such as "On-call Slack".

DestinationChangedResponse.description:
A destination just changed. A webhook gets a new signing secret,
shown this once.

signing_secret.description:
The webhook's new signing secret, or `null` for Slack and Teams. It
is never shown again.

DestinationResponse.description:
An organization's destination as read back. Its address and secret are
never shown.

oneOf.description:
A Slack channel, through its incoming-webhook address on Slack's
own host.

A Microsoft Teams channel, through its webhook address on
Microsoft's own hosts.

A public HTTPS endpoint of the organization's own; its posts are
signed with a secret shown once.

DeviceAnswerBody.description: Request body for answering a device request.

allOf.description: How the client proves itself.

scope.description: The scopes asked for, separated by spaces.

DeviceCodeForm.description: A device asking for its codes (RFC 8628 3.1).

DeviceCodeResponse.description: The codes a device is handed (RFC 8628 3.2).

device_code.description: The device code the device polls the token endpoint with.

expires_in.description: How long the codes stay valid, in seconds.

interval.description: The shortest wait between polls, in seconds.

user_code.description: The short code the person types on the other screen.

verification_uri.description: Where the person goes to type it.

verification_uri_complete.description: The same page with the code already filled in, for a QR code.

name.description: The name it is listed under.

status.description: `trusted`, or `revoked` once trust was taken back.

devices.description: Every device they trusted, revoked ones included, oldest first.

DifferenceResponse.description: One thing that differed in a failed case.

check.description: Which of the case's checks, counted from zero, for `check`.

found.description:
What was found at the check's path, cut to 500 characters; left out
when nothing was.

kind.description:
`run_ended`: the test run did not succeed. `check`: a check did not
hold.

run_end.description:
How the run ended, for `run_ended`: `failed`, `cancelled` or
`timed_out`.

DirectMembershipResponse.description: A group the principal was put in straight.

until.description: When the membership stops counting, or `null` for good.

DirectRoleResponse.description: A role given to the principal straight.

role.description: Identifies the permission bundle assigned directly to the principal.

until.description: When it stops counting, or `null` for good.

DiscoverRealmBody.description: Request body for finding where an address signs in.

email.description: The address the person typed.

DnsRecordSetResponse.description: One record set in a delegated zone.

is_managed_by_ianua.description:
Whether this set is one we maintain rather than the tenant: the
address that routes the delegated hostname to the proxy, and the
`_acme-challenge` names a certificate is issued through. Both are
shown, but writing or removing them is refused.

name.description: The name this set answers for, fully qualified.

record_type.description: The record type, as a zone file spells it.

ttl_seconds.description: How long a resolver may cache the answer, in seconds.

values.description: Every answer, as a zone file spells the value.

allOf.description: The registration, as the list answers it.

oneOf.description:
The certificate it serves; `null` when it was never given one or
the tenant removed it.

DomainDetailResponse.description: A registered domain read on its own, with the certificate it serves.

caa_record.description: Suggested CAA record for a tenant who writes their own records.

connection.description:
Who holds the DNS: `SelfManaged` (the tenant adds records at their
own provider) or `Delegated` (they handed the hostname to us with an
`NS` record, and we write its records).

dns_record_name.description:
DNS record name to add for verification. Absent for a `Delegated`
domain, whose `NS` records prove it instead.

dns_record_value.description: DNS record value to add for verification. Absent when delegated.

is_auto_verified.description:
Whether the domain arrived verified, because the operator vouches
for it.

tls_status.description:
`NotRequired`, `Provisioning`, `Active`, `Expired` or
`NoCertificate` (the tenant removed the certificate it uploaded and
has not uploaded or asked for another).

traffic_records.description:
The records that actually bring traffic here. Verifying proves
ownership and routes nothing: until one of these is added, the
domain resolves wherever it always did.

verified_at.description: When DNS verification completed, if it has.

DraftAfterBody.description: The step of a draft proposed steps come after.

workflow_id.description: Draft whose graph supplies the insertion point for proposed steps.

DraftBody.description: Request body for asking the tenant's model to draft steps.

oneOf.description:
The step of a draft the steps come after; left out for a whole new
workflow.

provider_id.description: The tenant's model provider the words are given to.

words.description: What the person wants, in up to 500 characters.

DriftModeDto.description: How to react when an agent's actions drift from the bound intent.

DuePasswordChangeBody.description: The new password a sign-in owes, set with the change's token.

change_token.description:
The change's token: the `change_token` the sign-in answered with, or
the one in the mailed link.

code.description:
A code from the person's own second factor, when the sign-in's
`proof` was `own_factor`.

fingerprint_hash.description:
The secret this browser keeps for itself, if it was trusted before,
as the sign-in sent it.

new_password.description:
The new password. It must meet the tenant's rules and repeat none
of the account's recent ones.

EarlierDataResponse.description: The values one source hands on.

source.description: `trigger`, or the key of the step before.

EarlyDeletionBody.description: An early deletion, with the platform's note on the record.

note.description: What happened, or which order it was.

reason.description: `abuse` or `legal_order`.

EarlyDeletionReason.description: Why the platform deletes an archived tenant before its grace has run.

EdgeBody.description: A way from one step to the next.

port.description: The way out it leaves by: `next`, `when_true` or `when_false`.

oneOf.description: Gives it a new name.

name.description: Replacement label shown for the draft.

oneOf.description: Replaces its steps and edges.
Starts it on something else.
Lets each execution run for another time.
Describes what it does, or takes the description away with `null`.

description.description: The description, in up to 500 characters.

oneOf.description: Chooses who is told when one of its runs fails.

Moves its steps on the canvas. This keeps the draft's revision and
records nothing, since no run is changed by it.

EditDraftBody.description: One change to a workflow's draft, named by `edit`.

EffectiveCapabilitiesResponse.description: An agent's effective capabilities across its live delegations.

active_delegations.description: The delegations contributing to the effective set.

computed_at.description: When the effective set was computed.

effective.description: The union of what its live delegations grant.

host.description: An exact host name; wildcards are refused.

port.description: The destination socket number paired with the exact host name.

EgressPolicyConfigBody.description: Where a service may send traffic, as declared.

name.description: A name people recognise the service by.

service.description:
The service: its SPIFFE ID, or `sha256:<fingerprint>` of its client
certificate. The document keys the policy by it.

EgressPolicyResponse.description: The destinations and data classification ceiling permitted for an upstream service.

name.description: The label administrators use to distinguish this outbound access rule.

service.description: The upstream name whose outbound requests this rule governs.

EmailTemplateResponse.description:
A tenant's own version of one email. A part still on the platform's
default is `null`.

body_html.description: The HTML body, when the tenant set one.

body_text.description: The plain-text body, when the tenant set one.

is_custom.description: Whether any part is the tenant's own.

locale.description:
The recipients' locale it is written for, such as `de-DE`, or
`null` for every locale without a version of its own.

subject.description: The subject, when the tenant set one.

EmailTrustBody.description:
Whether a provider's word on an address is enough to sign in to the
account with that address.

EncryptionCertificateResponse.description: The certificate a provider encrypts its assertions to.

certificate.description:
The certificate, PEM, to give the provider. The private key stays
here, sealed.

EncryptionKeyBody.description:
Where the key comes from: an empty body `{}` has this platform make a
new pair; `certificate` and `private_key` together bring the tenant's
own. Holds a private key, so it has no `Debug`.

certificate.description: The certificate the provider encrypts to, PEM, when bringing a pair.

private_key.description:
Its private key, PEM, when bringing a pair. Sealed before it is
stored; never shown again.

allOf.description: The request's parameters, as the browser brought them.

confirmed.description:
Whether the person confirmed they want to sign out. Asked when the
app did not name them with an ID token.

EndSessionBody.description:
Request body for the dashboard's sign-out step: the app's request as
the browser brought it, and whether the person confirmed.

EndSessionResponse.description: The answer to the sign-out step.

front_channel_logout_uris.description:
The pages of the apps that load in the browser to hear of the
sign-out, each in a hidden frame.

redirect_to.description:
Where to send the person afterwards, with the app's `state`; none
means the dashboard's own signed-out page.

EndSessionStep.description: What the sign-out step comes to.

EnrollConnectorBody.description: Request body an agent enrolls with.

code.description: The one-time code the administrator was shown.

csr.description:
A PEM certificate signing request (PKCS #10) for the key the agent
holds its link with, carrying no extensions.

EnrolledKeyDto.description:
The public half of a key pair an agent made for itself. The private
half never leaves the agent: the platform neither generates nor returns
one.

algorithm.description: Signing algorithm of the key pair (`EdDSA`, `ES256`, `RS256`).

ErasureBody.description: Asks for a person's data to be erased.

reason.description: Why, if a reason is given.

id.description: The request's id, to cancel or hold it by.

ErrorBody.description: Structured JSON error body returned to API consumers.

oneOf.description:
The challenge to solve before signing in again, on
`challenge_required` when one can be set. Absent when none can: only
a trusted device or single sign-on gets in until the pressure eases.

details.description: Internal error details (only present in development mode).

key.description:
The message key of `message`, when it has one, such as
`routing-cannot-move-a-route-from-to`: a client may show the
message in its own words from the key and `params`.

message.description:
Human-readable message, in the first language of `Accept-Language`
the platform words it in, else in English.

params.description: The values `message` was filled with, by name.

ErrorCode.description: Fixed set of machine-readable error codes.

EvaluationResponse.description: One evaluation of a workflow version against its sample cases.

cases.description: What each case came to, in the set's order.

deadline.description: When every case still open could not run.

revision.description: The revision of that version it tries, as a publisher hands it back.

started_by.description: The person who started it, as `<kind>:<uuid>`.

status.description:
`running` while cases wait or run, then `passed` when every case
passed, or `failed`.

EvaluationSetResponse.description: A workflow's sample cases and its publishing gate.

cases.description: The sample cases, each with its input and checks, in the order saved.

edited_by.description: The person who last saved it, as `<kind>:<uuid>`.

workflow_id.description: The workflow whose versions the cases try.

EventResponse.description:
One event an installed integration's service sends that a workflow may
start on.

filters.description:
The filters a trigger may set, each narrowing which of these events
start the workflow; a required one must be set.

outputs.description:
The values it gives the workflow, each at a path in the trigger's
output that the steps may read.

title.description: Its name for people, such as `An issue is opened`.

EventTypeResponse.description: One event a webhook may be subscribed to.

event_type.description:
The event, as a subscription lists it, such as
`{"Identity":"UserRegistered"}`.

EvidencePageResponse.description: A page of an agent's evidence and the state of the chain it sits in.

chain.description:
The scheduled sweep's last verdict on the tenant's chain. Records
from a chain that does not verify prove nothing.

EvidenceRecordResponse.description: One audit record with its place in the tenant's chain.

seq.description: The record's position in the chain: what a verdict cites.

EvolveSchemaBody.description: Request body for adding a schema version.

EvolveSchemaResponse.description: Answer to adding a schema version.

ExchangeTokenBody.description: Request to exchange an agent's self-signed assertion for a task token.

assertion.description: The compact JWS the agent signed with its identity credential.

granted.description: The capabilities the agent asks for this task token.

sender_constrained.description:
Binds the token to the agent's active credential key: the proxy then
requires a DPoP proof signed with that key on every request, so the
token alone is useless to whoever copies it.

task.description: Optional task binding describing the intended work.

ExecutionDecidedResponse.description: Where an execution stands after a decision on it.

execution_id.description: The run whose approval was decided or whose start just completed.

acting_for.description: The person it acts for, as `<kind>:<uuid>`.

cause.description:

`event`. A pass of a loop carries the cause of the run it belongs
to.

deadline.description: When it is stopped if it has not ended.

exposure.description: The most sensitive data it was started with.

input.description:
The data it was started with; `null` when it is above the caller's
clearance.

mode.description:
`live` for a real run, or `test` for a test of a draft, whose steps
that would reach out answer with a stand-in saying what they would
have used.

oneOf.description: The loop it runs one pass of; left out for a run that is no pass.

status.description:
`running`, or how it ended: `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`,
`timed_out`, or, for a pass whose loop failed or ended first,
`loop_ended`.

steps.description: Each step and where it stands.

ExportBody.description: Asks for a copy of a person's data.

scope.description: `access` or `portability`.

ExportDownloadResponse.description: Where a ready export is downloaded.

url.description:
A short-lived address of the file. Only the person it is about may
ask for it.

id.description: The export's id. It is mailed to the person once it is ready.

ExportResponse.description: One request for a copy of a person's data.

asked_by.description:
Whether the person asked for it themselves (`holder`) or staff did
for them (`staff`).

id.description: The export's id, to download it by.

scope.description: `access` or `portability`.

status.description:
`requested` while it is gathered, `ready` to download, `expired`
once its week is over.

ExportScopeBody.description: What a copy of a person's data is to hold.

allOf.description: What a waiting sign-in still owes; nothing for a person signed in.

offered.description:
The kinds the tenant offers them: `totp`, `email_code`, `sms_code`.

FactorOptionsResponse.description:
The second factors a person may set up, the one they hold, and what
their sign-in still owes.

enrollments_turned_off.description: Second factors turned off, in force or still being set up.

passkeys_removed.description: The number of registered credentials the person can no longer sign in with.

percent.description: Failures as a percentage of the total; null when there were none.

trend.description: Movement of the failure count versus the previous window.

How many known vulnerabilities below critical a company's image was
found to have; none of them refuse it.

low.description: Findings rated low or not rated.

FinishConnectionBody.description: Request body for finishing a connection.

code.description: The one-time code the browser brought back from the callback.

FixBody.description: Code that failed when tried, and what its trial said.

code.description: The failed source submitted to the model for correction.

failure.description: What the trial said, such as the end of its error.

approval_classes.description: Action classes whose tool calls wait for a person's approval.

ask_past_micros.description:
What the run may spend before it pauses for a person to let it go
on, in the same millionths; below the cap when both are set. Left

The signed-in user's MFA status.

The same shape as the organization plane's, so one client reads both.

enabled.description: Whether MFA is enrolled and active.

source_key_id.description: The key it moves away from.

target_key_id.description: The key it moves to, once the migration started.

allOf.description: The public key the agent made for itself.

rotated. The deployment's default when left out.

MintCredentialBody.description:
Request to enrol an agent credential.

Enrolling takes no attestation binding. An attestation records a proof
the platform verified, and an enrolment carries no proof to verify; bind
a credential by bootstrapping the agent against its attestation instead.
The `kid` is server-generated: it is unique per tenant and is the lookup
key at token exchange, so a caller-chosen one would be a namespace an
outsider could probe and collide with.

ModelPricingDto.description:
What a model provider charges, in millionths of the tenant's billing
currency per million tokens.

input_micros_per_million.description: The price of a million tokens sent to the model.

output_micros_per_million.description: The price of a million tokens the model wrote.

ModelProviderResponse.description: A model provider; never its key.

embedding_model.description:
The embedding model it offers beside its chat model, or `null` for
none.

has_credential.description: Whether an API key is stored (never the key itself).

last_test_message.description:

last_tested_at.description:
When the most recent connectivity test ran, or `null` if never
tested.

name.description: The name people know it by.

oneOf.description: What the provider charges, or `null` when nobody set a price.

MoveGroupBody.description: Where in the tree a group moves.

parent_id.description:

moves it to the top of the tree.

refresh_token.description: Its refresh token, shown this once. The old one stops working.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the new session works in.

revocation_lists.description:

checked.

trusted_ca_certs.description: PEM-encoded CA certificates trusted to sign client certificates.

NackResponse.description: What became of a refused message.

fate.description:

NameIdFormatBody.description: How an app is told who a person is.

NeedsAccountResponse.description: The account a held version needs.

NewKeyResponse.description: The key a rotation or a migration's start made.

NewPolicyRuleBody.description:

allOf.description: What it does, named by `kind`.

join.description:
How it waits for several steps before it: `all` (the default) or
`any`.

key.description:
Its key: lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, never `trigger`.

event_type.description: The event that caused it, such as `{"Tenant":"StatusChanged"}`.

read.description: Whether the notification has been read.

resource_id.description: The resource the event refers to.

OAuthErrorBody.description: An OAuth error: the registered code and what was wrong.

error_description.description:

a token or a secret.

ObjectBody.description: One object of the tenant's app: its resource type and its key there.

resource_type.description: The declared resource type, such as `document`.

recipient.description:
The tenant user the agent is offered to. They become its owner once
they accept.

OfferEmbeddingsBody.description:
Request body for setting the embedding model a provider offers beside
its chat model.

embedding_model.description:
The embedding model, such as `text-embedding-3-small`; `null` to
offer none.

target_tenant_id.description: The tenant that may take the domain, in the same organization.

value.description: What the input is set to when it is picked.

name.description: Its name, as the person is shown it.

organization_id.description: The membership scope this sign-in choice would enter.

slug.description: Its slug, to send as `organization` when signing in again.

OidcDiscoveryDocument.description:
The tenant's protocol endpoints and capabilities, used by relying parties to configure
sign-in.

revocation_endpoint_auth_methods_support.description: Supported revocation endpoint client authentication methods.

scopes_supported.description: The permission and identity bundles advertised to relying parties.

token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported.description: Supported token endpoint client authentication methods.

token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_s.description: Supported algorithms for a client's signed assertion.

OnFindingBody.description: What a guardrail's finding does to the run.

OpenApiImportBody.description: A spec plus the things a spec cannot say.

expected_audience.description:
The audience the upstream pins. Required for any policy other than

upstream_url.description:
The upstream URL, when the spec names no server or names the wrong
one.

one of `topics` or `resource`.

sender_agent_id.description: The agent whose area the messages come from.

topics.description:
The topics in the sender's area the receiver may read, such as
`agents.<sender id>.tasks` or `agents.<sender id>.>`.

Request body for opening a stream route to workflows: the login of the
system behind it that Protected data steps sign in with.

login_user.description: The user name, such as a database user made for workflows.

tls.description:
Whether the connection to the system is held to TLS: `required`
unless `off` is chosen.

tls_authority.description:
The PEM of the authority the system's certificate chains to, when
not a public one.

tls_server_name.description:
The name the system's certificate is for, when not the host every
backend shares.

OpenableAppResponse.description: One app on the caller's start page.

hosts.description: The company's addresses the app answers on; empty for every one.

name.description: The app's name, as its route is named.

opens.description:
`now` when it opens at once, `step_up` when the person signs in more
strongly first, `key_proof` when their client proves its key first.

path.description: The path the app opens at, to put after one of its addresses.

route_id.description: The route the app is served through.

oneOf.description:
How the builder asks for it; left out when its integration does not
explain it, and the builder asks with a plain text box.

required.description: Whether the operation runs without it.

OperationOutputResponse.description: One value an operation gives back.

path.description: Where it is in the step's output, such as `json.number`.

OperationResponse.description: One operation an installed integration offers.

ceiling.description: The most sensitive data it may be handed, such as `internal`.

effect.description:
The kind of action it takes, as the tenant counts it: `undeclared`
or an action class. A tenant's raised risk shows here.

needs_account.description:
Whether it acts through one of the tenant's accounts for its
integration.

outputs.description:
The values it gives back, each at a path in the step's output that
the steps after it may read.

oneOf.description:
How its inputs are previewed, shaped like the product it acts in;
left out when it has no preview.

title.description: Its name for people, such as `Open an issue`.

email.description: The address the operator signs in with.

OperatorSignInBody.description:
An operator signing in with their password for a short-lived key.
Holds the password, so it has no `Debug`.

email.description: The address the operator signs in with.

password.description: The credential checked before issuing a short-lived operator key.

OrgApiKeyResponse.description: An organization API key, without the key itself.

expires_at.description: When it expires, or `null` for never.

scopes.description: What the key may do, as `org:<domain>:<action>` scopes.

How the people who administer an organization sign in.

Sent and received whole. A half-applied config is an organization in a
state nobody chose, and the rules only hold across the whole thing.

challenge_threshold.description:
How many failed password sign-ins naming the organization, in the
deployment's window, put its sign-in under pressure: from then on a
device no member remembered must pass a challenge before its
password is checked. From 10 to 1,000,000; 200 when omitted.

idle_timeout_secs.description:
How long an org session may sit idle before expiring, in seconds.
Cannot outlast the session it belongs to.

CIDR ranges allowed to reach org sign-in. Empty means anywhere. With
any range set, a request whose address cannot be resolved is refused.

lockout_duration_secs.description: How long the network stays locked out of the account, in seconds.

max_login_attempts.description:
Failed attempts from one network before that network is locked out
of the account. Sign-ins from anywhere else go on.

password_policy.description:
How strong an administrator's password has to be. Applies from the
next password change or reset.

session_lifetime_secs.description: How long an org session stays valid from creation, in seconds.

step_up.description: When an org sign-in has to clear a higher bar than a password.

The organization's branding. A part it never set is `null`: the
platform's applies.

primary_color.description: The color of buttons and links.

sender_name.description: The name the organization's mail goes out under.

the browser that began it holds it.

not set up, so they set one up before the session is let in.

A member signed in sends `proof`, their password typed again with a code
from any factor they hold. A sign-in waiting for the factor the
organization requires sends no body, or one without `proof`: the
sign-in itself is its leave, for a few minutes after it began.

oneOf.description: The member's password typed again, when they are signed in.

assurance_trust.description: Whether its report of a multi-factor sign-in is believed.

name.description: The name members see on the sign-in page.

The proof that this browser passed the challenge an earlier answer
asked for (`challenge_required`), while sign-in is under pressure.
Leave it out otherwise.

email.description: The email address to authenticate.

The secret of a device the member remembered, if the client holds
one: 64 hex digits the browser made for itself.

Matching a device the member already remembered is what lets the
organization's step-up policy skip a second factor. Absent,
unrecognised and forgotten all mean the same thing: challenge them.

The slug of the organization to sign in to, picked from those an
earlier answer of `choose_organization` offered. Leave it out at
first: every organization holding the address is tried.

The tenant to sign in to. Without it the session lands in the first
active tenant the member reaches.

What this member reaches: their org role, the tenants they can
enter, and their permissions in each.

`null` while `mfa_required` is `true`: a session that proved only
a password has not finished authenticating, and must not read
the organization's tenant layout. Call `…/me/access` once it has.

Whether the member has no second factor and must set one up

`session_id` to confirm). Always `false` when `mfa_required` is
`false`.

The tenant's URL slug, `null` when the session works in no
tenant.

organization. Nothing was opened: sign in again with the same
address and password, naming one of these in `organization`.

active tenant the member reaches.

recovery_codes.description: Recovery codes: shown once, never again.

The member's password typed again, when they are signed in. A

The codes: shown once, never again. Every earlier code stopped

The member's password typed again, with a code from their second
factor.

Seconds before another may be requested. Count this down rather than

code.description: The `code` parameter.

oneOf.description: A SAML provider's posted form.

own signature is checked against.

Names the server-held ceremony. Send it back on confirm: it is the
only handle the client gets; the state it names stays here.

verification, so usually nothing.

How many times the password appeared in known breaches, for
`breached` only.

status.description:
`not_checked` when the tenant does not look new passwords up,
`unchecked` when the lookup could not be made, `clean`, or
`breached`, which a tenant that only warns lets through: tell the
person to choose another.

PasswordChangeBody.description: A signed-in person's new password, and their current one as proof.

mfa_code.description: A code from the person's authenticator, needed when they have one.

new_password.description: The new password, held to the tenant's rules.

PasswordChangeRequiredResponse.description:
A sign-in whose right password an admin set, or which expired. No
session opened; set a new password with the change's token to finish
it.

change_token.description:
The single-use token the new password is set with, for this sign-in
only; absent when it was mailed. Keep it in memory; never store or
log it.

expires_at.description: When the token stops working.

password_change_required.description: Always `true`: tells this answer from a session.

proof.description:
What the change asks besides the new password: `none`; `own_factor`,
a code from the person's own second factor sent as `code`; or
`mailed_link`, when the token went to the person's mailbox instead
of coming back here.

reason.description: Why: `set_by_admin` or `expired`.

PasswordLinkStatusResponse.description:
What a link that sets a password is worth, and the rules the new
password must meet.

password_policy.description:
The policy the new password must meet. Present only when `status`
is `Valid`.

PasswordResetConfirmBody.description: The reset link's token and the new password.

mfa_code.description:
A code from the account's authenticator, required when the account has
an active second factor.

Whoever holds the reset token also writes this body, so only a code
proves the factor: a mailbox alone must not get past it.

new_password.description: The new password, held to the tenant's rules.

token.description: The single-use token from the reset email.

PasswordResetRequestBody.description: The address a forgotten password is reset for.

email.description: The address the reset link goes to, if it has an account.

PasswordSetResponse.description: A password set, and what the breach lookup said about it.

password_breach.description: What the breach lookup said about the new password.

oneOf.description: Forward the path exactly as it arrived.

Forward only what the pattern's trailing `/*` caught: every segment
before it is dropped, `{name}` ones too, and a pattern without `/*`
forwards `/`. Keep a captured segment with a template instead.
Build the forwarded path from the parameters the pattern captured.

PathRewriteBody.description:
Wire form of the rule turning the requested path into the forwarded one.

Tagged by `mode` rather than mirroring the domain enum's shape: a field
that is sometimes a string and sometimes an object is awkward to type on
the client, and the template needs validating on the way in either way.

value.description: The value to send back in role create and update requests.

label.description: Its scope spelling, `org:<domain>:<action>`, to send verbatim.

permissions.description: The actions in this domain that may be named in an organization key's scopes.

labels; left out when it depends on none.

filled_by.description: The read operation listing its options.

stages.description:

omitted: a pipeline that skips them is not a pipeline this gateway
will run.

name.description: What a route names it by, unique within the tenant.

stages.description:
Every stage, enabled or not, in the order they run.

Ordered here so a caller can render the pipeline as it arrives and
hand the same list back to `PUT .../stages/order`. Disabled stages
keep their place: they are skipped, not removed.

PipelineSummaryResponse.description: One pipeline in a listing, with what it would cost to delete.

name.description: What a route names it by.

route_count.description: How many routes name it. Non-zero means deleting it is refused.

plans.description: The plans: Free, Starter, Business, Custom.

monthly_cents.description: Cost per month when billed monthly, in cents.

badge.description: A short label above the card, for the one being pushed.

call_to_action.description: What the card's button does: `sign_up` or `contact_sales`.

display_name.description: The name on the pricing card.

footnote.description: A caption under the card's button.

heading.description: A headline in place of a price, for a plan that has none.

highlighted.description: Whether this card is the emphasised one.

oneOf.description: What it costs, or `null` when the price is negotiated.

requirements_description.description: What a negotiated plan can cover.

PlanUsageResponse.description: What the organization uses next to what its plan allows.

limits.description: What it may use: its plan's limits, or those negotiated for it.

based_on.description:
Where the version started: `blank`, `copy` of another version, or
`restore` of a past one.

based_on_version.description: The version it copied or restored, absent for a blank start.

default_action.description: What happens to a request no rule matched.

editable.description:
Whether the rules can be edited right now, so a client does not have
to re-derive the lifecycle to know whether to disable its form.

rules.description: The rules, already in the order they will be checked.

PolicyRuleResponse.description: One rule in the tenant's policy, as it is read back.

action.description: What happens when the rule fires.

conditions.description:
Every condition must hold for the rule to fire. An empty list matches
every request.

enabled.description:
A disabled rule is kept but skipped, so a rule can be taken out of
service without losing how it was written.

name.description:
What the rule is called, shown in simulation results and the audit
log.

PolicyTransitionBody.description: Which way to move a version of the policy through its lifecycle.

ack.description:

stream then drops.

maxEvents.description: The most events to hand back, from 1 to 100; 100 when left out.

returnImmediately.description: Accepted for RFC 8936; a poll always answers at once.

PollResponse.description: The events a poll hands back, as RFC 8936 lays them out.

moreAvailable.description: Whether more events wait beyond these.

sets.description:
Each event not yet acknowledged, by its `jti`: the signed security
event token.

input.description: The operation field whose value fills this preview part.

PreviewResponse.description: How a step's inputs are previewed, shaped like the product it acts in.

parts.description: Which input fills each part of the preview.

works beside the new one.

credential_hint.description: Safe hint for telling the old credential apart.

until.description: When the overlap ends and the old credential is refused.

groups.description: Every group it is in, straight or through a group above.

memberships.description: The groups it was put in straight, each with its end.

through_groups.description:

external_id.description: What another directory calls the account.

family_name.description: The surname recorded separately from the personal name.

given_name.description: The personal name recorded separately from the surname.

phone_number.description: Their phone number, in international form. Not proved to reach them.

notes.description: What the person should know, such as a step no operation fits.

steps.description: Suggested nodes the person can accept into their draft.

purpose.description: What the task is for, in words.

resource_scope.description: The URL path prefixes the agent is confined to.

from.description: The step it leaves; left out for the step the proposal goes after.

path.description: The path read, when it reads earlier data.

text.description: The value written out, when it is one.

oneOf.description: Calls an operation.

integration.description: Installed provider offering the proposed action.

operation.description: Callable action key within the selected provider.

goal.description: Task instructions proposed for the agent the builder selects.

equals.description: What it should equal; left out to check it is there.

oneOf.description: Waits for a person to approve.

oneOf.description: Waits a while.

key.description: Identifier used by the proposal's edges to connect this node.

A call to its webhook.
Starts runs at the times described by a cron expression.
An event a service sends.

integration.description: Installed provider whose event would start the workflow.

method, and the keys or certificate subject it needs.

tls_client_auth_subject_dn.description: The subject its certificate carries, for `tls_client_auth`.

token_endpoint_auth_method.description:
`client_secret_basic` (the default), `client_secret_post`,
`private_key_jwt`, `tls_client_auth` or `none` for a public client.

A tenant to provision.

A tenant starts with no primary domain: it proves a domain once it
exists, then makes that one primary. Unknown fields are refused, so a
body still naming `primary_domain` learns that instead of having it
dropped.

display_name.description: The tenant's name in admin screens.

Where this tenant's data should live.

Omit it and the tenant lands on the platform's shared database in
the deployment's default region.

scope.description: The scopes it may ask for, separated by spaces.

tls_client_certificate_bound_access_toke.description:
Whether its access tokens are bound to its TLS certificate (RFC

RegistrationBody.description:
What an app registers itself with (RFC 7591 2), in the standard's
names. A field left out takes the standard's default.

RegistryResponse.description: An image registry the tenant allowed.

How images are pulled from it: `anonymous`, or `password` with a
login kept sealed.

A new PEM certificate signing request for the key the agent
enrolled with.

Every rule of the draft by name, first checked first. Each rule is
named exactly once.

Every stage id, in the order they should run.

The whole order, not one stage's new index: a drag-and-drop sends the

request. The list must name every stage exactly once: a partial list

tenant's limit, and never more than 30 days.

delegation_id.description: The delegation supplying the authority the call uses.

The person asked: a tenant user or an organization member, who would
grant the delegation.

granted.description: The capabilities the agent asks for.

Request body for an agent asking a person for a delegation, signed in as
itself.

Asks to move the signed-in person's own account to a new address.

Asking needs more than an open session: the person proves who they are
again, with their password or a sign-in link mailed to them just now,
and a code from their second factor when they have one.

How the gateway closed the connection this request upgraded, when

or the credential ran out. Absent for any other connection.

without a recorded decision, which the gateway refuses too.

status.description: The status returned to the client.

subject.description: Who the gateway decided was asking.

provider.description: Which cloud, for a tenant in the customer's own account.

region.description:

RunAgentBody.description: Request body for running an agent toward a goal.

approval_classes.description:
Further action classes whose tool calls wait for a person's approval
before running. High-risk classes (`delete`, `configure`,
`financial`, `admin`) always wait; this list can only add to them.

ask_past_micros.description:
What the run may spend before it pauses for a person to let it go
on, in the same millionths; below `spend_limit_micros` when both are
set. Whoever may resume the run lets it spend on, once. A call whose
cost cannot be told makes it pause too. Left out for no pause.

delegation_id.description:
The delegation the run acts under. Tool calls go through the
zero-trust proxy bearing a task token minted from it, and the
proxy's policy pipeline authorizes every call. Left out, the
delegation the caller granted the agent is used; with none at all,
the run may not call tools.

max_steps.description:
Maximum loop iterations. Left out or zero takes the deployment's
default; more than its maximum gets the maximum.

provider_id.description: The model provider to reason with.

purpose.description:
The action classes the run may exercise (`read`, `write`, `delete`,
`configure`, `communicate`, `financial`, `admin`).

spend_limit_micros.description:
The most the run may spend on its model, in millionths of the
tenant's billing currency. Once spent, or once a model call's cost
cannot be told, the run stops as `over_budget`. Left out for no
limit.

tool_names.description:
Tools granted to this run by name. A run reaches only the tools
named here; an empty list grants none.

RunDecidedResponse.description:
Where a run stands once a person decided the call it held. Read the run
for its steps.

run_id.description: Identifies the task whose pending call received the decision.

answer.description: The final answer, once the run completed.

The action classes the starter listed as needing approval;
high-risk classes need it too, listed or not.

delegation_id.description:
The delegation the run acts under, or `null` for a run that calls no
tool.

exposure.description:
The most sensitive data class the run has read (`public`,
`internal`, `confidential`, `restricted`). The run may call only
tools cleared for it, and its answer may carry it.

goal.description: The task the agent was asked to accomplish.

max_steps.description: The most steps the run may take.

pending_arguments.description:
The arguments that tool was called with, verbatim.

An approver has to see what they approve, and echo it back when
deciding, so the decision cannot land on a call that changed
meanwhile.

pending_at_step.description: The step the held call was made at, echoed back with the decision.

pending_tool.description: The tool awaiting a person's approval, if the run is paused.

purpose.description: The purpose: the action classes the run may exercise.

oneOf.description:
Where the run waits for a person before spending more, or `null`
when it never does.

spend_limit_micros.description: The most the run may spend, or `null` for no limit.

spent_micros.description:
What its model calls cost so far, in millionths of the tenant's
billing currency. Calls to a provider with no price are not counted.

usage.description: The tokens its model calls used so far.

arguments.description:
The arguments the tool was called with, if this step was a tool
call.

detail.description:
The tool result, refusal reason, final answer, the person's reply,
or what the check found.

outcome.description:
The outcome kind (`allowed`, `denied`, `answered`, `replied`, a
person's answer to a held call in place of running it, or
`check_failed`, an answer the run's check turned back).

tool.description: The tool named, if this step was a tool call.

RunSummaryResponse.description: A run summary; its steps and final answer are available on the detail endpoint.

approval_classes.description:
The action classes the starter listed as needing approval;
high-risk classes need it too, listed or not.

delegation_id.description:
The delegation the run acts under, or `null` for a run that calls no

Runs its own steps once for each item of a list, each pass a run of
its own. A step inside finds its item at `trigger.item`, its
position from zero at `trigger.index`, and the mapped `inputs` at
`trigger.<field>`. It gives back the list of what each pass gave
back: the output of each of its last steps, under their keys.

oneOf.description:
Runs one sandbox version's code in a sandbox with no network,
handing it the mapped `inputs` as one JSON object. What the code
gives back is the step's output. The version must be built, and its
sandbox not archived, when the workflow is published.

inputs.description: What of the step's input the code is given.

oneOf.description:
Checks a text from an earlier step before the run goes on. It hands
on `checked` (the value it checked, with its findings taken out when
it removes them), `findings` (each one's `kind`, `check`, `field`,
`start` and `length`, never the text it matched) and `found` (how
many in all). Rules that cannot be read, or nothing where `text`
points, stop the run whatever `on_finding` says. Publishing refuses
a `text` that starts at a condition, approval or wait, which hand
nothing on.
